pulls.title: Snowflake: Support SECRET statements
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made fixes #ISSUE_NUMBER Snowflake SECRET statements were not parsing in the Snowflake dialect. This PR adds support for them: - CREATE [OR REPLACE] SECRET [IF NOT EXISTS], for all types: OAUTH2, CLOUD_PROVIDER_TOKEN, PASSWORD, GENERIC_STRING, SYMMETRIC_KEY - ALTER SECRET [IF EXISTS] ... SET ... - DROP SECRET, DESCRIBE SECRET, SHOW SECRETS - SECRET / SECRETS in GRANT and REVOKE (including ALL and FUTURE) Syntax is taken from the Snowflake docs: - https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-secret - https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/alter-secret ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? I added a few new unreserved keywords (SECRET, USERNAME, ALGORITHM and the option names). I checked that they still work as column names, and all the existing Snowflake parse fixtures regenerate with no change. AI disclosure: I used an AI assistant to help write the grammar changes and test fixtures. I reviewed the code, checked the syntax against the Snowflake docs, and ran the Snowflake dialect tests (774 passed) and pre-commit locally. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects/snowflake` (create_secret, alter_secret, secret_misc). --- ## Summary by cubic Adds support for Snowflake SECRET statements, which previously failed to parse in the Snowflake dialect. **Scope** - Supports `CREATE [OR REPLACE] [IF NOT EXISTS] SECRET` for all five types (`OAUTH2`, `CLOUD_PROVIDER_TOKEN`, `PASSWORD`, `GENERIC_STRING`, `SYMMETRIC_KEY`), plus `ALTER`, `DROP`, `DESCRIBE`, and `SHOW SECRETS`. - Extends `GRANT` and `REVOKE` to reference `SECRET` and `SECRETS`, including `ALL` and `FUTURE` forms. - Adds the new keywords as unreserved, so they still work as column names; existing parse fixtures are unchanged. Written for commit 13949c99e5889a63f8c423845b5c7a31e7378853. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Fix Rust escaping of StringLexer templates
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8722. `StringLexer` templates are currently inserted verbatim into ordinary Rust string literals. A backslash or double quote can break compilation, while input such as a literal `\n` can compile with different contents. Escape backslashes, double quotes and ASCII controls using Rust string escapes. This preserves CRLF and Unicode content and avoids raw-string delimiter collisions. Add 11 parametrized generator-output regression cases. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? Generated lexer output for all 28 existing dialects is byte-identical before and after this change. Validation: - New regression tests: 9 failed and 2 passed on unchanged upstream; all 11 pass with the fix. - `pytest test/utils/ test/core/parser/lexer_test.py`: 191 passed, 10 skipped because the Rust extension is unavailable. - Standalone `rustc` 1.86.0 probes: 276 compiled literal cases preserve the original UTF-8 bytes, including every ASCII character, Unicode, CRLF, quotes, backslashes and deterministic random inputs. - `pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` pass. The full Python suite and Rust backend build/parity suite were not run locally. The Rust probes compile literals extracted from actual generator output, not the backend. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Included tests: 11 generator-output cases in `test/utils/build_lexers_test.py`. AI assistance: Codex assisted the implementation, regression tests, review and execution of the checks above. Human review and manual validation are pending. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes Rust `StringLexer` template escaping so generated lexers compile and preserve their original contents. Previously, templates were inserted verbatim into Rust string literals: backslashes and double quotes could break compilation, and input like a literal `\n` would compile with different contents. Templates now escape backslashes, double quotes, and ASCII controls using Rust string escapes. Generated output for all 28 existing dialects is byte-identical, and 11 regression cases in `test/utils/build_lexers_test.py` cover the escape paths. Written for commit 4f6b6bad1212a7e4245166dd8e60d75912666da5. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: perf(reflow): speed up building reflow sequences
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Follow-up to #8743. LT01, LT02, LT05 and LT14 each build a reflow sequence for the whole file. Much of their time went into two setup steps that repeated work: - DepthMap.from_parent() gave each raw segment its own copy of its ancestor stack, built through raw_segments_with_ancestors. That copied the stack once per level, so the cost per raw segment grew with the square of its depth. It now walks the tree once and shares the parts of the stack that siblings have in common. The depth info is the same. - ReflowBlock.from_config() built a new BlockConfig for every parent of every block. That only depends on the parent's class types, so ReflowConfig now caches it. This doesn't depend on #8743. The two PRs change different files. Rule time with only that rule on, best of 3 (Python 3.13): | Rule | File | Before (s) | After (s) | Change | Speed-up | | ----- | ---------------- | ---------: | --------: | -----: | -------: | | LT01 | 1,000 CTEs | 1.61 | 0.68 | -58% | 2.4x | | LT02 | 1,000 CTEs | 1.68 | 0.69 | -59% | 2.4x | | LT05 | 1,000 CTEs | 1.41 | 0.57 | -60% | 2.5x | | LT14 | 1,000 CTEs | 1.36 | 0.49 | -64% | 2.8x | | LT01 | 1,000 statements | 1.62 | 0.78 | -52% | 2.1x | | LT02 | 1,000 statements | 1.68 | 0.79 | -53% | 2.1x | | LT05 | 1,000 statements | 1.50 | 0.67 | -56% | 2.3x | | LT14 | 1,000 statements | 1.47 | 0.63 | -57% | 2.3x | | Total | | 12.32 | 5.29 | -57% | 2.3x | On 562 T-SQL files (mostly dbt models) with their own config (Python 3.14, Rust parser), LT01, LT02 and LT05 together fell from 57.1 s to 29.1 s (-49%). Time in all rules fell from 81.9 s to 53.9 s (-34%), and the whole run from 164.4 s to 126.6 s (-23%). ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - No change in behavior: lint results and fixed output are identical before and after on all 2,352 dialect fixtures and the 562 T-SQL files, with all rules on, in lint and fix mode. The depth info is identical for every raw segment in those files. - ReflowConfig keeps the BlockConfig objects it caches, and callers share them, so they must not change them. None do. - raw_segments_with_ancestors is no longer used inside sqlfluff. I left it in place because it's public and has its own tests. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other: test_reflow_depthmap_from_raws_and_root now compares the two ways of building a depth map on more queries, including a file with no code. The existing reflow and rule tests cover the rest. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up building reflow sequences so LT01, LT02, LT05, and LT14 run roughly 2–3x faster, with no change to lint results or fixed output. - `DepthMap.from_parent()` now walks the tree once, sharing the parts of ancestor stacks that siblings have in common instead of rebuilding a full stack for every raw segment at every level. - `ReflowConfig` now caches block configs for parent segments, which depend only on the parent's class types; cache hits are shared, so callers must not mutate them. - `raw_segments_with_ancestors` is no longer used inside sqlfluff but stays as public API, and the depth map test now checks equivalence on more queries, including a file with no code. Written for commit f5088b47ded0ebdd35d2a0024c53ae6e9d0316db. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(tsql): support HASH indexes and BUCKET_COUNT on memory-optimized tables
pulls.body:
### Brief summary of the change made

Fixes #8737

In T-SQL memory-optimized tables, hash indexes can be declared on primary keys, unique constraints, and inline indexes with `[NONCLUSTERED] HASH` and `WITH (BUCKET_COUNT = ...)`. Previously, `HASH` was not recognized in `PrimaryKeyGrammar`, `ColumnConstraintSegment`, or `TableIndexSegment`, and `BUCKET_COUNT` was not included in `RelationalIndexOptionsSegment` or unreserved keywords, causing parse errors.

This change:
- Adds `BUCKET_COUNT` to `UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS` in `dialect_tsql_keywords.py`.
- Adds `BUCKET_COUNT` to `RelationalIndexOptionsSegment` in `dialect_tsql.py`.
- Updates `PrimaryKeyGrammar`, `TableIndexSegment`, and `ColumnConstraintSegment` to allow `NONCLUSTERED HASH` and `HASH`.
- Adds test fixtures and YAML parse trees for table constraints, column constraints, and inline indexes.

### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of?

None.

pulls.title: T-SQL: Support GROUP BY GROUPING SETS, CUBE, and ROLLUP (#8738)
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8738. This PR adds support for `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (...)`, `CUBE (...)`, `ROLLUP (...)`, `()`, and optional `ALL` in the T-SQL dialect: - Overrides `GroupByClauseTerminatorGrammar` in `tsql_dialect` to include T-SQL specific terminators without referring to keywords like `QUALIFY` (which are not present in T-SQL). - Updates `GroupByClauseSegment` to include `GroupingSetsClauseSegment`, `CubeRollupClauseSegment`, `Bracketed()` (for empty grouping sets), and optional `ALL` within its delimited list, using `GroupByClauseTerminatorGrammar`. - Adds positive test fixtures under `test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/group_by_grouping_sets.sql` and the corresponding generated `.yml`. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None. All 548 existing T-SQL dialect tests and termination fixtures pass with zero regressions. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Implements T-SQL `GROUP BY` support for `GROUPING SETS`, `CUBE`, `ROLLUP`, empty grouping sets `()`, and the optional `ALL` modifier, fixing issue #8738 where `GROUPING SETS` with multiple sets failed to parse. - Extracts the `GroupByClause` terminators into a dialect-specific `GroupByClauseTerminatorGrammar` so T-SQL doesn't depend on ANSI-only keywords like `QUALIFY`. - Adds test fixtures covering all new grouping clause forms, with all 548 existing T-SQL tests passing unchanged. Written for commit 641e6c7b5911294f1a8b590dbe61f5b90df3832a. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: T-SQL: Support $action inside expressions in MERGE OUTPUT clause (#8739)
pulls.body: Fixes #8739 ### Description In a T-SQL `MERGE` statement, `$action` is a pseudo-column available within the `OUTPUT` clause. Previously, `ActionParameterSegment` was only matched as a direct top-level item in `OutputClauseSegment`, causing parse errors when `$action` was used inside expressions such as `CASE $action WHEN ...`, `IIF($action = ...)`, or `CASE WHEN $action = ...`. ### Changes - Added `Ref("ActionParameterSegment")` to `Expression_D_Grammar` and `BaseExpressionElementGrammar` in `dialect_tsql`. - Added test fixtures in `test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/merge_output_action_expression.sql` and generated the matching `.yml` fixture. ### Verification - Ran full T-SQL dialect test suite: 551/551 passed. - Verified with `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check`. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8739: T-SQL `MERGE` statements no longer fail to parse when `$action` appears inside an expression in the `OUTPUT` clause, such as `CASE $action WHEN ...`, `IIF($action = ...)`, or `CASE WHEN $action = ...`. Previously `$action` was only matched as a direct top-level output item. - Adds `Ref("ActionParameterSegment")` to the expression grammar in `dialect_tsql.py`. - Adds parse fixtures covering `CASE`, `IIF`, and `CASE WHEN` forms of `$action` inside `OUTPUT`. Written for commit 7106938a9b6dcd5b8c063622e76ac67247cce2b5. Summary will update on new commits. ### AI-Assistance Disclosure This contribution was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent (Google Antigravity / Gemini) to investigate issue #8739 and locate the relevant grammar segments in `dialect_tsql.py`. - **Manual Validation:** I verified the grammar changes against Microsoft's official T-SQL documentation for the `MERGE OUTPUT` clause, ran the full local T-SQL test suite (551/551 tests passing), generated the YAML fixtures using `test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py`, and verified clean styling with `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check`. - I take full responsibility for the correctness and maintainability of this pull request.

pulls.title: T-SQL: allow empty OVER () after WITHIN GROUP
pulls.body: ## Summary Fixes #8740: in the T-SQL dialect, `PERCENTILE_CONT` / `PERCENTILE_DISC` with `WITHIN GROUP (...)` followed by an empty `OVER ()` failed to parse, because the `WithinGroupClause` required a non-empty `PARTITION BY` inside the `OVER` brackets. ## Changes - `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_tsql.py`: make the `PartitionClauseSegment` reference optional inside the `OVER` brackets of `WithinGroupClause` (with `ParseMode.GREEDY`, mirroring the ANSI `OverClauseSegment`), so `OVER ()` parses. `OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` is unaffected. - `test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/functions_agg.sql` (+ regenerated `.yml`): add `PERCENTILE_CONT`/`PERCENTILE_DISC ... OVER ()` cases. ## Test Plan - Red/green: before the change the two new fixture statements were unparsable (the yml generator refused to generate); after it they parse and `test__dialect__base_parse_struct[tsql-functions_agg...]` passes. - `pytest test/dialects/dialects_test.py -k tsql`: 548 passed. Regression on ansi/synapse/duckdb/postgres: 1276 passed. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8740: T-SQL now allows an empty `OVER ()` after `WITHIN GROUP` for `PERCENTILE_CONT` and `PERCENTILE_DISC`. Previously the parser required a `PARTITION BY` inside the `OVER` brackets. The `PartitionClauseSegment` is now optional, mirroring ANSI behavior; `OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` still parses as before. Written for commit 0988dc1ced96a95e34ae96be2244d3fe21f2b6df. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Keep subquery and row-constructor parentheses in ST08 fixes
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made fixes #8744 In its `select_clause` path, ST08 removed the parentheses after `DISTINCT` whenever they were the first target expression's only child, without looking inside them. `SELECT DISTINCT (a, b) FROM foo` was turned into two columns in PostgreSQL, including with the default rules. With `--rules ST08 --dialect ansi`, `SELECT DISTINCT (SELECT a FROM t), b FROM foo` became SQL that no longer parses. The `select_clause` path now keeps the brackets when they contain a `select_statement`, using the same `recursive_crawl("select_statement", recurse_into=False)` check as the `function` path, or a comma directly inside them, as in `(a, b)`. In those cases the existing branch that only ensures a space after `DISTINCT` applies. `DISTINCT(a)` and the existing `COUNT(DISTINCT(...))` column, concat and subquery cases behave as before. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The subquery check is conservative: it also retains optional outer parentheses around expressions containing a nested `SELECT`, such as `SELECT DISTINCT (COALESCE((SELECT a FROM t), b)) FROM foo`. `SELECT DISTINCT(SELECT a FROM t), b FROM foo` is still flagged, but the fix now only adds the space after `DISTINCT` and keeps the subquery's parentheses. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`: `test_pass_distinct_scalar_subquery`, `test_fail_distinct_scalar_subquery_missing_space` and `test_pass_distinct_row_constructor` (postgres) in `ST08.yml`. On 078bf03, the two `pass_str` cases fail because ST08 reports unwanted violations, and the missing-space case fails its `fix_str` assertion because ST08 removes the subquery parentheses. All three pass with the change. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: not needed. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate: none. Validation outside the sandbox (Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS, Python 3.12.15): `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts='' test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k ST08 -q` passes (14 passed); with the new tests and production code from 078bf03, the three new cases fail and the 11 existing cases pass. The full `yaml_test_cases_test.py` run shows the same three pre-existing LT01 `VARIADIC ARRAY` spacing failures with and without this change. The changed-file ruff check, ruff format and codespell hooks pass. With the change, `sqlfluff fix --rules ST08` leaves the already-spaced row-constructor and scalar-subquery examples from the issue byte-for-byte unchanged, using `--dialect postgres` and `--dialect ansi` respectively; subsequent `sqlfluff lint` runs with those dialects report no parse errors. AI disclosure: the fix and the test cases were drafted with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex, coordinated with Claude Code). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8744. ST08 no longer removes the parentheses after `DISTINCT` in the `select_clause` path when they contain a subquery or a comma, so `SELECT DISTINCT (a, b) FROM foo` stays a row constructor and `SELECT DISTINCT (SELECT a FROM t), b FROM foo` remains parseable. Uses the same `recursive_crawl("select_statement", recurse_into=False)` check as the `function` path to detect subqueries, and keeps brackets containing a comma. `DISTINCT(a)` and existing `COUNT(DISTINCT(...))` cases behave as before. The subquery check is conservative: it also retains outer parentheses around expressions with a nested `SELECT`, such as `SELECT DISTINCT (COALESCE((SELECT a FROM t), b)) FROM foo`. Written for commit 472b3eea1088ae394a645cf9c9a88ab3c591b574. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: perf: avoid quadratic work in layout rules
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Follow-up to #8726. Several layout rules repeated a search over the whole parent, or the whole file, for each segment they checked, so their time grew with the square of the query size. - get_parent() compared each earlier sibling with ==. path_to() calls it at every level for each violation and fix, so LT01, LT02 and LT14 slowed down with many violations in one clause. It now checks the stored index first. - LT03, LT04: the shortcut used parent.segments.index(). It now uses context.segment_idx. - LT05 (with ignore_comment_lines or ignore_comment_clauses), LT07, LT11: called raw_segments.index() for each target (LT11 through from_around_target()). The new BaseSegment.raw_segment_index() returns the same index as list.index(), from maps cached with raw_segments. - LT07, LT15: provide_raw_stack rebuilds a tuple of every raw segment so far at each step. LT07 never read it. LT15 now looks back from its own index, and its batch check uses the parent's cached child types instead of copying all siblings for each newline. - LT08: built a log message from the rest of the WITH statement for each CTE, even with logging off. - LT09: with many targets on one line, searched for the previous target once per target. Rule time with only that rule on, best of 3 (Python 3.13): | Rule | Case | Before (s) | After (s) | Change | Speed-up | | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------: | --------: | -----: | -------: | | LT01 | 1,000 columns, spaces before each comma (1,000 violations) | 2.73 | 0.21 | -92% | 13x | | LT02 | INSERT with 1,000 VALUES rows (1,000 violations) | 2.78 | 0.61 | -78% | 5x | | LT03 | 1,000 AND conditions, one per line | 4.91 | 0.10 | -98% | 48x | | LT04 | 1,000 columns, one per line | 0.96 | 0.02 | -98% | 42x | | LT07 | 1,000 CTEs | 5.84 | 0.08 | -99% | 73x | | LT08 | 1,000 CTEs (999 violations) | 1.65 | 0.08 | -95% | 20x | | LT09 | 1,000 columns on one line | 3.64 | 0.07 | -98% | 56x | | LT11 | 1,000 UNION ALL branches | 19.54 | 0.34 | -98% | 58x | | LT14 | 1,000 one-line UPDATEs (1,000 violations) | 4.63 | 2.89 | -37% | 2x | | LT15 | 1,000 statements | 9.17 | 0.16 | -98% | 58x | | Total | | 55.86 | 4.56 | -92% | 12x | LT02 and LT14 now spend most of their time building the reflow sequence. I'll send a separate PR for that. On 562 T-SQL files (mostly dbt models) with their own config (Python 3.14, Rust parser), LT03, LT04, LT07, LT08, LT09, LT11 and LT15 together fell from 6.93 s to 4.16 s (-40%), mostly in LT04 (2.93 s to 0.68 s) and LT15 (1.45 s to 1.03 s). ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - No change in behavior: lint results and fixed output are identical before and after on all 2,351 dialect fixtures and the 562 T-SQL files, with all rules on, in lint and fix mode. - raw_segment_index() caches two dicts, each with one entry per raw segment, on the segment it's called on: the file root, and each WITH statement for LT07. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other: tests for raw_segment_index(), and for LT15 after LT08 inserts the same newline twice. The existing rule tests cover the rest. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up the layout rules by removing searches that grew quadratically with query or file size. Lint results and fixed output are identical before and after. - Adds `BaseSegment.raw_segment_index()` to replace repeated `raw_segments.index()` calls with a cached lookup; used by LT05, LT07, LT11 (via `from_around_target()`), `deduce_line_indent()`, and a new test covers its semantics. - `get_parent()` checks the stored index by identity first, avoiding comparison with every earlier sibling during path-to-root walks for violations and fixes. - LT03 and LT04 use the crawler-provided `segment_idx` instead of calling `parent.segments.index()`. - LT07 and LT15 stop requesting `provide_raw_stack`, which rebuilt the whole raw stack at every crawled segment. LT15 now indexes back from its own position; a new test covers LT08 inserting the same newline twice. - LT15 checks the parent's cached child types for batches instead of scanning all siblings, and LT08 builds its INFO log message only when logging is enabled. - LT09 caches target indices when many select targets share one line instead of searching clause children per target. - Adds a test for `select_children()` stopping early on `loop_while`, as LT09 was its only caller until it stopped using it. pulls.title: LT09: Don't move meta segments out of the select clause
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `sqlfluff fix` with LT02 and LT09 crashes LT09 for this SparkSQL query when `implicit_indents = require` is set: ```sql SELECT * FROM ( SELECT a FROM t ) x JOIN y ON x.a = y.a; ``` ``` CRITICAL [LT09] ... threw an Exception: Invalid edit found: [, , ]. AssertionError: Invalid edit found: ... ``` LT09 is skipped for the file, so it is only partly fixed (for example `SELECT\n * FROM (`). `lint` is not affected. It reproduces on SparkSQL (and Databricks, which inherits it) and not on ANSI, with a single select target, a multi-line subquery in `FROM`, and a `JOIN` after it. Cause: after LT02 splits `SELECT *` onto two lines, the select clause children are ordered differently by dialect: ``` ansi: SELECT, indent, newline, ws, element, dedent sparksql: SELECT, newline, ws, indent, element, dedent ``` In SparkSQL the `Indent` sits inside the range that `_eval_single_select_target_element` selects as leftovers to move after the clause. It is then deleted and re-inserted as a zero-width segment, which `LintFix` rejects. The range now excludes meta segments, so they stay in the clause together with their `Dedent`, which is what already happens for ANSI. Only skipping the re-insert is not enough, as the `Indent` is still deleted and its `Dedent` is left unbalanced. Adds an autofix test (`sparksql/002_LT02_LT09_single_target_subquery_join`) which fails on main and passes with this change. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? No. Meta segments are zero-width and are not part of the moved text. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser fixtures in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a crash in `sqlfluff fix` when LT02 and LT09 run together on a SparkSQL query with `implicit_indents = require`. Previously the crash caused LT09 to be skipped, leaving the file only partially fixed. **Bug Fixes** - In SparkSQL, the select clause `Indent` sits inside the range LT09 moves after the clause, so moving it creates a zero-width segment that `LintFix` rejects. - Excludes meta segments from the moved range so they stay in the clause with their `Dedent`. - Adds a SparkSQL autofix test case that failed on main and passes with this change. pulls.title: Fix LT02 crash when implicit_indents = require collapses a line break
pulls.body:
### Brief summary of the change made

With `implicit_indents = require`, linting this query crashes instead of reporting violations:

```sql
SELECT 1 AS u
FROM
(
  SELECT 1 AS c
  FROM t
) p
```

```
AssertionError: <WhitespaceSegment: (None) '    '> has no PositionMarker
```

`[sqlfluff:indentation] implicit_indents = require` and rule LT02 are enough to reproduce it, in ANSI as well as other dialects.

Cause: `_convert_newlines_to_spaces` runs after the per-line indent pass. The point between `FROM` and `(` has by then been rewritten to contain whitespace that the indent pass created for the `(` line. The collapse emitted `LintFix.delete()` for every segment after the first, including that new whitespace, which isn't in the tree. `_process_lint_result` then called `root.path_to()` on it and hit the assertion.

Two changes in `reindent.py`:

- Build the collapse from the original `elements` (whose segments are in the tree) instead of the working copy, so it never anchors or deletes on segments created by the indent pass.
- Drop indent results whose fixes anchor on a segment the collapse is already fixing. They replaced the same newline, and conflicting fixes on one anchor are never applied, so `sqlfluff fix` reported the violations as unfixable.

After this, lint reports the violations and `fix` collapses to `FROM (` and is stable on a second run.

### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of?

Indent results for a line break that is being removed are no longer reported (they were spurious, as the line is being joined to the previous one).

pulls.title: perf(LT09): avoid quadratic search in wide select clauses
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made LT09 slowed down sharply on select clauses with many targets, even when every target was already on its own line. Its run time grew with the square of the number of targets. This PR makes it grow linearly. - For each target, LT09 looks for the last code segment before it with Segments.select, passing the previous match as start_seg and the target as stop_seg. - Segments.select finds both segments with tuple.index. That scans from the start of the clause and runs a segment equality check on each segment it passes. - With 2,000 columns, one per line, that came to about 16 million equality checks, and LT09 alone took 5 s. - LT09 now remembers where the previous match was and searches forward from there. The same clause now needs about 20,000 checks. LT09 time on its own, with only LT09 enabled (best of 3 runs, Python 3.13): | Case | Before (s) | After (s) | Change | Speed-up | | --------------------------------- | ---------: | --------: | -----: | -------: | | 250 columns, one per line | 0.066 | 0.008 | -88% | 9x | | 500 columns, one per line | 0.278 | 0.014 | -95% | 20x | | 1,000 columns, one per line | 1.159 | 0.031 | -97% | 37x | | 2,000 columns, one per line | 5.001 | 0.066 | -99% | 76x | | Real T-SQL dbt model, 535 columns | 4.189 | 0.049 | -99% | 86x | | Total | 10.693 | 0.167 | -98% | 64x | On a real project of 562 T-SQL dbt files (sqlfluff 4.4.0, Rust parser, Python 3.14, all rules on), LT09's total time fell from 41.8 s to 2.1 s. To reproduce, write a file with SELECT, then col_0 to col_999 one per line, then FROM wide_table. Then run sqlfluff lint wide.sql --dialect ansi --rules LT09 --bench and read the linting line. The CLI skips files over 20,000 bytes by default, so 1,000 columns is about the largest case it will run. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - Behaviour does not change. tuple.index returns the first equal segment, and two different code segments in one parse tree are never equal, because equality compares the class, the raw text and the start position. So a search that starts at the previous match finds the same segments as one that starts at the beginning. - To check this, I ran LT09 with fixing on, before and after the change, on all 2,350 dialect fixture files, all 123 SQL files in the autofix fixtures and 562 private T-SQL dbt files. Each set ran twice: once with default settings, and once with wildcard_policy = multiple and single_target_policy = new_line, so single targets take this path too. The violations and the fixed SQL matched for every file. The multi-target check ran 17,834 times, on 75,631 targets in total. - LT09 is still slow when many targets share one line, for two reasons outside this change. LT09 calls get_child("select_clause_modifier") once for each flagged target, and the shared rule code calls path_to once for each fix. With 2,000 columns on one line, LT09 drops only from 18.0 s to 14.0 s. I can follow up on that in a separate PR. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other: no new tests. Behaviour is unchanged, and the existing LT09 cases run every changed line. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes LT09's quadratic slowdown on wide select clauses. For each select target, LT09 scanned the whole clause from the start to find the preceding code segment; a 2,000-column SELECT took about 16 million segment equality checks and 5 s. It now searches forward from the previous match, reducing the same clause to about 20,000 checks and 0.07 s. Results are unchanged — two different code segments in one parse tree are never equal, so the same segments are found. This was verified by running LT09 with autofix over all dialect fixtures, autofix fixtures, and 562 private T-SQL dbt files. LT09 is still slow when many targets share one line; that is left for a follow-up PR. Written for commit 9423b8daa03dffa1166d2ddf34c1af71806e8cfb. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(ST01): preserve comments when removing redundant ELSE NULL
pulls.body: ## Summary `Rule_ST01` (`structure.else_null`) removes a redundant `ELSE NULL` branch from a `CASE` on autofix. It deleted the entire `else_clause` segment as one unit, so a comment nested in the clause — e.g. `else /* keep default */ null` — was a child of the deleted segment and got silently dropped, with no lint message, log line, or `--fix` diagnostic. **Impact: data-loss on autofix.** ST01 is in the default `all` group. Fixes #8562. ## Reproduce ```sql select case when name = 'cat' then 'meow' when name = 'dog' then 'woof' else /* keep default */ null end from x ``` `sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules ST01` previously deleted `else /* keep default */ null` entirely, comment included. ## Fix In `Rule_ST01._eval`, before deleting, collect comment children of the `else_clause`. With no comments the behaviour is unchanged. With comments, re-home them in place of the clause via `LintFix.replace`, keeping the preceding newline/indent so the comment stays on its own line between the last `WHEN` and `END`. The redundant `null` is still removed. ## Tests Added `redundant_else_null_preserves_comment` to `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/ST01.yml`; fails on main, passes with the fix. ST01/ST02 suites pass; output is idempotent and lints clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `Rule_ST01` (`structure.else_null`) so its autofix no longer silently drops comments nested in a redundant `ELSE NULL` branch. The comments are kept in place of the removed clause, still on their own line between the last `WHEN` and `END`. **Bug Fixes** - A comment like `else /* keep default */ null` now survives the fix as `/* keep default */` instead of being deleted with no diagnostic. - When the clause contains no comments, the autofix behavior is unchanged. pulls.title: fix(snowflake): parse date parts by function argument position
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Snowflake currently parses a unit-looking column such as `year` or `month` as a date part in multi-argument function calls. CP01 consequently uppercases `year` in `my_udf(year, 1)`, while CP02 misses the corresponding identifier in `my_udf(YEAR, 1)`. The same unconditional grammar also misclassifies ordinary expression arguments of date functions, including `d` in `DATEADD(YEAR, 1, d)`. This change recognizes bare date parts in the documented argument slots of unqualified date functions. The first slot is used by DATEADD/DATEDIFF and their aliases, DATE_TRUNC, DATE_PART and EXTRACT; the second slot is used by LAST_DAY and TRUNC/TRUNCATE. Other arguments use the existing Snowflake expression grammar. Both comma and FROM extraction forms, quoted date units, named arguments, lambdas and function suffixes remain supported. Qualified and quoted function names keep generic expression arguments. The new parser fixture covers these distinctions, and CP01/CP02 fixtures verify the resulting lint and fix behavior. Related discussion: #8654 explicitly identified this Snowflake behavior and left it outside its BigQuery scope. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The changes are limited to the Snowflake dialect and its tests. No existing parser fixture trees change. This is a parsing and lint-policy correction; the case-only changes to unquoted Snowflake identifiers in the reproducer do not establish SQL semantic corruption. TRUNC/TRUNCATE have an inherently ambiguous second argument: a bare word such as `month` can be a date unit or a numeric scale column. Without type information, this patch preserves the existing date-part interpretation in that slot. General numeric scale expressions and the first argument remain expressions. ### Validation Executed locally on Python 3.12.14 and Rust 1.99.0, with the extension rebuilt from this source: - Negative controls on clean main: the new rule cases have three failures, and the new parser-tree comparison fails; both pass with the correction. - `pytest test/ -q -n 4 -m "not dbt"`: 11,697 passed, 2,675 skipped, zero failures. The venv CLI was available on PATH. - `pytest test/dialects/ -k snowflake -q -n 4`: 783 passed in the Python-only environment and 783 passed with the rebuilt Rust extension selected by default auto configuration. - `pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k "CP01 or CP02" -q -n 4`: 86 passed in each parser environment. - Additional explicit Python, Rust-parser and Rust-rules configurations: five Snowflake rule cases and the complete new parser fixture match in each configuration; fixes are idempotent. The checks assert the actual Rust arena, and native CP01 invocation is verified (CP02 remains Python). - `cargo test --release --test fixture_tests snowflake -- --nocapture`: both test functions passed; all 256 fixtures passed parsing and YAML comparison. - `python test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py -d snowflake`: all 256 fixtures generated successfully, with no existing fixture changes. - `python utils/rustify.py check` and `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed. - Independent Codex review: no blocking findings; five rule cases, three parser/broad-fix checks and 19 additional idempotent parse/fix probes passed. No live Snowflake execution or dbt templater testing was performed. ### AI assistance disclosure Codex inspected the source and primary Snowflake documentation, prepared the implementation and synthetic fixtures, generated the parser YAML, and ran the local validation. A separate Codex agent independently reviewed the source, fixtures and additional parse/fix probes. This describes automated implementation, verification and review; no personal human validation or live Snowflake execution is claimed. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Completed the applicable contribution steps. - Included `.sql`/generated `.yml` parser coverage and CP01/CP02 `.yml` rule cases. - Added grammar docstrings explaining the positional dispatch and the retained overload ambiguity. - Regenerated and checked the Rust dialect tables and rebuilt the extension from source. - No separate follow-up issue is necessary for this bounded correction. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes Snowflake parsing so unit-looking identifiers like `year` or `month` are treated as ordinary expressions in function calls instead of date parts, which previously caused CP01/CP02 to re-case or ignore them incorrectly. Date parts are now only recognized in the documented argument slots of unqualified Snowflake date functions: the first slot for `DATEADD`, `DATEDIFF`, `DATE_TRUNC`, `DATE_PART`, `EXTRACT` and their aliases; the second slot for `LAST_DAY`, `TRUNC`, and `TRUNCATE`. Qualified and quoted function names, string date units, named arguments, lambdas, and function suffixes keep their existing grammar. Adds parser fixtures and CP01/CP02 rule cases. **Behavior notes** - `TRUNC`/`TRUNCATE`'s second argument stays ambiguous: bare unit words keep the date-part interpretation because type information isn't available to distinguish them from numeric scale columns. Written for commit 9c23a2dfe04b2b2bc2d678f01dd5a4903e39a196. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Postgres: support ALTER COLUMN ... SET EXPRESSION AS
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8705. No other changes. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: added the statement from the issue, a short `ALTER mycolumn SET EXPRESSION AS (a + b)`, and `DROP EXPRESSION [IF EXISTS]` (which had no fixture yet) to `postgres/alter_table.sql`; YAML regenerated with `test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py -d postgres -f alter_table.sql`. - `pytest test/dialects/`: 7353 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean. pulls.title: Postgres: support ONLY in VACUUM and ANALYZE
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made PostgreSQL 18 lets each table in `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE` be written as `[ ONLY ] table_name [ * ]` ([VACUUM](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-vacuum.html), [ANALYZE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-analyze.html)). `ONLY` skips inheritance children and partitions. Neither form parsed with the postgres dialect: ```sql VACUUM ONLY measurements; VACUUM (ANALYZE) ONLY measurements (logdate), events *; ANALYZE VERBOSE ONLY measurements (logdate, peaktemp), ONLY events; ``` This adds an optional `ONLY` before the table reference and an optional `*` after it, in both statements. I don't have a PostgreSQL 18 server here, so I checked this against `vacuum_relation` / `relation_expr` in `gram.y` on `REL_18_STABLE`. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None that I found. Redshift has its own `VACUUM` grammar and isn't affected. Regenerating fixtures for postgres and the dialects that inherit from it (redshift, greenplum, materialize, duckdb) only changed `vacuum.yml` and `analyze.yml`. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: added cases to `postgres/vacuum.sql` and `postgres/analyze.sql`. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. Ran `pytest test/dialects/` (7335 passed), the Rust `fixture_tests` for postgres, and ruff. Made with help from Claude Code. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds support for the optional `ONLY` keyword and trailing `*` per table in PostgreSQL `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE` statements, as introduced in PostgreSQL 18. `ONLY` skips inheritance children and partitions; the grammar now matches the documented syntax with no impact on other dialects. Written for commit ed928cbff8287a1c96f7698d8e3ba39c698a512b. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: DuckDB: parse DESCRIBE and the extra SHOW forms
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made In DuckDB, `DESCRIBE`, `DESC` and `SHOW` are the same statement. Each can be followed by a table name, a query, `ALL TABLES`, `TABLES FROM `, or nothing ([describe](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/guides/meta/describe), [list tables](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/guides/meta/list_tables)). Most of these didn't parse: ```sql DESCRIBE tbl; DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM tbl; SHOW ALL TABLES; SHOW TABLES FROM memory.main; -- was split into two statements SHOW; ``` The only form that already worked was `DESCRIBE TABLE tbl`, through the ANSI object-type grammar. This PR overrides `DescribeStatementSegment` for DuckDB and gives the inherited Postgres `ShowStatementSegment` the same targets. Single-name `SHOW` forms like `SHOW TABLES` or `SHOW tbl` still parse as a `parameter`, same as before. I checked every statement in the new fixture against DuckDB 1.5.6. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None outside the DuckDB dialect. I regenerated the DuckDB fixtures and only the new `describe.yml` was added. `DESCRIBE` used as a subquery (`SELECT * FROM (DESCRIBE tbl)`) isn't covered here. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `duckdb/describe.sql`. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. Ran `pytest test/dialects/` (7338 passed), the Rust `fixture_tests` for duckdb, and ruff. Made with help from Claude Code. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds DuckDB support for `DESCRIBE`, `DESC`, and `SHOW`, which DuckDB treats as the same statement. Besides the previously working `DESCRIBE TABLE tbl`, DuckDB also accepts a table name, a query, `ALL TABLES`, `TABLES FROM `, or nothing after these keywords — none of which parsed before. `SHOW TABLES FROM db` was previously split into two statements. - Overrides `DescribeStatementSegment` for DuckDB and extends the inherited Postgres `ShowStatementSegment` with the same targets. - Single-name `SHOW` forms like `SHOW TABLES` or `SHOW tbl` still parse as a parameter, with no behavior change for existing statements. - Adds a `duckdb/describe.sql` fixture covering all new forms, verified against DuckDB 1.5.6. - Affects only the DuckDB dialect; no other dialect or existing fixture changed. Written for commit 45efcbaeb4d5a0a8670491113e7b86100413e677. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Keep the null-safe equals operator when ST09 swaps operands
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made fixes #8709 ST09 lists `<=>` among the operators it may reorder, but its inversion check looked only at the first raw token and excluded `<>`. In dialects that lex `<=>` as three tokens (mysql, mariadb, hive, impala, doris, starrocks) the leading `<` was inverted, so `sqlfluff fix` wrote `a.x >=> b.y`, which no longer parses. The inversion check now uses `operator_str` and inverts only the directional operators `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=`, preserving `<=>` when the operands are swapped. Other operator handling and the reorderable-operator allowlist are unchanged. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None found. The existing ST09 cases, including the `<=` → `>=` inversion and the unchanged `!=`/`<>` cases, still pass. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`: `test_fail_mysql_lt_eq_gt_operator` and `test_fail_hive_lt_eq_gt_operator` in `ST09.yml` (both fail on c9fc51c because the fixed SQL contains `ON bt.test >=> st.test` instead of `ON bt.test <=> st.test`; both pass with the change). - Added appropriate documentation for the change: not needed. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate: none. Validation on 43a73ad (based on c9fc51c), with SQLFluff 4.4.0, Python 3.12.15 and sqlfluffrs 4.4.0: `test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py` passes all 2605 tests with the default Rust parser, and the 32 ST09 cases also pass with the Python parser. On c9fc51c the same ST09 fixtures give the two expected failures and 30 passing cases. The repository's pre-commit hooks on the changed files (mypy, yamllint, ruff check, ruff format, codespell) pass. With the change, `sqlfluff fix --rules ST09 --dialect mysql` on `SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON b.y <=> a.x;` writes `SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON a.x <=> b.y;`, and `sqlfluff lint --dialect mysql` then reports no parse error (only the unrelated AM04, RF02 and AM05 for that toy query). AI disclosure: the fix, the test cases and this description were prepared with AI tools (OpenAI Codex for the code, Claude Code for coordination and review). The test runs, the CLI reproduction and the pre-commit checks above were run by those tools, and their outputs were checked before submitting; there was no additional manual testing beyond them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes ST09 so operand swapping no longer corrupts the null-safe equals operator `<=>`. In dialects that lex `<=>` as three tokens (mysql, mariadb, hive, impala, doris, starrocks), ST09's inversion check only looked at the leading `<` and rewrote `<=>` as `>=>`, producing SQL that no longer parsed. The check now inverts only the directional operators `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=`, leaving `<=>` intact when operands are swapped. - Adds mysql and hive test cases that fail with the old behavior and pass with the fix. - Operator handling and the reorderable-operator allowlist are unchanged. Written for commit b6c9480054dd15869a5f462e35170a62a5d8771b. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: ClickHouse: parse comma-separated ALTER TABLE actions
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made fixes #8707 ClickHouse parses `ALTER TABLE` actions as a comma-separated list. The action `OneOf` in `AlterTableStatementSegment` is now wrapped in `Delimited`, so `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a UInt8, ADD COLUMN b UInt8` parses as one statement. A single action parses exactly as before: every existing ClickHouse fixture regenerates unchanged. `MODIFY QUERY` takes a whole `SELECT`, whose select list has its own commas. Inside the new `Delimited`, the action comma would end that select early. Its `SelectStatementSegment` reference now resets inherited terminators and keeps only the statement delimiter, which restores the previous parse of `ALTER TABLE mv MODIFY QUERY SELECT id, name FROM t`. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None found. The `UPDATE` mutation's assignment list keeps its commas inside the one action, and a trailing `SETTINGS` clause still follows the last action. A trailing, doubled or leading comma remains a parse error. ### AI assistance Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the grammar change, the fixtures, the tests and this description, and ran the checks below. Not run locally: the full tox matrix and mypy. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `clickhouse/alter_table_multiple_actions.sql` covers two actions, `ON CLUSTER` with `IF NOT EXISTS ... AFTER`, three mixed actions, an `UPDATE` with two assignments, and actions followed by `SETTINGS`. - Other: `test/dialects/clickhouse_test.py` asserts `PRS` for a trailing, doubled and leading action comma. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes ClickHouse `ALTER TABLE` parsing so comma-separated action lists like `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN a UInt8, ADD COLUMN b UInt8` parse as one statement instead of failing. pulls.title: fix(jinja): support dbt materialization blocks in the Jinja templater
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #6215. Add support for dbt's `{% materialization %}` blocks to SQLFluff's Jinja templater. Previously, files containing these blocks could fail with an `unknown tag 'materialization'` templating error. The new Jinja extension parses materialization declarations and registers them as macros, following dbt's naming and argument conventions. The implementation supports: - Default and adapter-specific materializations. - Explicit `supported_languages` values. - dbt's default `supported_languages=['sql']` when the argument is omitted. - Validation of unsupported or malformed arguments. pulls.title: fix(bigquery): parse date parts by argument position
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #5015. Builds on the discussion in the closed, unmerged #8219 and #8654, including the authors' and reviewers' feedback on argument positions and `SAFE.` dispatch. BigQuery currently recognizes date-part words in every function argument. As a result, CP01 can change a column such as `year` in `REGEXP_EXTRACT(year, ...)`, and CP02 cannot consistently recognize those arguments as identifiers. This change restricts date-part recognition to the documented argument positions of the date/time difference, truncation, and `LAST_DAY` functions. Other arguments, including timestamp time-zone expressions, use the expression grammar. `SAFE.`-prefixed built-ins use the same positional grammar, while dataset-qualified UDFs keep ordinary expression arguments. Existing unqualified chained calls use the corresponding grammar after omitting the first expression supplied by the chain. This preserves actual date units in calls such as `(year).DATE_DIFF(month, YEAR)` and `(year).LAST_DAY(WEEK(MONDAY))`. The existing `EXTRACT` and `INTERVAL` paths continue to recognize their date units. Regression tests cover ordinary arguments, every affected function group, `SAFE.`, date-part positions, optional time zones, `WEEK(MONDAY)`, and existing chained calls. Both CP01 and CP02 expectations distinguish actual date units from column references. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The change is limited to the BigQuery dialect grammar and its tests. Two existing generated parser fixtures now correctly classify ordinary arguments as column references: `parse_date(..., year)` in `parameters.yml`, and `DAY` passed to the existing generic `SAFE.DATEADD(...)` example in `select_safe_function.yml`. This does not add `DATEADD` as a BigQuery built-in. The existing supported scope of unqualified chained calls is retained. Support for parenthesized multi-part chained function names is outside this change. Validation completed locally on Python 3.12.14 and the Rust extension built from this source using Rust 1.99.0: - Original five regressions: five failures on the base revision, then passing with the fix. - Two chained-call regressions: reproduced against the first implementation, then passing with the complete fix. - CP01/CP02 fixtures with explicitly selected Python, Rust-parser, and Rust-rules configurations, plus a complete new-fixture tree comparison: 268 passed. The verification asserts the actual Rust arena is present for Rust runs. - BigQuery parser, structure, and broad-fix suite with the Python parser selected: 455 passed. - The same BigQuery suite with the rebuilt Rust extension installed and selected by the default `auto` configuration: 455 passed. - Native Rust BigQuery fixture tests: both test functions passed; 145 fixtures passed with zero failures. - `python utils/rustify.py check`: passed. - `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks passed, including mypy, yamllint, Ruff, and codespell. ### AI assistance disclosure Codex prepared the implementation and regression tests, generated the parser fixtures, and ran the local validation above. Separate Codex agents reviewed the implementation and test coverage; that review found the chained-call regression, which was then fixed and revalidated. These are automated implementation, testing, and review activities. `normaltank` has not yet personally reviewed the patch, so this is intended as a draft for review. Maintainer approval is still required before merging. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Completed the applicable contribution steps below. - Included `.yml` rule tests and `.sql`/generated `.yml` parser fixtures. - Added grammar docstrings and comments explaining the positional and chained argument handling. - Regenerated and checked the Rust dialect tables, built the extension, and tested actual parser parity. - No separate follow-up issue is needed for this bounded fix. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #5015 by restricting BigQuery date-part recognition to documented argument positions so columns named `year`, `month`, etc. are no longer incorrectly parsed as date units. - Applies positional grammar to `DATE_DIFF`, `TIME_DIFF`, `DATETIME_DIFF`, `TIMESTAMP_DIFF`, truncation functions, and `LAST_DAY`, including `SAFE.` prefixed forms. - Chained calls like `(year).DATE_DIFF(month, YEAR)` keep the same behavior by omitting the first expression. - Updates two existing parser fixtures; no new built-in functions are added. Written for commit a1c4b1a5a0246edbfb82ff0b106b8253ce29b196. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: DuckDB: parse GROUPING SETS, CUBE and ROLLUP in GROUP BY
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made The DuckDB dialect overrides `GroupByClauseSegment` (for `GROUP BY ALL` and trailing commas), but the override left out the grouping set constructs that ANSI and Postgres support. So: - `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((a, b), (a), ())` was unparsable - `GROUP BY ()` was unparsable - `GROUP BY CUBE (a, b)` / `GROUP BY ROLLUP (a, b)` parsed, but only as plain function calls rather than `cube_rollup_clause` This adds `CubeRollupClauseSegment`, `GroupingSetsClauseSegment` and empty brackets to the DuckDB GROUP BY element list, the same way the Postgres dialect does. Since they're inside the delimited list, mixed forms like `GROUP BY country, ROLLUP (city, street_name)` work too. DuckDB docs: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/grouping_sets Every statement in the new fixture also runs on DuckDB 1.5.6. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? `CUBE (...)` / `ROLLUP (...)` in a DuckDB GROUP BY now give a `cube_rollup_clause` node instead of a `function` node, which matches the other dialects. No existing DuckDB fixtures changed. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `duckdb/grouping_sets.sql`. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. Ran `pytest test/dialects/` (7338 passed) and the Rust `fixture_tests` for duckdb. Made with help from Claude Code. --- ## Summary by cubic The DuckDB dialect's `GroupByClauseSegment` override left out grouping set constructs, so `GROUPING SETS` and `GROUP BY ()` were unparsable, and `CUBE`/`ROLLUP` only parsed as plain function calls. This adds `CubeRollupClauseSegment`, `GroupingSetsClauseSegment`, and empty brackets to the GROUP BY element list, matching the Postgres dialect. Mixed forms like `GROUP BY country, ROLLUP (city, street_name)` work because the new constructs sit inside the delimited list. Written for commit 9309a3b137594c4640df8d6a76fcb588178d4371. pulls.title: Trino: parse MATCH_RECOGNIZE row pattern matching
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made trino's `MATCH_RECOGNIZE` clause (row pattern matching) doesn't parse right now, e.g.: ```sql SELECT * FROM t MATCH_RECOGNIZE (ORDER BY a PATTERN (x+) DEFINE x AS a > 1); ``` this ports the standard-compliant grammar snowflake already has merged (`MatchRecognizeClauseSegment` + `PatternSegment` + the pattern quantifier/operator grammars), wired into trino's `JoinLikeClauseGrammar` hookpoint the same way snowflake wires it in, and adds the one clause trino has that snowflake's implementation doesn't: `SUBSET`, which names a union of pattern variables for use in `DEFINE`/`MEASURES` (verified against the [trino docs](https://trino.io/docs/current/sql/match-recognize.html), it sits between `PATTERN (...)` and `DEFINE`). covers: `PARTITION BY`/`ORDER BY`/`MEASURES` (with `RUNNING`/`FINAL`), `ONE ROW PER MATCH` and `ALL ROWS PER MATCH` with its `SHOW`/`OMIT EMPTY MATCHES`/`WITH UNMATCHED ROWS` variants, `AFTER MATCH SKIP` (all three forms), the `SUBSET` clause, and the `PATTERN` sub-grammar: concatenation, `|` alternation, grouping, `{- -}` exclusion, `PERMUTE(...)`, quantifiers (`* + ? {n} {n,m}` and their reluctant `?`-suffixed forms), and the `^`/`$` anchors. the fixture includes the full worked example from trino's own docs page, verbatim. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? no existing yaml fixtures changed (all 29 trino fixtures regenerated clean, including the SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN ones from an earlier PR). `$` needed its own lexer matcher added (trino had no construct using a bare `$` before this; `^` already had one at the ansi level for bitwise XOR, which is why only `$` needed it). confirmed `$` as a bare token outside `MATCH_RECOGNIZE` still correctly fails to parse, so nothing becomes newly valid elsewhere. ### AI disclosure i used an ai tool (claude code) to help port the grammar from snowflake's existing implementation and write the fixture. what i checked: the trino docs page directly to confirm the grammar (including the `SUBSET` clause snowflake's version doesn't have, and that `{- -}`/`PERMUTE` are genuinely part of trino's syntax, not just copied blindly), the new fixture fails on the unchanged grammar and passes with the change, the full trino dialect suite (87 tests) and trino rule tests (27 tests) pass, and ruff is clean. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Included test cases: parser fixture in `test/fixtures/dialects/trino`, yml generated with `generate_parse_fixture_yml.py` --- ## Summary by cubic Adds parsing support for Trino's `MATCH_RECOGNIZE` clause (row pattern matching), which previously failed to parse. - Implements the clause grammar: `PARTITION BY`, `ORDER BY`, `MEASURES` (`RUNNING`/`FINAL`), both row-per-match modes and their variants, `AFTER MATCH SKIP`, and the Trino-specific `SUBSET` clause. - Implements the `PATTERN` sub-grammar: concatenation, `|` alternation (including concatenation on one side of `|`), `{- -}` exclusion, `PERMUTE`, quantifiers (including reluctant `?` forms), and `^`/`$` anchors. - Pattern variables are their own namespace, so reserved keywords like `END` are valid variable names. - Adds lexer tokens for `$`, `?`, and the `{-`/`-}` exclusion brackets; bare `$` outside the clause still fails to parse. - Adds a fixture with the worked example from the Trino docs plus coverage of the row-per-match variants and skip forms; all existing Trino fixtures parse unchanged. Written for commit 6dbaf6aad71fd051ee94bf894c6e558858a56c47. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: T-SQL: allow bare SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON with no history-table options
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made t-sql's bare `WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON)` on a temporal table doesn't parse right now, e.g.: ```sql CREATE TABLE t ( a int, ValidFrom datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START, ValidTo datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END, PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (ValidFrom, ValidTo) ) WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON); ``` this is the plain, documented form where SQL Server auto-names the history table. it only parsed if you also supplied the bracketed `(HISTORY_TABLE = ..., ...)` sub-options, which are optional in real syntax. `TableOptionSegment`'s `SYSTEM_VERSIONING` branch had the inner `Bracketed(...)` for those sub-options without `optional=True`. the equivalent `ALTER TABLE ... SET (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (...))` branch elsewhere in the same file already has this marked optional, so this just brings the `CREATE TABLE` path in line with it. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? no existing yaml fixtures changed (all 182 t-sql fixtures regenerated clean). the form with explicit `HISTORY_TABLE = ...` still parses exactly as before, the fixture covers both plus a plain `PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME` table with no `WITH` clause at all. ### AI disclosure i used an ai tool (claude code) to help find and fix the grammar bug and write the fixture. what i checked: the new fixture fails on the unchanged grammar and passes with the change, the full t-sql dialect suite (548 tests) and t-sql rule tests (148 tests) pass, and ruff is clean. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Included test cases: parser fixture in `test/fixtures/dialects/tsql`, yml generated with `generate_parse_fixture_yml.py` --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes T-SQL parsing so `CREATE TABLE ... pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made clickhouse's query-level `SAMPLE` clause (e.g. `SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 0.1`) doesn't parse right now. it's left unparsable because the `SamplingExpressionSegment` referenced in `FromExpressionElementSegment` falls back to ansi's `TABLESAMPLE (BERNOULLI|SYSTEM) (n)`, which clickhouse doesn't use. adds a clickhouse-specific `SamplingExpressionSegment` for the real syntax: a bare numeric coefficient, optionally a ratio (`1/10`), and an optional `OFFSET` with the same shape. covers the forms from the [clickhouse docs](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/sql-reference/statements/select/sample): ```sql SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 0.1; SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 1/10; SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 10000; SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 0.1 OFFSET 0.5; SELECT * FROM t FINAL SAMPLE 0.1; ``` ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? no existing yaml fixtures changed (all 63 clickhouse fixtures regenerated clean). the existing `SAMPLE BY ` form inside `ENGINE = MergeTree() ...` (table definition, not a query) is untouched, it's a separate grammar node. ### AI disclosure i used an ai tool (claude code) to help write the grammar and the fixture. what i checked: the new fixture fails on the unchanged grammar and passes with the change, the full clickhouse dialect suite (189 tests) and clickhouse rule tests (20 tests) pass, and ruff is clean. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Included test cases: parser fixture in `test/fixtures/dialects/clickhouse`, yml generated with `generate_parse_fixture_yml.py` --- ## Summary by cubic Parses ClickHouse's query-level `SAMPLE` clause (e.g. `SELECT * FROM t SAMPLE 0.1`) instead of failing to parse it as ANSI's `TABLESAMPLE` syntax. pulls.title: Postgres: support ENFORCED / NOT ENFORCED constraint attribute

None of these parsed with the postgres dialect: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (a int REFERENCES p (id) NOT ENFORCED); CREATE TABLE t (a int, CONSTRAINT chk CHECK (a > 0) NOT ENFORCED); ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (a) REFERENCES p (id) NOT ENFORCED; ALTER TABLE t ALTER CONSTRAINT fk NOT ENFORCED; ``` This accepts the attribute after the existing DEFERRABLE / INITIALLY options on column constraints, table constraints and ALTER CONSTRAINT. `ENFORCED` moves from "not-keyword" to non-reserved, which is how the PG 18 keyword list has it, so it still works as a table or column name. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None that I found. Regenerating fixtures for postgres and the dialects that inherit from it (redshift, greenplum, materialize, duckdb) didn't change any existing file. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `postgres/constraint_enforced.sql`. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. Ran `pytest test/dialects/` (7278 passed), the Rust `fixture_tests` for postgres, and ruff. Made with help from Claude Code. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds support for PostgreSQL 18's ENFORCED / NOT ENFORCED constraint attribute on CHECK and foreign key constraints, both column and table level, and for toggling it via ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT. The postgres dialect previously failed to parse these statements. `ENFORCED` changes from `not-keyword` to `non-reserved`, so it remains usable as a table or column name. Regenerating parse fixtures for postgres and inherited dialects (redshift, greenplum, materialize, duckdb) produced no diff, so no behavior changes are expected.
