pulls.title: MySQL/MariaDB: parse the SOURCE client command
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8564 `SOURCE file_name` and the short form `\. file_name` are mysql/mariadb client commands that run another script. Right now they're unparsable, so any file that pulls in other files this way can't be linted. - `SOURCE` is recognised between statements at the top level of a file, which is where the mysql client recognises it too. The keyword stays unreserved, so `CREATE TABLE source (source INT)` and `SELECT source FROM source` still parse. - The file name isn't quoted and runs to the end of the line (or a `;`). It's matched with gaps disallowed, so it can contain spaces but stops at the newline. - The mysql `FileSegment` makes the delimiter optional after `SOURCE` only. Every other statement still needs one, e.g. `SELECT 1\nSELECT 2;` is still unparsable, same as main. - File name parts get their own type, plus `spacing_within = any` for `source_file_name` in the default config, so LT01/CP rules leave file names alone. - `\.`, `\g` and a lone `\` get small lexer matchers so backslashes can appear in a file name; anywhere else they're a parse error. I didn't lex the whole `SOURCE ...` line as one token. The lexer can't tell where a statement starts, so a column called `source` at the start of a line (`source = 'web'` in a WHERE) would have been swallowed. I followed the psql meta-commands in the postgres dialect and Oracle's `ExecuteFileSegment` instead. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - New `[sqlfluff:layout:type:source_file_name]` section in the default config. (Couldn't call the type `*_path`, since config keys ending in `_path` get resolved as file paths.) - Two things I hit in the Rust side and worked around rather than fixed: - Rust `OneOf` skips leading whitespace/newlines by default and Python's doesn't. Without `allow_gaps=False` the Rust parser carried the file name onto the next line. The Rust fixture parity test caught it. - `utils/build_lexers.py` doesn't escape backslashes in `StringLexer` templates and generates invalid Rust, which is why `\.` uses a `RegexLexer`. Happy to open issues for either. - Not covered: file names containing quotes (`'`, `"`, `` ` ``, they start quoted literals), `$` (doesn't lex), or `#` / `--` / `/*` (lex as comments, so `a--b.sql` won't work). A `;` after a backslash path (`SOURCE C:\db\x.sql;`) is a parse error, as is `\g` in one (`SOURCE C:\games\x.sql`), because the client would run those backslashes as commands. Otherwise backslashes are accepted, e.g. `C:\db\x.sql` and `\\server\share\x.sql` (thanks @rfanth for the patch and for testing it on real servers). ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `mysql/source_statement`, `mariadb/source_statement`. - Other: `test/dialects/mysql_test.py` covers the newline boundary, the delimiter still being required for other statements, invalid forms, and LT01 not respacing file names. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. Ran `pytest test/dialects/` (7257 passed), the LT01/CV06/CP01 yaml rule cases, the Rust `fixture_tests` for mysql and mariadb, ruff and mypy. Regenerating every mysql/mariadb fixture didn't change any existing file. AI-assisted with Claude Code (grammar, tests and the Rust workarounds). The parse trees and the tests above were checked before opening. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8564 by adding parsing support for the MySQL/MariaDB `SOURCE` client command and its short form `\.`, so scripts that include other files can now be linted. `SOURCE` is recognized between statements at the top level, and the file name runs to the end of the line; it may contain spaces, punctuation, and Windows-style backslash paths such as `C:\db\x.sql`, but stops at a newline and cannot include quotes, `$`, or comment markers. The keyword stays unreserved, so `source` remains usable as an identifier. **Behavior changes** - The delimiter after `SOURCE` is optional; other statements still require one before the next statement. - A `;` is not accepted after a file name that contains a backslash, since the client would then run the backslash as a client command. `\g` is likewise not accepted in such file names. - File name parts are typed as `source_file_name`, and a new layout config prevents rules from respacing them. - `\.` required a new lexer matcher, since backslashes otherwise fail to lex. Written for commit 70a2e36f708a47280625844142723810383bb2b5. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(mysql): Make FUNCTION/PROCEDURE parse and indent for MySQL/MariaDB declarations
pulls.body: Previously, FUNCTION/PROCEDURE header parsing failed on a whole lot of real code in the wild because it had only part of the grammar coverage in the server upstream, and where it had coverage, it demanded things in order that the server never required to be in order. Things that are now covered, for instance, IN/INOUT/OUT in functions in MariaDB, the various stanzas on the CREATE statement allowed by both MariaDB and MySQL. This also adds some MariaDB specific things in CREATE EVENT parsing, adds support for AGGREGATE functions, adds MariaDB argument DEFAULTs, and a number of other individually small things that wouldn't parse at all before in procedural code. This closes all of the big parser gaps in #901. The lexer side of #901, #3599, etc. (not fixed here) are fairly easy to work around (`DELIMITER ;;`, requiring quotes on 'user'@'localhost', etc.). Together with #8689 (CASE), this PR makes sqlfluff practical for the first time on most real-world MySQL and MariaDB procedural code. It also is the initial pass for indent in the FUNCTION/PROCEDURE context, building on #8682, making `sqlfluff fix` do something sane in this context for this dialect for the first time, fixing indent on RETURN and SIGNAL as well. It enforces header order and lack thereof just like the respective parser flavors upstream in the servers do. It does not forbid duplicate characteristics because the upstream parser does not either. Duplicates should eventually be noted by a linting rule, but aren't flagged here. It's about 150 lines of actual code, about half of that is doc/comment. None of it is particularly complicated, but there is quite a bit of it and the grammar isn't repetitive. It has reasonable comments and so should be fairly simple to review. The line count is overwhelmingly tests. I've run it against a large local corpus, and on three SQL servers, 2 MySQL 1 MariaDB. P.S. Cubic turned up a small bug that was really an ancient metastatic bug. I patched that at the root, which fixed lots of stuff no one has found yet (previously sqlfluff mysql dialect accepted a user variable wherever a name went). --- Mostly AI generated description below, verified and edited by me, feel free to stop reading here and look at the code if you just want the short version. --- ### What changed Routine headers (`CREATE FUNCTION` / `CREATE PROCEDURE`), both MySQL and MariaDB dialects: - Characteristics come in any order and may repeat, as on the server (`sp_c_chistics`). `COMMENT` is one of them, so it can go anywhere. A function no longer needs `DETERMINISTIC`. - `CREATE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS`, as procedures already had. - Parameter, `RETURNS` and `DECLARE` types can carry `CHARACTER SET` and `COLLATE` (`type opt_collate` on the server). - The parameter list is required (even empty), and each parameter needs a name. MariaDB only: - `IN` / `OUT` / `INOUT` on function parameters. MySQL allows a direction on procedure parameters only, so the mysql dialect is unchanged there. - `OR REPLACE` comes straight after `CREATE`, before `DEFINER`. The dialect had these swapped for functions and procedures. `CREATE OR REPLACE EVENT` added. - Parameter defaults: `name type DEFAULT expr`, on procedures and functions. - `CREATE AGGREGATE FUNCTION` and `FETCH GROUP NEXT ROW`. - `DEFINER = CURRENT_ROLE` / `CURRENT_ROLE()`, as MariaDB has some other places where it's user or role (GRANT/REVOKE/SHOW GRANTS, but that's beyond the scope of this PR), and some places where it's just user like `CREATE/DROP/KILL USER` and just a role like `CREATE ROLE`. MySQL roles are just user accounts. Routine body layout, building on #8682: - A value on the line after `RETURN` is indented, like a `WHERE` condition. - The `SET` clause of `SIGNAL` / `RESIGNAL` is indented when on its own line. - A cursor's query is indented under `DECLARE ... CURSOR FOR`, like a handler's statement. Only a query is accepted there, as on the server. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - Two tree changes: `comment_clause` now sits inside `characteristic_statement` (`function_comment` fixtures), and a cursor's query no longer has a `statement` wrapper (`declare_cursor` fixtures). - Now rejected, as on the servers: a parameter without a name, a routine without brackets, a cursor over a non-query (`CURSOR FOR DELETE ...`). - MariaDB function parameters no longer accept `ANY TYPE` (BigQuery syntax, inherited from ansi; never valid in MariaDB). Not covered: unquoted account hosts (`DEFINER = u@localhost`, a lexer issue) and MySQL 9's JavaScript routines. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - Parse fixtures for characteristics (single, any order, repeated), header order, parameter types, and MariaDB parameter modes and defaults. - `LT02-indent-mysql.yml`: parameter lists, labelled bodies, `RETURN`, `SIGNAL`, cursor queries. - `mysql_test.py` / `mariadb_test.py`: invalid headers are rejected. All of it was checked on MySQL 8.4 and 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8. ### AI assistance disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md. AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5); I reviewed the grammar, the layout and every test case. --- ## Summary by cubic Reworks MySQL and MariaDB routine header parsing and layout so real-world `CREATE FUNCTION`/`CREATE PROCEDURE` code parses correctly and `sqlfluff fix` indents routine bodies sensibly. - Characteristics (DETERMINISTIC, COMMENT, SQL SECURITY, etc.) can now appear in any order, any number, and are optional; previously they demanded a fixed order and functions had to be DETERMINISTIC. - Function headers now support `IF NOT EXISTS`, require the parameter list (even empty) and named parameters, and accept `CHARACTER SET`/`COLLATE` on parameter, return, and local variable types. - `RETURN` values, `SIGNAL`/`RESIGNAL` SET clauses, and cursor queries (including `VALUES`) are indented when placed on their own lines. **MariaDB-specific additions** - Function parameters accept `IN`/`OUT`/`INOUT` and default values; MySQL remains unchanged (directions stay procedure-only there). - `OR REPLACE` now comes before `DEFINER` for functions, procedures, and events; `CREATE AGGREGATE FUNCTION` and `FETCH GROUP NEXT ROW` are supported; `DEFINER = CURRENT_ROLE` (with or without brackets) is accepted. **Behavior changes** - User variables (`@x`) are no longer accepted as names (labels, collations, character sets, cursor names); `LOAD DATA` names them explicitly in its column list, and `SELECT @x` now parses the variable itself rather than as a column. - Two parse tree changes: `comment_clause` now nests inside `characteristic_statement`, and cursor queries are no longer wrapped in a `statement` segment. - Now rejected, matching server behavior: unnamed parameters, routines without brackets, cursors over non-queries, and MariaDB function parameters using BigQuery's `ANY TYPE`. Written for commit 454e2b77f0813b73763a03457dfde4435173a4bc. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(snowflake): indent scripting CASE WHEN/ELSE branches (LT02)
pulls.body: ### Summary In the Snowflake dialect, LT02 indentation for a scripting `CASE` statement is inverted: it expects (and `sqlfluff fix` enforces) the `WHEN`/`ELSE` branches at the **same** column as `CASE`, which is the opposite of correct and contradicts the dialect's own fixture. Fixes #8690. ### Root cause `ScriptingCaseStatementSegment` (`src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_snowflake.py`) placed `Indent`/`Dedent` only around each `THEN` body — there was **no `Indent` wrapping the branch list itself**. So `WHEN`, `ELSE`, and `END` stayed at the `CASE` column. Sibling constructs (`IF`, `WHILE`, `FOR`, the ANSI `CASE` expression) all wrap their branch block in an indent; this one was missing it. ### Fix Two meta placements: `Indent` after the optional case value, and `Dedent` immediately before `END`. Now `WHEN`/`ELSE` sit one level below `CASE`, their bodies two levels, and `END [CASE]` returns to the `CASE` column — matching the fixture. No reflow/core changes. ### Verification - Reporter's SQL: `lint` now clean (was 4 LT02 flags); `fix` is a no-op (was pulling `WHEN`/`ELSE` to `CASE`'s column). - `test/fixtures/dialects/snowflake/scripting_control_flow.sql`: **22 LT02 violations → 0**. - Added 3 cases to `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/LT02-indent.yml` (value form pass, searched form pass, fail→fix). - `pytest test/rules/ -k LT02`: 259 passed. Snowflake dialect parse tests: 750 passed. `ruff` clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes Snowflake Scripting `CASE` indentation so LT02 correctly expects `WHEN`/`ELSE` branches one level below `CASE` instead of at the same column (fixes #8690). **Root cause and fix** `ScriptingCaseStatementSegment` wrapped only the `THEN` bodies in `Indent`/`Dedent`, leaving `WHEN`, `ELSE`, and `END` at the `CASE` column — contradicting the dialect's own fixture and sibling constructs (`IF`, `WHILE`, `FOR`, ANSI `CASE`). Added an `Indent` after the optional case value and a `Dedent` before `END` so the branches indent one level below `CASE`, their bodies two levels below, and `END [CASE]` returns to the `CASE` column. `sqlfluff fix` is now a no-op on correctly-formatted code (previously it pulled `WHEN`/`ELSE` back to `CASE`'s column), and the dialect fixture drops from 22 LT02 violations to 0. Adds pass and fail→fix test cases for both the valued and searched `CASE` forms. Written for commit 9a225fe8fa95099a24213c0c5a1a8a6ed5d7fcbc. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(mysql): parse CASE statements
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made This is actually a small commit, it's ~+80 of code which is about half comments and many fixtures. The code is simple. Right now CASE statements (as distinct from CASE expressions) are not parsable at all in the MySQL dialect. This PR fixes that. It's written to be lint rule friendly with `when_clause` `else_clause` branches. It has a lot of tests but needs them because I want block context to continue to work going forward with the various CASE forms. Restricting where CASE and similar procedural statements may appear is planned for a future PR covering the whole topic. Text below is mostly AI, reviewed and edited by me, feel free to stop reading if you just want the short version, but I think it helps. I've instructed my bot to be less wordy. - Both forms are separate alternatives, like MySQL's grammar ([sql_yacc.yy](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/008e09c2834b/sql/sql_yacc.yy#L5349)) and ansi's `CASE` expression: simple (`CASE v WHEN 1 ...`) and searched (`CASE WHEN v > 1 ...`). - Each branch is a `when_clause` or `else_clause` holding a `statement_list`. Those are the `CASE` expression's types, so a rule can handle both. ST01, ST02 and ST04 only look inside `case_expression`, so they don't touch these. - Layout is the same as the `CASE` expression: `WHEN` and `ELSE` indented under `CASE`, statements one level further, `END CASE` level with `CASE`. This is fully consistent with what's in every other dialect, except snowflake which is clearly broken, but I'm filing a bug report for that. - `CASE v WHEN v > 2` is valid on the servers (it compares `v` with `v > 2`), so the grammar accepts it too. Catching that is a job for a rule. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None. The grammar is new and existing fixtures are unchanged. The `CASE` expression is untouched. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - Parse fixtures for both forms: several branches, with and without `ELSE`, blocks and loops inside branches, and a MariaDB fixture. - `LT02-indent-mysql.yml`: layout of both forms. - `mysql_test.py`: invalid forms are rejected (empty branch, no `WHEN`, plain `END`), in both forms. All of it was checked on MySQL 8.4 and 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8. ### AI assistance disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md. AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5); I reviewed the grammar, the layout and every test case. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds parsing support for MySQL `CASE ... END CASE` procedural statements, which previously made routines containing them unparsable. - Supports both simple and searched forms, matching MySQL's grammar and the `CASE` expression. - Branches reuse the `when_clause` and `else_clause` types, so rules can treat statements and expressions alike. - Applies the same layout as the `CASE` expression for LT02: `WHEN` and `ELSE` indented under `CASE`, statements one level further. - Adds parse fixtures for MySQL and MariaDB (including nested, blocks, loops, and mixed-value cases) and negative tests rejecting invalid syntax. Written for commit d3de3ac1df9614603f5f4a7a9d2ae427bcd723c2. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: [MRG] Fix LT05 long ORDER BY lines ending with semicolons
pulls.body: Fixes #8685. LT05 treated the dedent immediately before a final statement terminator as the best rebreak point. That only moved the semicolon and left the overlong line unchanged. Ignore that ineffective break point so LT05 can split the line at its commas. Added an autofix regression fixture for a long `ORDER BY` line ending in a semicolon. Validation: targeted autofix fixture passed; Ruff passed. **AI assistance disclosure:** OpenAI Codex assisted with the implementation and regression fixture. I manually reproduced the issue and ran the targeted autofix test and Ruff check. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes LT05 so long lines ending with semicolons are split at their commas instead of having only the semicolon moved. LT05 previously treated the dedent before a final statement terminator as the best rebreak point, which left the overlong line unchanged. The reflow logic now ignores that ineffective break point, so the line splits at its commas. Added autofix regression fixtures for a long `ORDER BY` line ending in a semicolon, including a case with no final newline. The no-newline fixtures are excluded from end-of-file-fixer in .pre-commit-config.yaml; trailing-whitespace still checks them. .editorconfig preserves their missing final newline in editors. Written for commit 406047ee1d17b5b997d57b32ecf88c93fb6579e2. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(LT05): wrap long ORDER BY lines ending in semicolons
pulls.body: Fixes #8685. LT05 reports an otherwise breakable ORDER BY line as unfixable when it ends with a semicolon. The closing dedent selects a break level that cannot produce a fix because the semicolon must stay on the preceding line. Ignore levels containing only these unusable points so the existing comma-wrapping logic can run. Preserve the semicolon and existing trailing-newline behavior. Validation run by the AI agent: the four ANSI/TSQL semicolon regressions failed before the fix; all eight semicolon/no-semicolon and trailing-newline cases pass after it, including a second fix and a clean LT05 lint. All 76 existing LT05 cases and four new ANSI/TSQL fixtures covering one-per-line and fill wrapping also pass. The reflow and rules suite passed (2,895 passed, 101 skipped), and all eight pre-commit hooks passed. The full CPU suite is still running; other Python versions, Rust, dbt integrations and hosted CI have not been tested. AI assistance was used to investigate the bug, implement the change, write tests, execute the checks above and draft this description. The contributor reviewed and approved this description before submission; the tests above were executed by the AI agent, not personally run by the contributor. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8685, where LT05 reported a long `ORDER BY` line as unfixable when it ended with a semicolon. The reflow logic now ignores break points that cannot shorten the line (dedents before semicolons), so comma-based wrapping runs as it does without a semicolon; the semicolon and trailing newline are preserved. - Added ANSI and TSQL fixtures for one-per-line and fill wrapping, plus parametrized tests covering semicolon and trailing-newline combinations. Written for commit f51684abb9b462d7ed6c85fcb3fd04653e95c145. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(mysql): indent procedural bodies, conditions and assignment lists
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made **Size note** - this is only +55/-49 of grammar (and even that's the same moves repeated over similar constructs) with minor fixture changes which look big due to indent level making a line appear to change, and some tests. Follow-up to #8531, where @keraion asked for `Indent`/`Dedent` in the `BEGIN ... END` body. The other bodies and lists had the same indent gap, and I also [said in #8531](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/pull/8531#discussion_r4057742788) that I would unify some similar constructs (which makes sense as the MySQL/MariaDB parser source does too). After looking at the recent `IF` improvements (#8380), it makes sense to do it as a segment (`statement_list`) rather than a grammar because `IF` already needs a node per branch to mark where each branch ends. As such, this fixes them all together, following one rule: - **A nested statement is indented under its header.** A `BEGIN ... END` block keeps `BEGIN` and `END` at the header's level and indents its own contents; a body written as a single statement is indented under the header. - **A statement's own list of assignments or actions is indented,** as `UPDATE ... SET` already is. - **A condition that runs onto more lines is indented,** as a `WHERE` clause's is. - **A query that is a statement's payload stays flat,** as `INSERT ... SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` already do. `CREATE VIEW ... AS SELECT` is unchanged. Changes, all in `dialect_mysql.py` (MariaDB inherits them): - `BEGIN ... END`, `WHILE`, `LOOP` and `REPEAT` bodies are indented. For `REPEAT`, `UNTIL` lines up with `REPEAT`. - `IF`, `ELSEIF`, `WHILE` and `UNTIL` conditions take an implicit indent, as `WHERE` and `CASE WHEN` do. Until now a multi-line condition was flattened to the keyword's level. By default `fix` now puts a line break after the keyword; with `implicit_indents = allow` the condition may start on the keyword's line and continue indented. `THEN` or `DO` may also go on its own line at the keyword's level. - Routine, trigger and event (`CREATE`/`ALTER EVENT ... DO`) bodies and handler actions use a new `ProceduralBodyGrammar`: a `BEGIN ... END` block, or a single statement indented under the header. - `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` assignments and the `ALTER TABLE` action list are indented. SparkSQL and Databricks already indent their `ALTER TABLE` actions. - The statements inside a block, loop or `IF` branch are one `StatementListSegment` (`statement_list`), placed between each construct's `Indent`/`Dedent` as `IF` already did. Both servers' grammars use one rule for all of them, `sp_proc_stmts1` (one or more statements), except that a `BEGIN ... END` block may be empty, `sp_proc_stmts` ([MySQL](https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/blob/008e09c2834b/sql/sql_yacc.yy#L4112-L4120), [MariaDB](https://github.com/MariaDB/server/blob/f21444cd039e/sql/sql_yacc.yy#L3409-L3417)), so there the list is optional. `CASE` branches and MariaDB's `FOR` loop use the same rule. This replaces `IfStatementListSegment` (#8380) and the inline block and loop lists. The `IF` list differed only in its node type, which no rule or other code refers to, and in requiring a statement, which the shared list keeps. The old lists also excluded their closing words (`END`, `UNTIL`, `ELSEIF`, `ELSE`). That was an oversight in more than one prior PR, including my own #8531: none of these words can start a statement, so the list ends there anyway, as on the server. They are reserved, and since each list item needs a delimiter, `END IF` never parsed as a statement even while the transaction grammar still had a standalone `END` (removed in #8531). The order of `ELSEIF` and `ELSE` was never the list's job: `IfExpressionStatement` enforces it, and #8380's invalid-`IF` tests all still pass. Until now LT02 flattened every MySQL routine body to the start of the line, so `sqlfluff fix` removed the indentation people write. On a large codebase, broken LT02 violations are mostly fixed with this change. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - `sqlfluff fix` with LT02 now indents these bodies and lists instead of flattening them. One-line forms (`DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND SET done = 1;`, `... FOR EACH ROW SET NEW.a = 1;`) are unaffected. - `WHILE`, `LOOP` and `REPEAT` bodies must now contain a statement, as on the server (they inherit the `IF` list's rule); main accepted them empty. New tests in `mysql_test.py` cover all three and an empty `IF` branch. - Parse trees, two changes, 87 regenerated fixtures: - the statements in every block, loop and `IF` branch now sit in a `statement_list` node (`IF` branches: renamed from `if_statement_list`); - a `BEGIN ... END` used as a handler action or an event body no longer has a `statement` wrapper, giving it the same shape as a routine or trigger body (`compound_statement` directly under the parent). Indents themselves change no fixture, as parse fixtures do not record them. #### Where this is going `ProceduralBodyGrammar` names the one rule every body slot follows, so the five slots cannot drift apart. A procedural `CASE` statement is next; it will use `StatementListSegment` for its branches rather than adding another list type. After that: separating procedural statements (blocks, flow control, cursor statements) from ordinary ones. They are only valid inside a stored program (and, for MariaDB, `BEGIN NOT ATOMIC` and a few others at top level), but are currently accepted anywhere a statement is. That includes `DECLARE`, which the server accepts only at the start of a block (`BEGIN sp_decls sp_proc_stmts END`), so it will become the block's declarations section rather than a statement. The split also resolves the one remaining difference here: a block used as a body is bare, while a loop used as a body still sits in a `statement`. I'm not planning to stop until MySQL/MariaDB dialect is actually good for procedural code, and there's lots more to do. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`: a new `LT02-indent-mysql.yml` with a fail/fix case for each construct, a MariaDB case, multi-line conditions under both the default and `implicit_indents: allow`, and pass cases showing that `BEGIN` stays at the header's level, `THEN`/`DO` may take their own line, and one-line forms are untouched. Every statement in these cases (before and after the fix) runs on live MySQL 8.4 and 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8 servers (the `mariadb` case on MariaDB only), and the four empty-body tests in `mysql_test.py` are syntax errors (1064) on all three. An empty `BEGIN ... END` is accepted on all three. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: the new grammar says what it accepts and why. ### AI assistance disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md. The grammar change, the test cases and the test runs were AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5). Manually validated by me: the diff, the indentation rule above, and every test case's expected output. Checks run locally: full test suite, all pre-commit hooks, and `lint-imports`. Fixture regeneration for mysql and mariadb reproduces every `.yml` in this branch. pulls.title: Postgres: keep VARIADIC outside the typed array literal
pulls.body: `sqlfluff fix` with LT01 turned `f(VARIADIC ARRAY[1, 2])` into `f(VARIADICARRAY[1, 2])` on postgres (and the dialects derived from it). The postgres override of `TypedArrayLiteralSegment` inserted an optional `VARIADIC [name :=]` prefix inside the segment, so the `spacing_within = touch` layout for `typed_array_literal` also applied at the `VARIADIC` / `ARRAY` boundary and the space was removed. The call-site `VARIADIC` keyword is already handled by `FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar`, which accepts `VARIADIC `, so the override is redundant. Drop it so `typed_array_literal` covers exactly `ARRAY` + `[...]` again, with `VARIADIC` as a sibling keyword in the function contents. The `arr := ARRAY[...]` form now parses as a `named_argument`, consistent with the `=>` and `=` forms. pulls.title: Snowflake: parse CREATE STORAGE LIFECYCLE POLICY
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes #8678.

`CREATE STORAGE LIFECYCLE POLICY` was not in the Snowflake dialect, so the
statement from the issue is reported as an unparsable section. This adds it,
following the grammar in
https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-storage-lifecycle-policy:

```
CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] STORAGE LIFECYCLE POLICY [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <name>
  AS ( <arg_name> <arg_type> [ , ... ] )
  RETURNS BOOLEAN -> <body>
  [ ARCHIVE_TIER = { COOL | COLD } ]
  [ ARCHIVE_FOR_DAYS = <number_of_days> ]
  [ COMMENT = '<string_literal>' ]
  [ [ WITH ] TAG ( <tag_name> = '<tag_value>' [ , ... ] ) ]
```

The new `CreateStorageLifecyclePolicyStatementSegment` is modelled on the
existing `CreateRowAccessPolicyStatementSegment`, which has the same
`AS (<params>) RETURNS BOOLEAN -> <body>` shape, plus the four trailing option
clauses matched with `AnySetOf`, so they can appear in any order but each at
most once.

Four keywords were missing from `dialect_snowflake_keywords.py` and are added to
the unreserved list in alphabetical order: `ARCHIVE_FOR_DAYS`, `ARCHIVE_TIER`,
`COLD`, `COOL`. `STORAGE`, `LIFECYCLE`, `POLICY` and `BOOLEAN` were already there.

One detail worth flagging: the `TAG` clause here is **bracketed**, so this uses
the existing `TagBracketedEqualsSegment` rather than `TagEqualsSegment` (which
matches the unbracketed `TAG t = 'v'` form used elsewhere). Using the unbracketed
one parses the minimal statement fine but fails on every `TAG (...)` case, so it
is worth being explicit about.

## Tests

New fixture `test/fixtures/dialects/snowflake/create_storage_lifecycle_policy.sql`
with six statements: the full form from the issue; the example from the docs,
whose body is a compound expression with an `EXISTS` subquery; an `OR REPLACE` +
quoted-identifier + `WITH TAG` form; an `IF NOT EXISTS` minimal form; a bare
`TAG (...)` without `WITH`; and a schema-qualified policy name. `OR REPLACE` and
`IF NOT EXISTS` are covered in separate statements because the docs state they
are mutually exclusive.

`test/dialects/dialects_test.py` also asserts that each option clause may appear
at most once, following the pattern in #8658.

## Verification

- `pytest test/dialects/ -k snowflake` — 768 passed
- `pytest test/` — **11540 passed, 8 failed**. The same 8 fail on a clean `main`
  checkout in my environment: 3 in `test/core/plugin_test.py` and 5 in
  `test/diff_quality_plugin_test.py`, because I used a plain venv rather than the
  `tox -e dbt180 --devenv` flow, so `plugins/sqlfluff-plugin-example` is not
  installed. **0 new failures.** dbt tests were deselected with `-m "not dbt"`.
- Mutation check: removing the `StatementSegment` registration line fails the new
  fixture (3 failed), so the fixture genuinely depends on the new segment.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` — clean
- Checked by hand against the parse tree that every optional clause in the
  documented grammar parses, individually and combined: `OR REPLACE`,
  `IF NOT EXISTS`, quoted identifier, multiple parameters, `ARCHIVE_TIER = COOL`,
  `ARCHIVE_TIER = COLD`, `ARCHIVE_FOR_DAYS`, `COMMENT`, `TAG (...)`,
  `WITH TAG (...)`, all options together, and a multi-expression body.
- Also checked that invalid input is still rejected rather than silently
  accepted: a missing `RETURNS`, `ARCHIVE_TIER = WARM`, and `RETURNS STRING` all
  still produce an unparsable section.

## Changes since review

- `AnySetOf` instead of `AnyNumberOf`, and the redundant optional `WITH` dropped,
  per review. Repeated options are now rejected, with cases in `dialects_test.py`.
- The mutually exclusive `OR REPLACE` / `IF NOT EXISTS` fixture statement split.
- The docs example added.
- Policy names accept the qualified form via `ObjectReferenceSegment`, and the
  fixture yml was regenerated for the resulting parse-tree change — the stale
  snapshot was what `ymlchecks` was failing on.

## AI assistance

Per the AI-assisted contributions section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`: this change was
developed with AI assistance. AI-assisted: finding the closest existing segment
to model on, drafting the grammar, the keyword additions, the fixture and this
description. Manually validated: every case in the two Verification bullets above
was run through the parser on this branch and its parse tree inspected; the
bracketed-vs-unbracketed `TAG` problem was found that way rather than assumed,
and the mutation check and lint commands were run as listed.

pulls.title: fix(AM09): flag LIMIT/OFFSET without ORDER BY on set expressions (UNION/etc.)
pulls.body: ### Summary **AM09** (`ambiguous.order_by_limit`) misses `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` without `ORDER BY` when it's applied to a **set expression** (`UNION`/`INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT`). The rule flags the plain-SELECT case but silently passes the equivalent set-expression case, even though it's exactly as non-deterministic. ### Example (on `main`) ```sql SELECT a FROM foo UNION ALL SELECT a FROM bar LIMIT 10; ``` → **no AM09 violation**, whereas `SELECT a FROM foo LIMIT 10;` (same determinism problem) **is** flagged. Inconsistent. ### Root cause `src/sqlfluff/rules/ambiguous/AM09.py` crawls only `select_statement`: ```python crawl_behaviour = SegmentSeekerCrawler({"select_statement"}) ``` A set-level `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` (and its `ORDER BY`) attaches to the enclosing `set_expression`, not to any inner `SELECT`, so the crawler never visits it. The existing `_eval` child-lookup already works for `set_expression` unchanged. ### Fix Add `set_expression` to the crawler and the type guard — one spot, no change to the detection logic: ```python crawl_behaviour = SegmentSeekerCrawler({"select_statement", "set_expression"}) ... if not segment.is_type("select_statement", "set_expression"): return None ``` ### Tests `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/AM09.yml`: a failing `UNION ALL … LIMIT 10` (no `ORDER BY`) case and a passing `UNION ALL … ORDER BY a LIMIT 10` case (confirms no new false positive). Full rule suite: 2739 passed, 0 failed; `AM09.py` stays at 100% coverage; `ruff`/`mypy` clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the `AM09` rule (`ambiguous.order_by_limit`) so it also flags `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` without `ORDER BY` applied to set expressions (`UNION`/`INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT`), not just plain `SELECT` statements. - The rule previously only crawled `select_statement` segments, so set-level clauses that attach to the enclosing `set_expression` were silently missed. - Detection logic is unchanged; the crawler and type guard now also visit `set_expression`. - Adds test cases covering both the failing `LIMIT`-without-`ORDER BY` case and the passing equivalent with `ORDER BY` to guard against false positives. Written for commit a48f01f1666f50ce9d6aefc2397676c2c9be39d4. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: DuckDB: Support ATTACH, DETACH and SUMMARIZE statements
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Adds DuckDB parser support for: - [`ATTACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/statements/attach): `ATTACH [OR REPLACE | IF NOT EXISTS] [DATABASE] 'path' [AS alias] [(option [value], ...)]`. Options are free-form, because extensions define their own (`TYPE sqlite`, `READ_ONLY`, ...). - [`DETACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/statements/attach#detach): `DETACH [DATABASE [IF EXISTS]] alias`. - [`SUMMARIZE`](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/guides/meta/summarize): followed by a query, or by an optional `TABLE` and a table name or quoted file/URL. `SUMMARIZE` is added as an unreserved keyword. `ATTACH DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` and `DETACH IF EXISTS` (without `DATABASE`) are not accepted, matching DuckDB itself, which rejects them. New fixtures: `duckdb/attach`, `duckdb/detach` and `duckdb/summarize`. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None expected. No existing fixtures changed. `SUMMARIZE` used as a subquery (`FROM (SUMMARIZE t)`) is not covered here. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`. The new statements failed to parse on `main`. With this change, `pytest test/dialects` passes, as do `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy -p sqlfluff`, `yamllint` and `codespell`. `sqlfluff lint` reports no parse errors on the new fixtures. ### AI assistance The grammar changes and fixtures were drafted with an AI coding assistant. I reviewed the changes, verified the statements against the official docs and DuckDB 1.5.6's own parser, and ran the dialect parse tests and linters listed above locally. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds DuckDB parser support for `ATTACH`, `DETACH`, and `SUMMARIZE` statements, which previously failed to parse. - `ATTACH` accepts `OR REPLACE`/`IF NOT EXISTS`, an optional `DATABASE`, an alias, and free-form bracketed options because extensions define their own. - `DETACH` supports an optional `DATABASE` keyword and `IF EXISTS`. - `SUMMARIZE` is now an unreserved keyword and accepts a table reference, a quoted file or URL, or a query. - `ATTACH DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` and `DETACH IF EXISTS` without `DATABASE` remain unparsed, matching DuckDB's own parser. - Adds parse fixtures for all three statements; no existing fixtures changed. Written for commit 51c059749ff9966b23b2b219084bc221711b83c6. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Honor inline dialect directives when loading SQL files
pulls.body:
### Brief summary of the change made

SQL files that specify their dialect using an inline `-- sqlfluff:dialect:...` directive currently fail before the file is read when no dialect is configured elsewhere. Defer dialect validation until the rendering pipeline has processed the file's directives. This enables `parse`, `lint`, `render`, `format` and `fix`, while files with no dialect still produce the existing user error.

Makes progress on #7114: this addresses inline dialect selection only. Per-file templater switching is outside this change.

### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of?

Dialect validation remains in `render_string()` before templating. Regression tests use T-SQL-specific syntax and cover all five file commands, both with and without an inline dialect.

### Validation

- Full Python 3.12 suite: 11,489 passed, 2,636 skipped. External database/plugin matrices were not run locally.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed, including pinned mypy, Ruff, formatting, YAML and spelling checks.

pulls.title: perf(rust): only probe `greedy_match` terminators where their hint hits
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made This improves performance on terminator parsing. TPC-H parse 33.8ms -> 26.0ms (-23%), TPC-DS 369ms -> 301ms (-18%), peak memory -15%. Additionally brings Python parity between terminators and brackets order - fixes #8612 ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up `greedy_match` terminator scanning in the Rust parser by probing only terminators whose simple hint can match the current token, and fetching grammar tables once per call, instead of probing every terminator at every position. This cuts TPC-H parsing from 33.8ms to 26.0ms (-23%), TPC-DS from 369ms to 301ms (-18%), and peak memory by 15%, while also restoring Python parity on terminator-versus-bracket ordering. **Bug Fixes** - Terminators are now checked before brackets, so a `(` terminator wins over bracket skipping. - Fixes #8612: a block comment piece that is exactly `)` no longer ends the search early. Written for commit 578772b308f0c27e1f3a582ae19efd3f6db0e749. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: SQLite: Parse multiple ON CONFLICT clauses in INSERT
pulls.body:
### Brief summary of the change made

SQLite allows multiple `ON CONFLICT` clauses in one INSERT, but SQLFluff reports a parse error at the second clause. For example:

```sql
INSERT INTO t1 (a, b) VALUES (1, 2)
ON CONFLICT (a) DO UPDATE SET b = excluded.b
ON CONFLICT (b) DO NOTHING;
```

Allow repeated targeted UPSERT clauses after both VALUES and SELECT, followed by at most one final targetless clause. Add SQL/YAML fixtures covering multiple targets, a conditional update, a final targetless clause, and RETURNING.

Reference: [SQLite UPSERT documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_upsert.html). Multiple clauses have been supported since SQLite 3.35.0.

### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of?

This changes only SQLite INSERT parsing. Existing zero- and single-clause inserts remain covered by the dialect fixtures.

### Validation

pulls.title: Add an RF06 case for a case-sensitive quoted alias in Oracle
pulls.body: ## Summary Closes #3704. The reported false positive no longer happens on `main`: ```sql SELECT col AS "renamedCol" FROM mytable -- RF06 passes ``` (The `PRS` violation in the issue's output is from its `FROM table`, `table` being reserved — unrelated to RF06.) RF06 has no Oracle case at all today, so nothing pins it. Oracle casefolds to upper (`dialect_oracle.py`, `casefold=str.upper`), which makes the behaviour worth having a test for: a quoted alias that is *not* already uppercase cannot be unquoted without changing the identifier, so RF06 must leave it alone, while an all-uppercase one is genuinely redundant quoting and should still be flagged. Adds both halves to `RF06.yml`: | Alias | Expected | |---|---| | `"renamedCol"` | pass — mixed case, must stay quoted | | `"renamed_col"` | pass — lower case, must stay quoted | | `"RENAMEDCOL"` | fail, fixed to `RENAMEDCOL` — redundant quoting | No production code changes. ## Verification - `pytest test/rules/ -k RF06` — green - `pytest test/rules/` — green - Each row of the table above was checked against `sqlfluff lint --dialect oracle --rules RF06` on this checkout before being written as a test. - Mutation check: changing the `"renamedCol"` case to `fail_str` fails, and changing the `"RENAMEDCOL"` case to `pass_str` fails — so both directions are actually asserted. ## AI assistance Per the AI-assisted contributions section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`: this change was developed with AI assistance. AI-assisted: re-testing the issue against `main`, working out that the issue's `PRS` output came from its reserved-word table name, checking RF06 for existing Oracle coverage, and drafting the cases and this description. Manually validated: every row of the table was produced by running the linter on this checkout, and the test and mutation commands above were run on this branch. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds Oracle test cases for RF06, pinning down that case-sensitive quoted aliases are left alone while redundant uppercase quoting is still flagged. Closes #3704. The reported false positive no longer occurs on main, but RF06 had no Oracle coverage. Since Oracle casefolds to uppercase, unquoting `"renamedCol"` or `"renamed_col"` would change the identifier, so both pass; `"RENAMEDCOL"` is redundantly quoted and fails, with the fix removing the quotes. No production code changes. Written for commit f834a636b5140efd869bfe857533b26b88cf51fa. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(bigquery): don't parse a column named like a datetime unit as a date part
pulls.body: ## Summary Fixes #5015. In BigQuery, a column whose name happens to be a datetime unit (`year`, `day`, `month`, …) is parsed as a `date_part` rather than a `column_reference` whenever it appears in a function call that takes **two or more** arguments: ```sql SELECT my_udf(year, 1) FROM t -- year -> date_part SELECT my_udf(year) FROM t -- year -> column_reference (correct) ``` The function name is irrelevant — the issue reports `REGEXP_EXTRACT`, but a plain UDF reproduces it just as well, and `my_udf(day, month)` turns both arguments into date parts. Because the segment is then typed as a keyword, `CP01` reports it and `sqlfluff fix` rewrites the user's column name, so this silently changes queries rather than just mis-reporting them. ## Root cause `FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar` is only reached through `Delimited(Ref("FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar"))` in ANSI's `FunctionContentsGrammar`; a sole argument matches the bare `Ref("ExpressionSegment")` branch earlier in that `AnyNumberOf`, which is why the single-argument form is correct today. `dialect_bigquery.py` overrides that grammar with `Ref("DatetimeUnitSegment")` first in the `OneOf`, so with two or more arguments every argument is tried as a datetime unit before being tried as an expression. That entry is redundant for BigQuery: the functions that legitimately take a bare date part are matched through `DateTimeFunctionContentsSegment`, which is gated on the `date_part_function_name` set (`DATE_TRUNC`, `DATE_DIFF`, `EXTRACT`, `TIMESTAMP_TRUNC`, …) and is a separate branch of `FunctionContentsSegment`. Removing the unconditional alternative leaves those paths untouched. ## Scope BigQuery only. `dialect_snowflake.py` has the same `DatetimeUnitSegment` entry and reproduces the same misparse, but Snowflake has no equivalent gated date-part path (`DATEADD(year, 1, d)` relies on this alternative), so removing it there would be a different and larger change. I've left Snowflake alone rather than bundle it in. ## Behaviour change A datetime-unit word used as one of several function arguments is now a column reference, so `CP01` no longer reports it and `fix` no longer rewrites it. Date parts in the gated date-part functions are unaffected. Two existing fixtures change, and the second one needs a decision from you: - `bigquery/parameters.yml` — `parse_date("%Y%m", year)` now records `column_reference: year` instead of `date_part: year`. The `.sql` line already carried the comment `-- this should parse year as an identifier`, so this is the fixture catching up with its own stated expectation. - `bigquery/select_safe_function.yml` — `SAFE.DATEADD(DAY, -2, CURRENT_DATE)` now records `DAY` as a column reference. `DATEADD` is in the gated set, but `DatePartFunctionNameSegment` matches an unqualified name, so the `SAFE.`-prefixed form takes the generic path. I have deliberately **not** judged whether `SAFE.DATEADD(DAY, ...)` is valid BigQuery (`DATEADD` is not in BigQuery's documented function list, and `SAFE.` applies only to certain functions), nor extended the gated branch to accept a qualified name — both felt like decisions for you rather than for this change. Happy to do either if you'd prefer. ## Tests `parameters.sql` already contained the reported shape with a comment stating the expected result; its `.yml` now matches that comment. I've added a case to the same file for the general form, so it is clear the behaviour does not depend on the function name: ```sql select my_udf(year, 1), my_udf(day, month) from t; ``` Two existing fixture `.yml` files change as a result — see Behaviour change. ## Verification - `pytest test/dialects/ -k bigquery` — 452 passed - `pytest test/` — **11471 passed, 8 failed**. The same 8 fail on a clean `main` checkout in my environment: 3 in `test/core/plugin_test.py` and 5 in `test/diff_quality_plugin_test.py`, because I used a plain venv rather than the `tox -e dbt180 --devenv` flow and so `plugins/sqlfluff-plugin-example` is not installed. **0 new failures.** dbt tests were deselected with `-m "not dbt"`. - Mutation check: restoring the removed `Ref("DatetimeUnitSegment")` line makes the regenerated fixtures fail again. - Checked by hand against the parse tree that the gated date-part functions still produce `date_part`: `DATE_TRUNC(d, YEAR)`, `DATE_DIFF(a, b, DAY)`, `EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d)`, `TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(ts, HOUR)`, `DATE_TRUNC(d, ISOWEEK)`, and that unqualified `DATEADD(DAY, -2, CURRENT_DATE)` still does. ## AI assistance Per the AI-assisted contributions section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`: this change was developed with AI assistance. AI-assisted: narrowing the reproducer from the reported `REGEXP_EXTRACT` case down to the arity-dependent behaviour, locating the grammar override, and drafting the patch, fixtures and this description. Manually validated: every claim above was checked by running the commands listed in Verification against this branch, including the full test suite and the mutation check; the date-part cases were confirmed one by one against the parse tree rather than taken on trust. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #5015. In BigQuery, a column named like a datetime unit (`year`, `day`, `month`, …) was parsed as a `date_part` when it appeared as one of several arguments in a function call, so `CP01` reported it and `sqlfluff fix` rewrote the column name. These words now parse as `column_reference` regardless of argument count. **Bug Fixes** - Removed the unconditional `DatetimeUnitSegment` alternative from `FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar`; the gated date-part functions (`DATE_TRUNC`, `DATE_DIFF`, `EXTRACT`, …) parse through a separate branch and are unaffected. - Added `DATEADD` to the `date_part_function_name` set so its leading bare date part still parses as before. - BigQuery only; Snowflake keeps its equivalent entry because it has no gated date-part path. - `SAFE.DATEADD(DAY, …)` now records `DAY` as a `column_reference`, since the `SAFE.`-prefixed form takes the generic path; whether that form is valid is left for reviewers to decide. Written for commit b7c3e69128fb10d459478d0c240341cb8216d267. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: LT02: keep unrendered Jinja block indentation stable
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #5410. LT02 can infer zero indentation for a conditional block whose SQL is entirely skipped in a rendered variant. The resulting fix can move only its opening tag, or move an SQL-empty enclosing block's tags, even though a fully rendered variant accepts their existing source indentation. On subsequent calls, different variants can alternately remove and restore that indentation. Extend the existing skipped-source filtering to exclude a complete matched block occurrence spanning only template lines when it contains skipped source and its tags occupy different source lines. Boundaries must match by UUID and occurrence; visible SQL, incomplete spans, same-line blocks and unrelated boundary content remain outside this exclusion. Existing loop handling and source-patch merging are unchanged. Tests cover the original issue, nested and explicitly configured intermediate renderings, repeated UUIDs, occurrence isolation, visible-body corrections, if/else, LT02 with LT09, boundary content, and existing CRLF-to-LF normalization. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? An eligible SQL-empty occurrence abstains from changing that block's indentation; a rendered alternative remains lintable. With only an unrendered variant, the existing block indentation is preserved rather than guessed. This does not change Jinja evaluation, parser grammar, general fix safety or patch-merger semantics, and does not implement the separate constructor work discussed in#4183. Executed validation so far: - Focused regression suite:46passed. Initial RED:11failed/20passed; extended nested/boundary RED against the first candidate:8failed/38passed. No parse or templating failure was substituted for the intended assertions. - LT02/reflow selection:309passed,2339deselected. - Complete installed dbt1.8 templater suite:63passed,1skipped,345 dependency deprecation warnings. Baseline has the same skip and warning counts; warnings originate from pathspec/dbt dependencies, not a claimed warning-free result. - Full Python run: 11503 passed, 5 failed, 2634 skipped and 5 deprecation warnings. All five failures were diff-quality CLI detection because this invocation's PATH did not include the task virtualenv. With that PATH corrected and no code change, the complete diff-quality test module passed all 9 tests. These are separate invocations, not a claim of one fully green full-suite run. Skips cover unavailable Rust components and one Windows-only case. - Repository all-files pre-commit: all 8 hooks passed, including mypy, Ruff, yamllint and codespell; no tracked files were auto-modified. - Independent task and whole-change agent reviews: approved, with no unresolved Critical, Important or Minor findings. AI assistance disclosure: implementation planning, code/tests and independent agent reviews were performed with Codex/Astra. Commands were executed by agents in an isolated worktree, including before/after checks. No human code review or manual validation by the account owner is claimed. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases: other — real Linter integration and reflow unit tests in the existing test modules, with exact source output and second-fix stability. - Added appropriate documentation: internal function explanation; no new public option or interface. - Followup/future enhancements: no unrelated changes or new issue submissions. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #5410: LT02 no longer infers zero indentation for Jinja conditional blocks whose SQL is entirely skipped in a rendered variant, so repeated lint runs no longer toggle the block's indentation. `_revise_skipped_source_lines` now excludes complete template-only block occurrences whose tags span multiple lines, matching boundaries by UUID and occurrence. Visible SQL, incomplete spans, same-line blocks, and unrelated boundary content keep their existing behavior; loop handling and source-patch merging are unchanged. Tests cover the original issue, nested and explicitly configured intermediate renderings, repeated UUIDs, occurrence isolation, visible-body corrections, if/else, LT02 combined with LT09, boundary content, and LF/CRLF normalization. Written for commit 4c2ba6e1f438e445d1531c8bb1ca34a3686360bd. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: perf(rust): cut frame-engine allocation and copying
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made This removes a good number of the allocations and copies that happen within the frame engine - Share terminator sets as `Arc<[GrammarId]>`: ~40% of frames spilled the `SmallVec<4>`, ~17% of parse allocations. - `Box` compound `FrameContext` states: `TableParseFrame` 312B -> 144B, `memmove` 17% -> 5% of samples. - `settle_frame`: combine/commit `Combining` and `Complete` frames directly instead of a push/pop round trip. - Share empty `MatchResult`s, pool frame-stack buffers, and read terminator/children ids straight from the grammar tables. (I have a follow up to get this a bit faster without needing `unsafe`) - `check_and_handle_table_frame_cache` returns a `CacheLookup` enum. - Remove the never-set `element_key` from the result hand-off. Parse time -27% to -37% across dialects (-34.6% overall). ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Cuts frame-engine allocation and copying, reducing parse time 27-37% across dialects (34.6% overall). **Performance** - Share terminator sets as `Arc<[GrammarId]>`; ~40% of frames spilled the previous `SmallVec<4>`. - Box compound `FrameContext` states, shrinking `TableParseFrame` from 312B to 144B and cutting memmove samples from 17% to 5%. - `settle_frame` now chains any consecutive `Combining`/`Complete` results in a loop instead of pushing and popping them through the stack. - Pool frame-stack buffers across parses, reuse shared empty and last-built terminator sets and empty `MatchResult`s, and read terminators and children ids directly from grammar tables. - `check_and_handle_table_frame_cache` now returns a `CacheLookup` enum and takes the frame by reference. - Dropped the never-set `element_key` from the result hand-off. **Behavior** - An empty grammar match in `match_algorithms` now reports the start position instead of raising "trying but only an empty match found". pulls.title: fix(LT09): preserve comments after SELECT modifiers
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8646. LT09's search for a comment between `SELECT` and the first newline stopped at a `select_clause_modifier`. This missed a trailing comment after `DISTINCT`, `ALL`, or `TOP`, allowing the autofix to move the select target into a line comment. Allow the search to continue through modifier segments so the existing comment protection applies: report the LT09 violation without moving the target. Six YAML regression cases cover comments after `DISTINCT`, `ALL`, and Snowflake `TOP 10`, ordinary autofixing with `ALL` and `TOP`, and a comment after the target on its own line. Existing DISTINCT and other LT09 cases also pass. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? Queries with a comment after a modifier on the SELECT line retain the LT09 violation and are left unchanged by that rule, matching the existing behavior for a comment directly after SELECT. The CLI can therefore report an unfixable violation. The change does not alter configuration or SQL grammar. ### Validation Tested locally on Windows with Python 3.12.14: - The six new cases produced **3 failed, 3 passed** before the source change; all six pass after it. - `python -m pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k LT09 -q --cov=sqlfluff.rules.layout.LT09 --cov-report=term-missing`: **52 passed**. LT09 file coverage is 99%; the uncovered line is the existing no-select-target return. - `python -m pytest test/rules -n 4 -q -rs --tb=short --basetemp=../sqlfluff-8646-test-temp-normal`: **2734 passed, 101 skipped**. All skips require the optional Rust parser. The run had one pytest cache-write permission warning. Earlier attempts hit local directory permissions; the successful run used normal permissions and a separate temporary directory. - `python -m pre_commit run --all-files`: all eight checks passed. - `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, and `lint-imports`: passed. - `python -m mypy -p sqlfluff` and `python -m mypy -p sqlfluff.core --strict`: passed. - `python -m pip check` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Re-ran the issue's CLI reproduction and the LT09-only reproductions for all three modifiers: the target remains outside the comment. The full project test matrix and dbt tests were not run. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included regression cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/LT09.yml`. - Documentation updates are not needed for this correction to existing behavior. - No followup issues are needed for this scoped fix. AI assistance: This change was developed with the assistance of Codex. I directed the investigation and scope of the fix, reviewed the implementation and tests, and verified the final result locally. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes [#8646](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/8646) by safely handling comments after `SELECT` modifiers (`DISTINCT`, `ALL`, `TOP`). LT09's search for a trailing comment previously stopped at the modifier segment, so the autofix could move the select target into a line comment. The scan now continues through `select_clause_modifier` segments, allowing LT09 to detect the comment and report the violation without applying an unsafe fix, matching the existing behavior for comments directly after `SELECT`. Six regression cases cover comments after each modifier, normal autofixing with `ALL` and `TOP`, and a trailing comment after the select target. Configuration and SQL grammar are unchanged. Written for commit b29b63ddebfa820f4a96dcbb8ab5617189288eb4. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: perf(rust): use a per-process regex cache
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made The parser cached `RegexParser` patterns per `Parser` instance, but the Python bridge builds a `Parser` per file. Every grammar regex was recompiled for every file. Use the process-global `REGEX_CACHE` instead, and store `Arc` there. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` (note YML files can be auto generated with `tox -e generate-fixture-yml`). - Full autofix test cases in `test/fixtures/linter/autofix`. - Other. - Added appropriate documentation for the change. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate. --- ## Summary by cubic Replaces the per-`Parser` regex cache with a process-global one, so grammar regexes are compiled once per process instead of once per file. - Stores `Arc` in the global `REGEX_CACHE`, keyed by `(pattern, case_insensitive)`, and shares the same instance across all callers. - Adds a test verifying cached instances are shared and that case sensitivity is part of the cache key. pulls.title: CV06: keep a one-line block comment on the code's line before a newline semicolon
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8642. With `multiline_newline: true`, CV06 keeps an inline comment on the code's line when the semicolon is on the next line (`FROM foo -- c` then `;`). A block comment in the same place was flagged instead, and the fix moved it after the terminator (`FROM foo` / `; /* c */`). It isn't TSQL-specific: ANSI does the same. The cause is `_handle_preceding_inline_comments`. It treats a same-line comment as part of the code's line, but excludes every `block_comment`. That exclusion is right for a block comment that spans lines: `test_fail_newline_preceding_block_comment_custom_multiline` pins moving one, and the lexer splits it into one `block_comment` piece per line (`'/* multiline'`, `'comment'`, `'*/'`). A block comment that opens and closes on the code's line is a single piece, and it now gets the inline comment's treatment. The check is that the piece starts with `/*`, ends with `*/`, and closes every `/*` it opens. The last part matters in PostgreSQL and T-SQL, where comments nest: the first line of `/* outer /* inner */` + newline + `still outer */` also ends in `*/` but is not whole. Test cases in `CV06.yml`, each failing before the change: - `test_pass_newline_single_line_block_comment`: the issue's shape passes. - `test_fail_newline_single_line_block_comment`: with a blank line before the `;`, the fix keeps the comment on the code's line. - `test_fail_final_semi_colon_newline_single_line_block_comment_custom_multiline`: `require_final_semicolon` inserts the `;` after the comment. That path uses the same helper. Two more cases, added after review, pin the nested shape in `postgres` and `tsql`: `test_fail_newline_nested_block_comment_custom_multiline_postgres` / `_tsql`. They pass on `main`, which moves the comment. They failed on this PR's first commit, whose fix put the `;` inside the still-open comment. The existing multi-line block comment cases are unchanged and pass. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - A single-line block comment between the code and a semicolon on a later line now behaves like an inline comment there. `_handle_trailing_inline_comments` (a comment after the `;`) still excludes block comments; I left it alone, since the issue is about the preceding case. - The issue's file with the reporter's full config: the comment stays with its line and CV06 reports nothing. The one change `sqlfluff fix` still makes is `fv (col)` → `fv(col)`. That's a spacing rule, applied the same way to the inline-comment statement, so it's unrelated. What I ran: - `pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k CV06`: 67 passed. On `main` the three single-line cases fail. - `pytest test/rules -n 8`: 2731 passed, 101 skipped (on the current head). - `pytest test -n 8` on the current head: 11463 passed, 2634 skipped, 3 failed. The 3 are in `test/core/plugin_test.py` and fail because the example plugin isn't installed in this venv (tox installs it); on the first commit they failed the same way on `main`. The 5 `test/diff_quality_plugin_test.py` failures from that earlier run did not occur this time. - `pre-commit run` on the two changed files (mypy, yamllint, ruff check, ruff format, codespell): passed. - Not run: the dbt templater tests and the Rust parser. The change is in a rule, not the grammar. AI disclosure: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) did the work end to end. It reproduced the bug with a minimal config and with the reporter's config, wrote the three test cases and confirmed they fail on `main`, wrote the fix, and ran the commands above. I'm submitting it as is; the validation is the test runs listed. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: the helper's docstring; no user docs describe this case. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate: none yet (the trailing-comment case above, if you think it should change too). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8642. With `multiline_newline: true`, CV06 now keeps a block comment that opens and closes on the code's line in place when the semicolon is on the next line, matching how inline comments are handled. Previously the fix moved such a comment after the semicolon. Block comments that span lines are still moved. Since the lexer splits them into one piece per line, a piece only counts as complete when every `/*` in it is closed, so the first line of a nested block comment (PostgreSQL/T-SQL) is not mistaken for a whole comment. pulls.title: RF06: Preserve MySQL and MariaDB account quotes
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8462. RF06 treats quoted MySQL/MariaDB account components as ordinary identifiers and removes their quotes. Account specifications such as `'jeffrey'@'localhost'` then fail to parse after fixing. Exclude `role_reference` parents from RF06 in these two dialects. Regression cases cover `CREATE USER`, privilege and role grants, `DROP USER`, `SET DEFAULT ROLE`, and `DEFINER`, including single quotes, backticks and accounts without a host. Four new regression cases fail before the fix. Additional cases check that table identifiers in the same statements and PostgreSQL role identifiers still receive the expected fixes. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? MySQL/MariaDB account references are excluded from RF06's quoting policy. Their parser types are retained, avoiding the CV10 interaction raised on the previous, unmerged attempt in #8463. ### Validation - `python -m pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k "RF06 or CV10" -q --tb=short --show-capture=no --cov=sqlfluff.rules.references.RF06 --cov-report=term-missing`: 109 passed; RF06 coverage 100%. - 32 additional local checks exercise the account statements with all rules and with RF06/CV10 using double-quoted literals. Account quotes survive, fixed SQL reparses, and a second fix run is unchanged. - `python -m pre_commit run --all-files`: all checks passed, including mypy, Ruff, yamllint, doc8 and codespell. ### AI assistance Codex prepared the fix and regression cases and ran the automated validation above. No independent human validation has been performed. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Completed the applicable contribution steps and included YAML regression cases. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #8462 by stopping RF06 from removing quotes from MySQL/MariaDB account names, so statements like `CREATE USER 'jeffrey'@'localhost'` no longer fail after a fix. - RF06 now excludes `role_reference` parents from its fix in the `mysql` and `mariadb` dialects. - Adds regression cases covering account quotes in user creation, grants, drops, role defaults, and definers, while confirming table identifiers still get unquoted. pulls.title: Postgres: keep VARIADIC outside the typed array literal
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8623 `sqlfluff fix` with LT01 corrupted variadic array arguments on `postgres` (and the dialects that derive from it, e.g. `redshift`, `duckdb`, `materialize`): ```sql SELECT f(VARIADIC ARRAY[1, 2]); --> SELECT f(VARIADICARRAY[1, 2]); SELECT f(VARIADIC arr := ARRAY[1, 2]); --> SELECT f(VARIADICarr:=ARRAY[1, 2]); ``` Root cause: the postgres override of `TypedArrayLiteralSegment` inserted an optional `VARIADIC [name :=]` prefix *inside* the `typed_array_literal` segment. `default_config.cfg` sets `spacing_within = touch` for that segment type (from #5005, to keep `ARRAY[...]` tight), so the touch rule also applied at the `VARIADIC` / `ARRAY` boundary and LT01 removed the space. The call-site `VARIADIC` keyword is already handled by `FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar` (`VARIADIC `, added in #7115), so the override is redundant. This PR removes it: `typed_array_literal` again covers exactly `ARRAY` + `[...]`, and `VARIADIC` is a sibling keyword inside the function brackets. As a side effect, `VARIADIC arr := ARRAY[...]` now parses as a `named_argument`, consistent with how the `=>` and `=` forms in `variadic.sql` already parse. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? - The parse tree for `VARIADIC ARRAY[...]` / `VARIADIC arr := ARRAY[...]` changes shape as described above (`variadic.yml` regenerated). - The intended #5005 behaviour is preserved: `SELECT ARRAY [1, 2]` is still flagged and fixed to `ARRAY[1, 2]`, including inside a VARIADIC argument. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - `.yml` rule test cases in `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases`: three new LT01 cases in `LT01-brackets.yml` (two pass, one fail/fix). They fail on `main` and pass with this change. - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects`: `postgres/variadic.yml` regenerated. - Tested with `pytest test/dialects/dialects_test.py -k "postgres or duckdb or redshift or materialize"` (963 passed) and `pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py` (2531 passed); `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` and `yamllint` clean on the changed files. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes LT01 corrupting `VARIADIC` array arguments in Postgres and the dialects derived from it (Redshift, DuckDB, Materialize). `sqlfluff fix` previously turned `SELECT f(VARIADIC ARRAY[1, 2])` into `SELECT f(VARIADICARRAY[1, 2])`. The Postgres `TypedArrayLiteralSegment` override inserted an optional `VARIADIC [name :=]` prefix inside the array literal segment, so the `spacing_within = touch` layout also applied at the `VARIADIC`/`ARRAY` boundary. Removing the override keeps the touch rule scoped to `ARRAY[...]`; the call-site `VARIADIC` keyword is already handled by `FunctionContentsExpressionGrammar`. The `VARIADIC arr := ARRAY[...]` form now parses as a `named_argument`, consistent with how the `=>` and `=` forms parse. The intended behavior that `ARRAY [1, 2]` still fixes to `ARRAY[1, 2]` is preserved, including inside a VARIADIC argument, and the parse tree shape changes are captured by the regenerated Postgres dialect fixture. Written for commit e91d69934a5664f333a685a10b8b2116d2e662fc. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: fix(dialect): allow column reference in redshift's exclude syntax
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made These are valid syntax in Redshift that got parsing error ` L: x | P: x | PRS | Line x, Position x: Found unparsable section 'exclude....` ```sql SELECT a.col1, b.* EXCLUDE (b.col2, b.col3) FROM table1 AS a, table2 AS b; SELECT a.col1, b.* EXCLUDE b.col2 FROM table1 AS a, table2 AS b; ``` Prior implementation only accept single identifier. I simply replace it with a column reference segment **How to reproduce** Below sql executed in redshift successfully ```sql select tbl.* exclude (tbl.a, tbl.b) from (select 1 as a, 2 as b, 3 as c) as tbl ``` ironically, redshift query editor also does not recognize the syntax :) ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? v1.20.0 — August 19, 2026

This release hardens runtime option handling, adds RFC 9110 status-code aliases, fixes Node.js and XHR reliability issues, and refreshes project tooling and documentation.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • HTTP Status Naming: Added ContentTooLarge (413) and UnprocessableContent (422), while retaining PayloadTooLarge and UnprocessableEntity as backward-compatible deprecated aliases. (#11082)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Runtime Option Handling: Hardened behavioral configuration reads against shared and foreign prototype pollution and normalized unsafe interceptor replacement objects. (#11141)
