Its four existing path cases are untouched. - [x] Added appropriate documentation for the change — the reference URL is on the new alternative and in the fixture. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate — n/a. **Testing** - `pytest test/dialects/` in full, not a `-k` subset. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed file. - A probe set of twelve statements, five deliberately broken, all still rejected — including the three path forms as regression checks. - Measured against a corpus of 867 files of published Databricks SQL: no file regresses, and the mutation corpus still rejects 100% of its guaranteed-invalid inputs. In fairness, no file in that corpus *improves* either — no published SQL I have on hand converts a registered table, so this one rests on the reference rather than on an observed failure. ## AI assistance This pull request was co-authored with AI assistants: **Claude Opus 5** (Anthropic) and **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**. They drafted the grammar, the fixtures and the rejection tests, and ran the measurements, under the contributor's direction. Every construct was checked against the Databricks SQL reference, and the changes were run through the whole `test/dialects/` suite, the Python/Rust parity tests, `make reference` and `make corpus` before submission. The human contributor remains responsible for the final pull request, including its correctness, tests and maintainability, as [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assisted-contributions) requires. --- ## Summary by cubic Lets `CONVERT TO DELTA` accept a table identifier as the target, so converting a catalog-registered table works instead of only file paths. - Retains existing path support and keeps `NO STATISTICS` and `PARTITIONED BY` working with table targets. - Adds parser test fixtures covering bare, qualified, and optioned table-name conversions. Written for commit 0087551a55f3e670cee7d77c37efdafe288110b0. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Databricks: support SHOW GRANTS
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `SHOW GRANTS` didn't parse including examples from Databricks' official docs: ```sql SHOW GRANTS ON demo.schema.names; SHOW GRANTS `alf@melmak.et` ON SCHEMA my_schema; ``` Syntax, from the [reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/security-show-grant): `SHOW GRANTS [ principal ] ON securable_object`, where `GRANT` can be used in place of `GRANTS`. This adds it to `ShowObjectGrammar`, the same way `SHOW VOLUMES` is handled. The securable reuses `AccessObjectSegment` and the principal is a `RoleReferenceSegment`. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? `SHOW GRANTS ON SHARE|CONNECTION|EXTERNAL LOCATION` still don't parse, because those securables aren't in `AccessObjectSegment` and `GRANT` rejects them too. Widening that list should change `GRANT`, `REVOKE` and `SHOW GRANTS` together, so I've left it for a separate PR. ### Tests New fixture `databricks/show_grants` (ten statements: the securable kinds, quoted and unquoted principals, `GRANT` and `GRANTS`). Full `test/dialects/` passes. ### AI assistance Written with Claude and DeepSeek. I checked each form against the Databricks reference and ran the dialect suite myself. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds support for `SHOW GRANTS [ principal ] ON securable_object` in the Databricks dialect, which previously failed to parse in every spelling. `GRANT` is also accepted as an alternative to `GRANTS`, matching Databricks' reference. - Reuses `AccessObjectSegment`, so `SHOW GRANTS` accepts exactly the securables `GRANT` and `REVOKE` accept today. - `ON SHARE`, `ON CONNECTION`, and `ON EXTERNAL LOCATION` remain unsupported because `GRANT` rejects those securables too; widening that list should happen for both statements together. - The optional principal uses `RoleReferenceSegment`, covering quoted and unquoted users, service principals, and groups. - The securable and its `ON` are required, so `SHOW GRANTS;` still does not parse. Written for commit c6caa76466eb6dccdc4dc0c49bf44c5e7cc6ab23. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: SparkSQL: support EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` was not implemented in this dialect at all. Not just the argument clauses — the simplest form was unparsable too: ```sql EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1'; ``` [Spark's reference](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-ref-syntax-aux-exec-imm.html) gives: ``` EXECUTE IMMEDIATE sql_string [ INTO var_name [, ...] ] [ USING { arg_expr [ AS ] [ alias ] } [, ...] ] ``` and adds that "for compatibility with other SQL dialects, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` also supports `USING ( { arg_expr [ AS ] [alias] } [, ...] )`". [Databricks documents the same grammar](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-aux-execute-immediate), down to that bracketed form, so this goes in SparkSQL and `databricks` inherits it rather than being written twice. Four details taken from the references and Spark's own parser rather than guessed: - **`sql_string` is an expression**, as in Spark's parser, so it is not limited to a literal or a variable. The reference's own last example needs that: `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT ' || func || '(c1) ...' USING 5 + 7 AS first`. - **`INTO` takes multipart identifiers**, again following Spark's parser, so a session variable can be qualified: `INTO session.v1`, `INTO system.session.v1`. - **`AS` is optional** before an alias. Spark's test suite uses the lower-case `as` spelling. - **`INTO` takes no brackets.** See below. Found in a published Databricks notebook on parameterised queries, and in Spark's own `execute-immediate.sql` test input. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? `INTO (a, b)` is deliberately **not** accepted. Spark's test file labels that line `-- INTO does not support braces - parser error`, and the syntax block gives `INTO var_name [, ...]` unbracketed. The Databricks parameter description writes the heading as `INTO ( var_name [, ...] )`, which looks like a contradiction but is just the heading's formatting — the syntax block on the same page agrees with Spark. It is rejected because the `INTO` list only takes names. There is no dedicated test for it, following the maintainer guidance on #8516 that fixtures are sufficient. Regenerating the parse fixtures for **every** dialect leaves all 2315 unchanged, so nothing that parsed before parses differently now. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - [x] `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` — a new `sparksql/execute_immediate` fixture with fourteen statements: literal and variable SQL strings, `INTO` alone, `INTO` with several variables, qualified `INTO` variables (`session.v1`, `system.session.v1`, and a mix of qualified and plain names ahead of `USING`), `USING` bracketed and unbracketed, upper and lower case `AS`, and a concatenated constant expression. - [x] Added appropriate documentation for the change — the reference URL is on the new segment and in the fixture header. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate — n/a. **Testing** - `pytest test/dialects/` in full, not a `-k` subset, on both the Rust and the Python parser: 7192 passed on each. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed file. - A probe set covering qualified and mixed `INTO` lists and three deliberately broken statements (`INTO (a, b)`, a missing SQL string, `INTO ,,,`), all still rejected. ## AI assistance This pull request was co-authored with AI assistants: **Claude Opus 5** and **Claude Sonnet 5.5** (Anthropic), and **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** on earlier revisions. They drafted the grammar and the fixtures, ran the measurements and made the changes from review, under the contributor's direction. Each construct was checked against the Spark and Databricks references, and the `INTO` and `sql_string` rules against Spark's own grammar. The changes were run through the whole `test/dialects/` suite on both parsers. The human contributor remains responsible for the final pull request, including its correctness, tests and maintainability, as [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assisted-contributions) requires. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds support for `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` in SparkSQL and `databricks`, so the previously unparsable statement now parses. - Accepts `sql_string` as a literal, identifier, or constant expression. - Supports bracketed and unbracketed `USING` clauses, with `AS` optional before aliases. - Takes `INTO` variables as multipart identifiers, so session variables like `session.v1` and `system.session.v1` are allowed. - Adds a parse fixture with 14 valid statements, including qualified `INTO` targets and a concatenated constant-expression SQL string. Written for commit cecdb574a77cf121afa38c3209c37d23e8efe448. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: SparkSQL: allow DESCRIBE HISTORY and DESCRIBE DETAIL as relations
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `DESCRIBE HISTORY` and `DESCRIBE DETAIL` both return a result set, and Databricks documents querying that result set directly. From [Work with table history](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/history): ```sql SELECT version, operationMetrics.numAddedFiles AS files_added FROM (DESCRIBE HISTORY table_name) WHERE operation = 'OPTIMIZE' ORDER BY version DESC; ``` That was unparsable. `TableExpressionSegment` offers `Bracketed(Ref("SelectableGrammar"))` for a nested select, which does not cover a describe statement — so the bare `DESCRIBE HISTORY t;` parsed while any query over its output did not. The two Delta introspection statements now sit alongside the nested-select alternative. Found in a published Databricks pipeline demo that collects storage locations with `SELECT ... location FROM (DESCRIBE DETAIL )` and unions the rows together. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? Narrow by construction: only these two statements are added, and only inside brackets in a table expression. `SELECT * FROM DESCRIBE HISTORY t` without brackets is still rejected, as is `(DESCRIBE TABLE t)`, which is not a result-set statement. Regenerating the parse fixtures for **every** dialect leaves all 2269 unchanged, so nothing that parsed before parses differently now. The `databricks` dialect picks this up automatically: its `TableExpressionSegment` is a `.copy()` of this one. One thing worth knowing, though it predates this change: `SELECT * FROM (DESCRIBE HISTORY)` — no target — parses today, because `DESCRIBE` is not reserved, so it reads as a table named `describe` aliased to `history`. That is unchanged here; I mention it only because it makes a tempting negative test case that does not actually test anything. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - [x] `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` — a new `sparksql/delta_describe_as_relation` fixture with seven queries: both statements as relations, the documented `WHERE`/`ORDER BY` form, an aliased one, a path target, one with `LIMIT`, and a `UNION ALL` of two `DESCRIBE DETAIL` relations. It is a new file rather than an addition to `delta_describe_history` / `delta_describe_detail` so that it does not collide with #8510, which edits both of those. - [x] Added appropriate documentation for the change — the reference URL is on the new grammar and in the fixture header. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate — n/a. **Testing** - `pytest test/dialects/` in full, not a `-k databricks` subset — that filter skips the hand-written rejection tests in `databricks_test.py`. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed file. - A probe set of nine statements including four deliberately broken ones — an extra token after the target, trailing junk after the bracket, an unclosed bracket, and plain garbage — all still rejected. - Measured against a corpus of 867 files of published Databricks SQL: no file regresses, and the mutation corpus still rejects 100% of its guaranteed-invalid inputs. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Allows `DESCRIBE HISTORY` and `DESCRIBE DETAIL` to be used as relations inside brackets, so queries like `SELECT * FROM (DESCRIBE HISTORY t)` now parse in the `sparksql` dialect. - Adds a `Bracketed` alternative for the two statements in `TableExpressionSegment`. - `databricks` inherits the change via its copied grammar. - Adds a `sparksql/delta_describe_as_relation` fixture covering aliases, paths, `LIMIT`, and `UNION ALL`. - Existing parse fixture outputs are unchanged. Written for commit 24397bfbb965436699d2d42d1a32ef665af63be9. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Databricks: restore LIVE and STREAMING LIVE view support
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made The `databricks` dialect rejects three forms its own reference documents, all dropped when #7405 rewrote `CreateViewStatementSegment` from scratch instead of subclassing `sparksql`: - Pipeline views: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] [GLOBAL] TEMPORARY [STREAMING] LIVE VIEW ...` — `sparksql` parses them, so the dialect named after Databricks was the one that could not. - The temporary view backed by a data source: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] TEMPORARY VIEW name [column_list] USING data_source [OPTIONS (...)]`. - The parenthesised `with_clause` list: `WITH ( schema_binding [, ...] )`. `test/fixtures/dialects/sparksql/databricks_dlt_create_view.sql` has covered the pipeline forms since well before that change. It simply was never exercised under the `databricks` dialect, so nothing failed. Restored here: - `LIVE`, with `STREAMING` bound to it rather than independently optional, because there is no `CREATE STREAMING VIEW`. - `OR REFRESH` is deliberately **not** accepted on a view. It belongs to streaming tables and materialized views, which have their own segments; the corpus of published Databricks SQL uses it with `MATERIALIZED VIEW`, `STREAMING TABLE` and `LIVE TABLE`, and with no `VIEW` form at all. - The data-source production, whose `TEMPORARY` is unbracketed (so `CREATE VIEW v USING csv` stays rejected) and whose `USING` data source and `OPTIONS` name-value pairs are all required. - The parenthesised `with_clause` list, as an alternative to the existing `WITH SCHEMA ...` and `WITH METRICS` forms. - `ConstraintStatementSegment` in the column list, so pipeline expectations (`CONSTRAINT valid_a EXPECT (a IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW`) parse. The LIVE schema is [deprecated](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/live-schema) in favour of the default publishing mode, but the page is explicit that "you can still use legacy publishing mode and the LIVE virtual schema for pipelines that were created with this mode" — so a linter still has to parse it. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? `CREATE STREAMING VIEW`, `CREATE LIVE STREAMING VIEW`, `CREATE VIEW v USING csv` (without `TEMPORARY`) and a bare `CREATE LIVE` are all still rejected; only the documented orderings are added. Expectations are accepted in the column list of any view here, not only a `LIVE` one, which matches what `sparksql` does today. Restricting them to the `LIVE` branch would mean duplicating the whole bracketed column list into two alternatives; I did not think that was worth it without a maintainer saying so, and am happy to change it if you disagree. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - [x] `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` — `databricks/create_view` gains the pipeline forms, the data-source forms and the parenthesised `with_clause`; `databricks_test.py` gains the rejection boundaries: `OR REFRESH`, a data source missing, a non-`TEMPORARY` data-source view, empty and value-less `OPTIONS`, and `WITH` without a clause. - [x] Added appropriate documentation for the change — the LIVE schema and CREATE VIEW reference URLs are on the grammar and in the fixture header. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate — n/a. **Testing** - `pytest test/dialects/` in full, not a `-k databricks` subset — that filter skips the hand-written rejection tests in `databricks_test.py`. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed file. ## AI assistance This pull request was co-authored with AI assistants: **Claude Opus 5** (Anthropic) and **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**. They drafted the grammar, the fixtures and the rejection tests, and ran the measurements, under the contributor's direction. Every construct was checked against the Databricks SQL reference, and the changes were run through the whole `test/dialects/` suite, the Python/Rust parity tests, `make reference` and `make corpus` before submission. The human contributor remains responsible for the final pull request, including its correctness, tests and maintainability, as [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assisted-contributions) requires. --- ## Summary by cubic Restores Databricks `LIVE` view parsing so pipeline views like `CREATE TEMPORARY STREAMING LIVE VIEW` are accepted again, and reinstates the data-source view production and parenthesised `with_clause` that were also lost in the #7405 rewrite. - Adds `LIVE` and `STREAMING` (bound to `LIVE`) to `CreateViewStatementSegment`. - Accepts `CONSTRAINT ... EXPECT ...` in the column list, matching `sparksql`. - Restores `CREATE [OR REPLACE] TEMPORARY VIEW ... USING data_source [OPTIONS (...)]`. - `CREATE OR REFRESH ... VIEW`, `CREATE STREAMING VIEW`, bare `CREATE LIVE`, and `USING` without `TEMPORARY` remain rejected. Written for commit ed751dd0a2fc9396fc2ca590e330162fd3ccfd04. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Databricks: support Unity Catalog volume privileges in GRANT and REVOKE

pulls.title: Databricks: support MANAGED LOCATION on CREATE CATALOG
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `CREATE CATALOG ... MANAGED LOCATION` was unparsable in the `databricks` dialect: ```sql CREATE CATALOG de_book MANAGED LOCATION 's3://data-lake/de-book-ext-data'; ``` The [CREATE CATALOG reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-catalog) gives the trailing clauses as a bracketed alternation followed by `[...]`: ``` CREATE CATALOG [ IF NOT EXISTS ] catalog_name [ USING SHARE provider_name . share_name | MANAGED LOCATION location_path | RETAIN DROPPED FOR number { HOUR | HOURS | DAY | DAYS | WEEK | WEEKS } | COMMENT comment | DEFAULT COLLATION default_collation_name | OPTIONS ( { option_name = option_value } [ , ... ] ) ] [...] ``` but the grammar accepted only a single trailing `COMMENT`. `MANAGED LOCATION` now joins `COMMENT` in an `AnySetOf`, which also makes the two order-independent, as the `[...]` in the reference describes. `CREATE DATABASE` in this dialect already spells the clause the same way (`Ref.keyword("MANAGED", optional=True), "LOCATION", ...`), so `MANAGED LOCATION` worked on a schema while failing on the catalog immediately above it in the same script. Found in a published Databricks notebook setting up a Unity Catalog hierarchy. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The remaining documented clauses — `USING SHARE`, `RETAIN DROPPED FOR`, `DEFAULT COLLATION` and `OPTIONS` — are deliberately left out. Each needs keywords this dialect does not currently carry (`SHARE`, `DROPPED`, `COLLATION`), none appeared in the SQL that prompted this, and adding them blind is how a grammar starts accepting things the vendor does not. `CREATE FOREIGN CATALOG` is likewise untouched. `AnySetOf` allows each clause at most once, so `COMMENT 'a' COMMENT 'b'` and `MANAGED LOCATION 'a' MANAGED LOCATION 'b'` are still rejected. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes, which may be one or more of the following: - [x] `.sql`/`.yml` parser test cases in `test/fixtures/dialects` — the existing `databricks/create_catalog` fixture gains the `MANAGED LOCATION` form and a both-clauses case, rather than a new file, keeping coverage for the statement in one place. The regenerated `.yml` diff is additive apart from its `_hash` line: no existing parse structure changes. - [x] Added appropriate documentation for the change — the reference URL was already on the segment. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate — n/a. **Testing** - `pytest test/dialects/` in full — 7000 passed. (Not a `-k databricks` subset: `databricks_test.py` holds hand-written rejection tests that a filtered run skips.) - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed file. - A probe set covering the corpus statement, both clause orders, the three pre-existing forms, and five deliberately broken ones — `LOCATION` without `MANAGED`, `MANAGED` without `LOCATION`, `MANAGED LOCATION` with no path, and each clause repeated — all of which are still rejected. - The syntax came from the reference page linked above, not from inference. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Databricks dialect so `CREATE CATALOG ... MANAGED LOCATION 's3://...'` parses correctly. Previously only a single trailing `COMMENT` was allowed; now `MANAGED LOCATION` and `COMMENT` can appear in either order, matching the documented `[...]` alternation. - `MANAGED LOCATION` is still limited to one occurrence per statement; repeats are rejected. - The other documented trailing clauses (`USING SHARE`, `RETAIN DROPPED FOR`, `DEFAULT COLLATION`, `OPTIONS`) are intentionally not added because they require keywords not yet present in this dialect. Written for commit 8f75053e84d6fb60ca399b5d19c053d4f8c76524. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: SparkSQL: accept DESC as an abbreviation for DESCRIBE HISTORY and DETAIL
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made `DESC` is accepted wherever `DESCRIBE` is, and `DescribeStatementSegment` already spells that as `OneOf("DESCRIBE", "DESC")`. The two Delta introspection statements were added separately and hardcoded `"DESCRIBE"`: ```python class DescribeHistoryStatementSegment(BaseSegment): match_grammar: Matchable = Sequence( "DESCRIBE", "HISTORY", ... ``` so these were unparsable while their `DESCRIBE` spellings parsed: ```sql DESC HISTORY my_table; DESC DETAIL my_table; ``` Both now take the same `OneOf` as every other describe statement. Found in a published Databricks notebook using `DESC HISTORY` to inspect a change data feed. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? This only widens two statements to accept an abbreviation the dialect already accepts everywhere else, so it cannot change how any currently-parsing statement parses. Checked: - `pytest test/dialects/` — **7000 passed**. - Verified in **both** the `sparksql` and `databricks` dialects, since the change is in the shared SparkSQL dialect: `DESC HISTORY`, `DESC DETAIL`, `DESC HISTORY ... LIMIT`, alongside regression checks that `DESCRIBE HISTORY`, `DESCRIBE DETAIL`, `DESC TABLE` and `DESCRIBE ` are unaffected, and that a deliberately broken statement is still rejected. - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. The two regenerated fixture ymls change **only** their `_hash` line; every other line in both diffs is an addition. No existing parse structure changes. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes: - The existing `delta_describe_history` and `delta_describe_detail` fixtures gain the `DESC` spellings, rather than new fixture files, so the coverage for each statement stays in one place. Ymls produced by the standard fixture generator. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: n/a — no user-facing documentation describes this. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup: none needed. ### AI-assisted contribution disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md: developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). - **AI-assisted:** the grammar change, the commit message and the added fixture cases. - **Validated by running:** the full dialect suite (7000 passed); fixture yml regeneration, with the resulting diffs inspected line by line to confirm they are additive apart from `_hash`; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`; and a probe set run against both affected dialects including regression and negative controls. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the SparkSQL dialect rejecting `DESC HISTORY` and `DESC DETAIL`, which previously only parsed with the full `DESCRIBE` spelling. Both statements now accept `DESC`, matching every other describe statement in the dialect. - Replaces the hardcoded `"DESCRIBE"` with `OneOf("DESCRIBE", "DESC")` in both statements. - Adds `DESC` spellings to the existing `delta_describe_history` and `delta_describe_detail` fixtures; no existing parse structure changes. pulls.title: Databricks: support PRIVATE streaming tables and CREATE FLOW append flows
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Fixes #8455. Three pieces of Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines DDL were unparsable, each with a close relative that already parsed. The issue lists ten reproduction statements; all ten now parse, and the two controls it names are unaffected. **1. `PRIVATE` on streaming tables** ``` CREATE [ OR REFRESH ] [ PRIVATE ] STREAMING TABLE table_name ... ``` A private streaming table is visible inside the pipeline but not published to the catalog. Materialized views already accepted `PRIVATE`; streaming tables come from the shared SparkSQL `TableDefinitionSegment`, which has no such keyword. Databricks now overrides that grammar to insert `PRIVATE` before `STREAMING`, rather than adding Databricks-only syntax to SparkSQL — which is the direction #6891 asks for. The insertion is anchored on the `STREAMING` keyword rather than an index, so it fails loudly if that sequence changes upstream. **2. The `CREATE FLOW` append branch** ``` CREATE FLOW flow_name [ COMMENT comment ] AS { AUTO CDC [ ONCE ] INTO target_table create_auto_cdc_flow_spec | INSERT [ ONCE ] INTO target_table BY NAME [ replace_using_spec ] query } ``` `CreateFlowStatementSegment` hardcoded `Sequence("AS", "AUTO", "CDC", "INTO")`, so the `INSERT ... BY NAME` branch could not parse at all. Append flows are how a pipeline points several sources at one streaming table. **3. `ONCE` and `COMMENT`** Both appear in the syntax block above, and both failed — including on the CDC branch that was otherwise supported. As the issue notes, the [reference page](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/ldp-sql-ref-create-flow) writes `INSERT [ONCE] INTO` while [Use flows in Lakeflow pipelines](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/flow-examples) and [Backfilling historical data](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/flows-backfill) write `INSERT INTO ONCE`. Both spellings are in the Databricks documentation, so both parse. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? **`ONCE` becomes a keyword**, which is the one part worth a close look. It is added to `UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS`, so it remains usable as an identifier — a column named `once`, or an alias `AS once`, both still parse. Both are covered explicitly in the probes run against this change, because making a common word reserved is exactly the kind of change that turns a working query into a syntax error. Everything else is additive: `PRIVATE` is optional, `COMMENT` is optional, and the `AUTO CDC` branch keeps its existing shape inside the new `OneOf`. Checked: - `pytest test/dialects/` — **7003 passed**. - Regenerating every Databricks fixture yml produces **no diff** outside the one added here. - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. - Controls verified alongside: `CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE` and `CREATE OR REFRESH PRIVATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` (the two the issue names as already working) still parse, and a deliberately broken statement is still rejected. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test case at `test/fixtures/dialects/databricks/create_flow_and_private_streaming_table.sql`, covering all ten statements from the issue's reproduction plus its two controls. The yml was produced by the standard fixture generator. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: n/a — dialect syntax support, no user-facing documentation describes it. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup: none needed; this closes #8455 in full. ### AI-assisted contribution disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md: developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). - **AI-assisted:** the grammar changes, the commit message and the test fixture. - **Validated by running:** the full dialect suite (7003 passed); fixture yml regeneration confirming no existing fixture changes; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`; and a probe set covering all ten statements from the issue, its two controls, a deliberately broken statement, and `ONCE` used as both a column name and an alias. - The syntax was taken from the Databricks documentation pages linked above, not inferred. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds Databricks dialect support for `PRIVATE` streaming tables, `CREATE FLOW` append flows, and `COMMENT`/`ONCE` clauses on both flow branches, all of which previously raised parse errors. All ten statements from issue #8455 now parse, and the two control statements still parse unchanged. - `ONCE` is added as an unreserved keyword, so identifiers like a column named `once` still work; both `INSERT ONCE INTO` and `INSERT INTO ONCE` are accepted. - `PRIVATE` is bound to `STREAMING`, so `CREATE PRIVATE TABLE` and similar invalid forms are rejected. - Append-flow targets named `once` parse correctly instead of being mistaken for the optional `ONCE` keyword. - Fixture coverage exercises `once` as a column, alias, table, and flow target, and `private` as a column. Written for commit 35faf32f3afb7e4cc2cae582b0c3827ddac999c0. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Databricks: allow a materialized view to declare only expectations
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made A Lakeflow/DLT materialized view declares its data-quality expectations in the same bracketed list that holds its columns, and may declare **only** expectations, letting the column types come from the query: ```sql CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW jhu_covid19_cleansed( CONSTRAINT valid_confirmed EXPECT (confirmed IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW ) COMMENT "The cleansed Johns Hopkins COVID-19 dataset." AS SELECT ... ``` `CreateMaterializedViewStatementSegment` required the bracketed list to begin with a column definition, so the leading `CONSTRAINT` had nothing to match and the statement was unparsable. This makes the column group optional. **The ordering is deliberately left alone.** ### Why only that, and not the ordering The documented syntax does write the column group as required: ``` ( { column_name column_type column_properties } [, ...] [ CONSTRAINT expectation_name EXPECT (expectation_expr) [ ON VIOLATION { FAIL UPDATE | DROP ROW } ] ] [, ...] [ , table_constraint ] [...] ) ``` — [CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW (pipelines)](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/ldp-sql-ref-create-materialized-view) My first attempt at this replaced the whole list with an unordered `Delimited(OneOf(...))`, which broke `test_materialized_view_constraints_reject_invalid_order`. Checking the documentation showed that test is right: columns, then expectations, then table constraints is the documented order, and this PR keeps enforcing it. Both orderings that test covers are still rejected. Where documentation and reality diverge is the *required* column group. Databricks' own published pipelines ([databricks/delta-live-tables-notebooks](https://github.com/databricks/delta-live-tables-notebooks)) ship materialized views with no column list at all, only expectations. Those pipelines run, so the column group is optional in practice, and that is the only thing this PR changes. Across four published DLT pipelines using this form (the repo above, plus a public Lakeflow connector project), all four now parse; all four were unparsable before. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The new alternative only applies where the list begins with an expectation — previously a parse error — so every list that parsed before takes the same path it did before. Checked specifically: - `pytest test/dialects/` — **7003 passed**, including `test_materialized_view_constraints_reject_invalid_order`. - Regenerating every Databricks fixture yml (60 fixtures) produces **no diff** outside the one added here. - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test case at `test/fixtures/dialects/databricks/create_materialized_view_expectations.sql`, covering expectations alone, several expectations with and without `ON VIOLATION`, expectations followed by a table constraint, the documented column-first ordering, and the two shapes that already worked (columns only, and no column list). The yml was produced by the standard fixture generator. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: n/a — no user-facing documentation describes this grammar detail. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup: none needed; no existing issue covers this. ### AI-assisted contribution disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md: developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). - **AI-assisted:** the diagnosis, the grammar change, the commit message and the test fixture. - **Validated by running:** the full dialect suite (7003 passed); fixture yml regeneration confirming no existing fixture changes; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`; and a before/after measurement over an external corpus of published Databricks notebooks. - As noted above, the first version of this change was wrong — it removed the documented ordering constraint and broke an existing test. It was corrected against the published Databricks syntax rather than by adjusting the test. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Allows Databricks `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` to parse when the bracketed list contains only expectations, with no column definitions. Previously such statements failed to parse; they now parse, while the documented ordering (columns, then expectations, then table constraints) is still enforced. Written for commit 84fa0e7d6ba49ffeb42531b15db381f1a1bb86ff. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Databricks: allow a magic cell body after a single-line magic directive
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made A Databricks magic cell opens with a directive line that either stands alone: ```sql -- MAGIC %md -- MAGIC # Title ``` or carries content of its own: ```sql -- MAGIC %md # Title -- MAGIC -- MAGIC Some prose. ``` `MagicCellStatementSegment` only allowed continuation lines after the first form. The second matches `MagicSingleLineGrammar`, which takes no body, so the `-- MAGIC` lines following it had nothing to attach to and the file was reported unparsable from that point on — taking every subsequent statement in the notebook with it. The directive names the language; it does not say how many lines the cell has. Both spellings now take an optional body: ```python OneOf( Sequence( OneOf( Ref("MagicStartGrammar"), Ref("MagicSingleLineGrammar"), optional=True, ), AnyNumberOf(Ref("MagicLineGrammar"), optional=True), ), AnyNumberOf( OneOf( Ref("BareMagicCellGrammar"), Ref("NotebookStartBareMagicCellGrammar"), ) ), ) ``` The shape it fixes is common in real notebooks — a markdown cell whose first line is a heading. Measured against 46 published Databricks notebooks ([jaceklaskowski/learn-databricks](https://github.com/jaceklaskowski/learn-databricks)), files parsing cleanly went from **13 to 40**. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? None found. The change only adds an optional body to an alternative that previously had none, so it accepts a superset of what it accepted before. Two checks specifically for regressions: - Regenerating every Databricks fixture yml (`test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py --dialect databricks`, 60 fixtures) produces **no diff**, so no currently-parsing construct now parses differently. - The full dialect suite passes: **7003 passed**. This does not address #8376 (the LT01 spacing rule on magic lines), which is a separate lint-rule issue in the same feature area. ### Pull Request checklist - [x] Please confirm you have completed any of the necessary steps below. - Included test cases to demonstrate any code changes: - `.sql`/`.yml` parser test case added at `test/fixtures/dialects/databricks/magic_single_line_with_body.sql`, covering a directive-plus-body cell, a single-line magic with no body, and a non-`%md` language with a body. The yml was generated with the standard fixture generator. - Added appropriate documentation for the change: n/a — no user-facing documentation describes this grammar detail. - Created GitHub issues for any relevant followup/future enhancements if appropriate: no existing issue covers this case, and none was opened separately since this PR closes it. ### AI-assisted contribution disclosure Per CONTRIBUTING.md: this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). - **AI-assisted:** the diagnosis, the grammar change, the commit message, and the test fixture. - **Validated by running:** the full dialect suite (7003 passed); Databricks fixture yml regeneration, confirming no existing fixture changes; and a before/after measurement over an external corpus of 46 published notebooks (13 → 40 parsing cleanly). `test/core` was also run before and after and shows the same 13 pre-existing failures in both, all from the example plugin not being installed in the local environment and unrelated to this change. - An earlier hypothesis — that empty `-- MAGIC` lines were the trigger — was tested and **disproved** before arriving at this one; empty continuation lines parse fine today. The trigger is specifically content on the directive line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes Databricks magic cell parsing so continuation lines are accepted after a directive that carries content (e.g. `-- MAGIC %md # Title`), which previously made the file unparsable from that point on. The grammar now accepts a superset of the previous syntax, with no effect on existing valid files. Written for commit 651babc0f834ded7b359a7831097d810fca10be8. Summary will update on new commits.

pulls.title: Snowflake: parse multiple ALTER SESSION SET parameters
pulls.body: ### Brief summary of the change made Parse multiple assignments in Snowflake `ALTER SESSION SET`, allowing commas, whitespace, and mixed separators as documented in [Snowflake's syntax reference](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/alter-session). For example, `ALTER SESSION SET TIMEZONE = 'UTC', QUERY_TAG = 'job';` currently fails to parse. The new SQL/YAML fixture covers all separator forms and string, boolean, and numeric values. Empty assignments and leading, trailing, or repeated commas remain rejected. ### Are there any other side effects of this change that we should be aware of? The grammar change is limited to `ALTER SESSION SET`; existing single assignments and `UNSET` retain their behavior. Each later assignment accepts its own optional comma because `OptionallyDelimited` currently raises an assertion on mixed separators. AI assistance: OpenAI GPT-6 assisted with the grammar change and tests. issues.title: ST08 fix removes the parentheses a scalar subquery or a row constructor needs
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

ST08's fix removes the parentheses after `DISTINCT` even when they belong to the select target itself, which changes or breaks the query:

- A PostgreSQL row constructor, `SELECT DISTINCT (a, b) FROM foo` (one row-valued column), becomes `SELECT DISTINCT a, b FROM foo` (two columns). The fixed SQL still parses, but the result shape changes. This also happens with the default rule set.
- A scalar subquery, `SELECT DISTINCT (SELECT a FROM t), b FROM foo`, becomes `SELECT DISTINCT SELECT a FROM t , b FROM foo`, which no longer parses. This one shows with `--rules ST08`; with the default rules the other fixes reorder the targets first and the subquery keeps its parentheses.

In the `select_clause` path (`src/sqlfluff/rules/structure/ST08.py`, around line 62 at 078bf03), ST08 strips the brackets whenever they are the expression's only child, without looking inside them. The `function` path already refuses this when the brackets hold a subquery (around line 85), and `test_pass_distinct_subquery_inside_count` in `ST08.yml` covers that case.

### Expected Behaviour

The parentheses around a scalar subquery or a row constructor stay, because removing them changes what the statement means. `SELECT DISTINCT(a), b` still becomes `SELECT DISTINCT a, b`.

### Observed Behaviour

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT a, b FROM foo
```

for the postgres row constructor, and for the ANSI scalar subquery:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT SELECT a FROM t , b FROM foo
```

Linting the second result reports:

```
L:   1 | P:  42 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 42: Found unparsable section: 'foo'
```

### How to reproduce

From a checkout of 078bf03 with SQLFluff installed in the active environment, run from the repository root:

```sh
printf 'SELECT DISTINCT (a, b) FROM foo\n' > row.sql
PYTHONPATH=src sqlfluff fix --dialect postgres row.sql
cat row.sql

printf 'SELECT DISTINCT (SELECT a FROM t), b FROM foo\n' > sub.sql
PYTHONPATH=src sqlfluff fix --rules ST08 --dialect ansi sub.sql
cat sub.sql
PYTHONPATH=src sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi sub.sql
```

### Dialect

postgres (row constructor) and ansi (scalar subquery)

### Version

SQLFluff 4.4.0 from commit 078bf03, Python 3.12.15.

### Configuration

None beyond the `--dialect` and `--rules` flags shown.

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

issues.title: T-SQL: $action inside an expression in a MERGE OUTPUT clause fails to parse
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In a T-SQL `MERGE` statement, `OUTPUT $action` parses, but `$action` used inside an expression in the `OUTPUT` clause does not. Common forms such as `CASE $action WHEN ...`, `IIF($action = ...)` and `CASE WHEN $action = ...` all produce a parse error.

`$action` parses anywhere an expression is allowed in the `OUTPUT` clause, as SQL Server accepts ([OUTPUT clause docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/queries/output-clause-transact-sql)).


### How to reproduce

Save as `merge_output_action.sql` and run `sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql merge_output_action.sql`:

```sql
MERGE dbo.Inventory AS tgt
USING dbo.Staging AS src
    ON tgt.ProductId = src.ProductId

WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN

INTO @changes;
```

issues.title: T-SQL: LINENO statement is not supported
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

`LINENO <n>` fails to parse in the T-SQL dialect. It is usually placed at the top of a procedure body so that `ERROR_LINE()` and error messages report line numbers matching the source file. Because the failure happens inside the body, the whole `CREATE PROCEDURE` is reported as unparsable, so nothing else in the file gets linted.

### Expected Behaviour

`LINENO <n>` parses as a statement. `LINENO` is a T-SQL [reserved keyword](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/reserved-keywords-transact-sql) and SQL Server accepts it with or without a trailing semicolon.

### Observed Behaviour

Save as `lineno.sql` and run `sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql lineno.sql`:

```sql
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dbo.DoWork

BEGIN
```

issues.title: using return() values in nested macros from the same file result in rendering only inner result
lacking RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS syntax support for MariaDB
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Since version 10.5, MariaDB has supported the syntax
```sql
ALTER TABLE table_name RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS old_name TO new_name;
```

However, SQLFLUFF does not support the use of `IF EXISTS`  after `RENAME COLUMN`, so using that syntax causes a parser error.

Naively, I would first try to fix  this by inserting 
```python
Ref("IfExistsGrammar", optional=True),
```
after  `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_mariadb.py` line 1053, to make the sequence
```python
# Rename column
Sequence(
    "COLUMN",
    Ref("IfExistsGrammar", optional=True),
    Ref("ColumnReferenceSegment"),
    "TO",
    Ref("ColumnReferenceSegment"),
),
```

based off the sequence for `type = "alter_table_statement"`  beginning at line 886:
```python
  type = "alter_table_statement"
  match_grammar = Sequence(
      "ALTER",
      "TABLE",
      Ref("IfExistsGrammar", optional=True),
      Ref("TableReferenceSegment"),
      ...
```

### Expected Behaviour

I expect the query 
```sql
ALTER TABLE table_name RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS old_column_name TO new_column_name;
```
to pass the sqlfluff linter.

### Observed Behaviour

The query
```sql
ALTER TABLE table_name RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS old_column_name TO new_column_name;
```
produces a parser error 
```
Line X, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS ...
```

### How to reproduce

run .sql file with content: 
```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS example_error;

CREATE TABLE example_error (
    id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    example_column VARCHAR(15) DEFAULT NULL
) CHARACTER SET latin1 COLLATE latin1_general_ci;

ALTER TABLE example_error
RENAME COLUMN IF EXISTS example_column TO new_name;
```

### Dialect

MariaDB

### Version

Version 4.4.0, installed via pip

### Configuration

.sqlfluff:
```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = mariadb
exclude_rules = None
tab_space_size = 4
capitalisation_policy = upper
max_line_length = 120
large_file_skip_byte_limit = 0

[sqlfluff:rules:references.special_chars]
quoted_identifiers_policy = none
```

issues.title: build_lexers.py doesn't escape StringLexer templates for Rust
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the issues and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`utils/build_lexers.py` writes `StringLexer` templates into the generated Rust as a plain string literal without escaping them:

```python
if lexer_class == "StringLexer":
    ...
    template = f'"{lexer_matcher.template}"'
```

So a template containing a backslash or a double quote produces invalid Rust. For example `StringLexer("source_shorthand", "\\.", SymbolSegment)` generates `"\."`, which doesn't compile (`unknown character escape: '.'`). `RegexLexer` templates are fine because they're written as raw strings (`r#"..."#`).

I ran into this while adding the MySQL `\.` shorthand in #8693 and worked around it by using a `RegexLexer` instead. Nothing on main hits it today as far as I can see, so it only bites when someone adds a string lexer with one of those characters.

### Expected Behaviour

`StringLexer` templates are escaped (or written as raw strings like the `RegexLexer` ones), so any template that's valid in Python produces valid Rust.

### Observed Behaviour

The generated lexer fails to compile when a `StringLexer` template contains `\` or `"`.

### How to reproduce

Add a string lexer with a backslash to a dialect, e.g. in `dialect_mysql.py`:

```python
mysql_dialect.insert_lexer_matchers(
    [StringLexer("source_shorthand", "\\.", SymbolSegment)],
    before="word",
)
```

then run `python utils/rustify.py build`. The Rust build fails on the generated string.

### Dialect

Any (found with mysql).

### Version

main (36656b2).

### Configuration

N/A

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

issues.title: RF03 with single_table_references = unqualified strips outer references in subqueries of UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE, producing always-true predicates
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

With `single_table_references = unqualified`, RF03 removes the qualifiers from correlated subqueries inside UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE statements. A correlation such as `l.id = o.id` then becomes `id = id`, which is always true, so the fixed statement updates or deletes far more rows than intended.

This is the same problem as #8626, but in DML statements. PR #8627 fixes it for subqueries inside SELECT statements (APPLY / LATERAL, nested WHERE subqueries). It doesn't cover DML: RF03 treats the SELECT inside the DML statement as a top level query. That query has no parent query, so the DML target table (`orders as o` below) never counts as a visible table, and the subquery is linted as a single table select.

### Expected Behaviour

The subquery can see the target table of the DML statement, so more than one table is visible. RF03 shouldn't offer a fix that removes `o.` (or `l.`) here. Ideally it doesn't report these references at all, the same as for correlated `WHERE EXISTS (...)` subqueries in a SELECT.

### Observed Behaviour


```sql
update orders as o set x = 1 where exists (select 1 from lines as l where l.id = o.id);
-- fixed to:
update orders as o set x = 1 where exists (select 1 from lines as l where id = id);
```

```sql
update orders as o set x = (select l.x from lines as l where l.id = o.id);
-- fixed to:
update orders as o set x = (select x from lines as l where id = id);
```

```sql
delete from orders as o where exists (select 1 from lines as l where l.id = o.id);
-- fixed to:
delete from orders as o where exists (select 1 from lines as l where id = id);
```

T-SQL, `UPDATE ... FROM` with `CROSS APPLY`:

```sql
update o set x = s.j from orders as o cross apply (select l.x as j from lines as l where l.id = o.id) as s;
-- fixed to:
update o set x = s.j from orders as o cross apply (select x as j from lines as l where id = id) as s;
```

T-SQL, `MERGE`:

```sql
merge into t using s on t.id = s.id when matched then update set t.y = (select m.y from m where m.id = t.id);
-- fixed to:
merge into t using s on t.id = s.id when matched then update set t.y = (select y from m where id = id);
```

### How to reproduce

`test.sql`:

```sql
update orders as o set x = 1 where exists (select 1 from lines as l where l.id = o.id);
```

```
sqlfluff fix test.sql --dialect postgres --rules RF03
```

Use the T-SQL examples above with `--dialect tsql`.

### Dialect

Seen with postgres and tsql. RF03 handles DML statements the same way for every dialect, so others are probably affected too.

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0 (current `main`), Python 3.13.15

### Configuration

```ini
[sqlfluff:rules:references.consistent]
single_table_references = unqualified
```

issues.title: ST09 fix rewrites the null-safe equals operator <=> into >=>, producing unparsable SQL
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` with ST09 turns the null-safe equality operator `<=>` into `>=>` when it swaps the operands of a join condition, and the fixed file no longer parses.

ST09 lists `<=>` among the operators it may reorder (`src/sqlfluff/rules/structure/ST09.py`, line 79 at c9fc51c), and the existing YAML case for SparkSQL expects the operator to stay `<=>`. The inversion check (line 282 at c9fc51c) looks only at the first raw token and excludes `<>`. In dialects that lex `<=>` as three tokens, the leading `<` is inverted.

### Expected Behaviour

`ON b.y <=> a.x` becomes `ON a.x <=> b.y`, as it already does for SparkSQL and ClickHouse.

### Observed Behaviour

```sql
SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON a.x >=> b.y;
```

Linting the fixed file then reports:

```
L:   1 | P:  31 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 31: Found unparsable section: '>=> b.y'
```

This reproduces with the mysql, mariadb, hive, impala, doris and starrocks dialects. `<=` is still correctly inverted to `>=`.

### How to reproduce

With SQLFluff installed from a checkout of c9fc51c:

```sh
printf 'SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON b.y <=> a.x;\n' > t.sql
sqlfluff fix --rules ST09 --dialect mysql t.sql
cat t.sql
sqlfluff lint --dialect mysql t.sql
```

### Dialect

mysql (also mariadb, hive, impala, doris, starrocks)

### Version

SQLFluff 4.4.0 at c9fc51c, Python 3.12.15, sqlfluffrs 4.4.0 (default `use_rust_parser=auto`).

### Configuration

None beyond `--rules ST09 --dialect mysql`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: ALTER TABLE with several comma-separated actions is unparsable
issues.body:
### What Happened

ClickHouse accepts several actions in one `ALTER TABLE`, separated by commas. SQLFluff's
ClickHouse dialect parses only the first action and marks the rest unparsable.

### Expected Behaviour

The statement parses as one `alter_table_statement` containing both actions.

### Observed Behaviour

```
L:   1 | P:  39 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 39: Found unparsable section: ', ADD COLUMN b
                       | UInt8;'
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
ALTER TABLE example ADD COLUMN a UInt8, ADD COLUMN b UInt8;
```

```sh
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse example.sql
```

ClickHouse's own parser reads the actions as a comma-separated list
(`ParserAlterCommandList::parseImpl` in
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Parsers/ParserAlterQuery.cpp).
`AlterTableStatementSegment` in `dialect_clickhouse.py` ends in a single `OneOf(...)` of
actions, so a second action cannot match.

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

4.4.0, and main at c9fc51cab9.

### Proposed fix

https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/pull/8708

issues.title: Needs support for Postgres ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION AS
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

I'm writing migrations to change the generated column expression in a Postgres table

```sql
ALTER TABLE message_events
ALTER COLUMN guild_id
SET EXPRESSION AS ((raw_data ->> 'guild_id')::BIGINT);
```

SQLFluff reports this as unparsable.

### Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff should handle [the documented syntax](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-altertable.html#SQL-ALTERTABLE-DESC-SET-EXPRESSION) correctly.

### Observed Behaviour

```
sqlfluff lint --verbose migrations/20261010182608_message-logging_table_guild_id_improvement.down.sql 
==== sqlfluff ====
sqlfluff:                4.3.0 python:                3.13.11
implementation:        cpython verbosity:                   1
dialect:              postgres templater:               jinja
rules:                                all
==== readout ====

== [migrations/20261010182608_message-logging_table_guild_id_improvement.down.sql] FAIL
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'ALTER
                       | TABLE message_events\nALTER COLUMN ...'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'postgres'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
==== summary ====
violations:        1 status:         FAIL
All Finished 📜 🎉!

```

### How to reproduce

The table was originally created in this migration, which SQLFluff can handle just fine:

```sql
CREATE TABLE message_events (
    id BIGSERIAL NOT NULL,
    raw_data JSONB NOT NULL,
    additional_data JSONB,
    -- message_id SHOULD never be null. but we're getting it from Discord and I'd rather store an invalid json blob than reject something.
    message_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((raw_data ->> 'id')::BIGINT) STORED,
    -- channel_id SHOULD never be null. but we're getting it from Discord and I'd rather store an invalid json blob than reject something.
    channel_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((raw_data ->> 'channel_id')::BIGINT) STORED,
    -- guild_id can in fact be null
    guild_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((raw_data ->> 'guild_id')::BIGINT) STORED,
    -- user_id can be null if it's a message_delete event, but for this reason we have the additional_data column.
    user_id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (COALESCE((raw_data #>> '{author,id}')::BIGINT, (additional_data #>> '{author_id}')::BIGINT)) STORED,
    -- this is when we received the message event. it may approximate a timestamp in the message json, but is not guaranteed to be equal.
    received_at TIMESTAMP(3) WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    event_kind VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_message_events PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
```

I'm adding a migration which changes the generation expression for the `guild_id` field:

```sql
ALTER TABLE message_events
ALTER COLUMN guild_id
SET EXPRESSION AS (COALESCE((additional_data #>> '{guild_id}')::BIGINT, (raw_data ->> 'guild_id')::BIGINT));
```

And, of course, the "down" migration to change it back:

```sql
ALTER TABLE message_events
ALTER COLUMN guild_id
SET EXPRESSION AS ((raw_data ->> 'guild_id')::BIGINT);
```

Postgres (version 18.6) runs these migrations just fine. But SQLFluff can't handle them.


### Dialect

Postgres

### Version

- sqlfluff, version 4.3.0
- Python 3.13.11 (main, Dec 25 2025, 14:02:48) [Clang 17.0.0 (clang-1700.6.3.2)] on darwin

```
[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.identifiers]

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.functions]
extended_capitalisation_policy = lower
[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.literals]
capitalisation_policy = upper
[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.types]
extended_capitalisation_policy = upper

[sqlfluff:rules:convention.not_equal]

preferred_not_equal_style = c_style
```

issues.title: Snowflake - CASE statement indent broken, doesn't even match fixture
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

LT02 wants the `WHEN`/`ELSE` branches of a Snowflake scripting `CASE` statement at the same level as `CASE`.  This is the opposite of what everything else does.

Below is what is generally correct, but rejected by LT02 on snowflake.
```sql
BEGIN
    CASE (v)
        WHEN 1 THEN
            x := 2;
        ELSE
            x := 3;
    END CASE;
END;
```

`sqlfluff lint --dialect snowflake --rules LT02` flags every line inside the `CASE`, and `fix` pulls `WHEN`/`ELSE` back to `CASE`'s column. Snowflake's own fixture is written the indented way, and LT02 flags its `CASE` statements too (`test/fixtures/dialects/snowflake/scripting_control_flow.sql`, around lines 72, 86 and 155).

`WHILE`, `IF` and `REPEAT` in the same dialect indent their bodies fine, and the `CASE` expression (ansi) and Oracle's `CASE` statement indent `WHEN` under `CASE`. It looks like `ScriptingCaseStatementSegment` just has no `Indent` between the case value and the first `WHEN`:
https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/375ea6550f40/src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_snowflake.py#L11770

Probably an `Indent` after the optional case value and a `Dedent` before `END`, plus LT02 tests. Similar to #8452 (EXCEPTION indentation).


### Expected Behaviour

SEE What Happened.

### Observed Behaviour

See What Happened.

### How to reproduce

It's obvious in the code on HEAD.

### Dialect

It's obvious in the code on HEAD.

issues.title: BigQuery - More options for Chained Function Calls
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### Description

In BigQuery, you can use [chained function calls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-reference#chained-function-calls) which makes repeated function call much easier to read:

```sql
SELECT
    -- Traditional way
    REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(foo, 'a', '0'), 'b', '1'), 'c', '2') AS foo,

    -- Chained calls way
    (foo)
    .REPLACE('a', '0')
    .REPLACE('b', '1')
    .REPLACE('c', '2') AS bar;
```

Those produces the same output. However, readability can be damaged by not using linebreaks, or lack of indentation.

### Use case

Having a way to force different layout styles would be really nice:

```sql
SELECT
  -- One-liner
  (foo).REPLACE('a', '0').REPLACE('b', '1').REPLACE('c', '2') AS foo,

  -- Aligned linebreaks
  (foo)
  .REPLACE('a', '0')
  .REPLACE('b', '1')
  .REPLACE('c', '2') AS bar,

  -- Indented linebreaks
  (foo)
    .REPLACE('a', '0')
    .REPLACE('b', '1')
    .REPLACE('c', '2') AS baz;
```


We could have a rule such as:

```ini
[sqlfluff:rules:layout.chained_functions]
# one of 'consistent', 'one_liner', 'aligned', 'indented'
writing_style = consistent
```

---

This example show how much better chained function calls can be:

```sql
SELECT
  -- Before
  REPLACE(
    REPLACE(
      REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
          LOWER(
            TRIM(
              adresse
            )
          ),
          'ch',
          'chemin'
        ),
        'av',
        'avenue'
      ),
      'bd',
      'boulevard'
    ),
    'bvd',
    'boulevard'
  ) AS adresse_clean,

  -- after - one-liner
  (adresse).TRIM().LOWER().REPLACE('ch', 'chemin').REPLACE('av', 'avenue').REPLACE('bd', 'boulevard').REPLACE('bvd', 'boulevard') AS adresse_clean,
  
  -- after - aligned linebreaks
  (adresse)
  .TRIM()
  .LOWER()
  .REPLACE('ch', 'chemin')
  .REPLACE('av', 'avenue')
  .REPLACE('bd', 'boulevard')
  .REPLACE('bvd', 'boulevard') AS adresse_clean,

  -- after - indented linebreaks
  (adresse)
    .TRIM()
    .LOWER()
    .REPLACE('ch', 'chemin')
    .REPLACE('av', 'avenue')
    .REPLACE('bd', 'boulevard')
    .REPLACE('bvd', 'boulevard') AS adresse_clean;
```

- BigQuery

issues.title: LT09 single-target SELECT + DISTINCT + trailing comment: fix breaks the select statement
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

If a single-target `SELECT` statement has `DISTINCT` and a trailing comment on the first line, the fix wrongly moves the select target after the comment.

This also happens with other modifiers like `ALL` and `TOP 10` (Snowflake dialect).

### Expected Behaviour

It should either:
1. keep the select target on the following line regardless of policy
2. move the select target after the modifier but before before the comment
3. mark as unfixable

My preference is for 1, but that's probably a change to the intent of LT09.

### Observed Behaviour

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT -- comment
    A
FROM TBL;
```

becomes

### What Happened

issues.title: RF03 with `single_table_references = unqualified` strips outer reference inside T-SQL `APPLY` subquery, producing always-true predicate
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

With `single_table_references = unqualified`, `sqlfluff fix` (rule RF03) removes the table qualifier from a correlated reference inside a T-SQL `OUTER APPLY` / `CROSS APPLY` subquery. The reference points to a table in the outer query, but RF03 treats the subquery as a single-table select and unqualifies it. The fixed SQL still parses, but its meaning changes: `a.patientid = s.patientid` becomes `patientid = patientid`, which is always true (for non-null values).

Other rules then make it worse. After RF03, AL05 removes the now-unused alias `a`. ST05 (`forbid_subquery_in = both`) then moves the subquery, which no longer looks correlated, into a CTE. On its own, ST05 correctly leaves the correlated subquery alone.

### Expected Behaviour

RF03 must not unqualify references to tables outside the current select, such as the outer query of an `APPLY`. For the same pattern with `WHERE EXISTS (...)`, RF03 keeps `s.patientid` correctly. `APPLY` should behave the same.

### Observed Behaviour

Input:

```sql
select s.patientid
from dbo.spoed as s
outer apply (
    select top 1 1 as heeft_afspraak
    from dbo.afspraken as a
    where a.patientid = s.patientid
) as lg
```

After `sqlfluff fix --rules RF03`:

```sql
select s.patientid
from dbo.spoed as s
outer apply (
    select top 1 1 as heeft_afspraak
    from dbo.afspraken as a
    where patientid = patientid
) as lg
```

`sqlfluff lint --rules RF03` reports:

```
L:   6 | P:  11 | RF03 | Qualified reference 'a.patientid' found in single table select. [references.consistent]
L:   6 | P:  26 | RF03 | Qualified reference 's.patientid' found in single table select. [references.consistent]
```

After `sqlfluff fix --rules RF03,AL05,ST05` (with `forbid_subquery_in = both`):

```sql
with lg as (
    select top 1 1 as heeft_afspraak
    from dbo.afspraken
    where patientid = patientid
)
select s.patientid
from dbo.spoed as s
outer apply lg
```

`CROSS APPLY` gives the same result. With the default `single_table_references = consistent`, RF03 does not change the file.

### How to reproduce

`.sqlfluff`:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = tsql

[sqlfluff:rules]
single_table_references = unqualified
```

Save the input above as `repro.sql`, then run:

```
sqlfluff fix repro.sql --rules RF03
```

### Dialect

tsql

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0, Python 3.13.15

### Configuration

The `.sqlfluff` shown above. Add `[sqlfluff:rules:structure.subquery]` with `forbid_subquery_in = both` to reproduce the ST05 step.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!
