issues.title: LT05 and LT09 loop forever on a single-target SELECT longer than max_line_length
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` **never converges** for a `SELECT` with a single target that is longer than `max_line_length`. **LT05** and **LT09** (both enabled in the default rule set) undo each other's fix on every run, so repeated runs flip the file between two states forever:

```sql
-- state A
SELECT a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;
-- state B
SELECT
    a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;
```

A → B → A → B … indefinitely. `sqlfluff fix` reports the file as fixed each time, so `sqlfluff fix --check` in CI never passes and a pre-commit hook would rewrite the file on every commit.

The telling part is that **state B is still 86 characters** — LT05's own output does not satisfy LT05. LT05 breaks after `SELECT` and leaves the (still too long) target on its own line; LT09 then sees a single select target on its own line and pulls it back up, per its default `single_target_policy = same_line`.

### How to reproduce

```sh
$ printf 'SELECT a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;\n' > q.sql
$ for i in 1 2 3; do sqlfluff fix --dialect postgres --rules LT05,LT09 -f q.sql; cat q.sql; done
```

Observed (82 chars in, alternating 82/86 out):

```
SELECT a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;
SELECT
    a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;
SELECT a_really_long_column_name_that_goes_past_the_limit_okay AS alias_padding_x;
```

A natural trigger from real code (found in this repo's own fixtures, `test/fixtures/dialects/postgres/select.sql`, 85 chars):

```sql
SELECT timestamp with time zone '2025-11-20 00:00:00+00' AT TIME ZONE 'Africa/Cairo';
```

### Scope

- **Rules:** minimal set is exactly **LT05 + LT09** (found by greedily removing rules from the full rule set while the loop persisted). Each rule alone converges.
- **Dialects:** reproduced on `postgres`, `ansi`, `bigquery`, `snowflake`, `mysql`, `duckdb` and `tsql` — so this is reflow behaviour, not dialect-specific.
- **Conditions:** the line must exceed `max_line_length` (80) and the `SELECT` must have exactly **one** target. Two or more targets converge, and lines within the limit are untouched.

### Candidate directions

I don't have a strong preference between these, and the fix touches reflow, so I'd rather not guess:

1. **LT05 shouldn't emit a break that leaves the line over the limit** — either pick a different break point (e.g. before `AS`) or report the line as unfixable, consistent with the other "unfixable" guards in `reindent.py`.
2. **LT09 shouldn't re-join a select target when the resulting line still exceeds `max_line_length`.**

`rules.layout.select_targets.single_target_policy` is relevant context here, but I couldn't get an override to apply through the Python API quickly enough to verify whether `new_line` avoids the loop, so please treat that as unverified.

Related but distinct: #8389 (cycle of LT09/LT14/LT02 for tsql function keywords). This one is LT05/LT09, no dialect-specific constructs.

### Dialect

Any — `postgres` used above.

### Configuration

Defaults (LT05 and LT09 are both in the default rule set).

### Version

```
sqlfluff, version 4.3.0
```

Measured on `main` at `2e2275713`, Python 3.13.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [X] Yes I am willing to submit a PR! (once the maintainers pick a direction — happy to add the regression test either way)

### AI assistance disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING.md ("AI-Assisted Contributions"): this report was drafted with AI assistance. I validated it manually: reproduced the loop through the CLI and the Python API, minimised the rule set by greedy removal, checked seven dialects, and confirmed the boundary conditions (single target only, over the limit only, converges with each rule alone and with multiple targets).

issues.title: LT01 removes the space between `VARIADIC` and `ARRAY`, corrupting variadic array literal arguments
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` with **LT01** (enabled by default) **corrupts** a variadic array literal argument in the `postgres` dialect by deleting the space between `VARIADIC` and `ARRAY`, fusing the two keywords into a single identifier:

```sql
-- in
SELECT f(VARIADIC ARRAY[1, 2]);
-- out
SELECT f(VARIADICARRAY[1, 2]);
```

`VARIADICARRAY` is no longer the same token: before the fix `VARIADIC` is a `keyword` and `ARRAY` is an `array_type`, afterwards the pair parses as one `naked_identifier`. The query changes meaning (and stops being a variadic call). The fix is reported as applied and `sqlfluff fix` exits 0.

The named-argument form is mangled too:

```
SELECT f(VARIADIC arr := ARRAY[1, 2]);  ->  SELECT f(VARIADICarr:=ARRAY[1, 2]);
```

### How to reproduce

```sh
$ printf 'SELECT f(VARIADIC ARRAY[1, 2]);\n' > v.sql
$ sqlfluff fix --dialect postgres --rules LT01 -f v.sql
== [v.sql] FIXED
$ cat v.sql
SELECT f(VARIADICARRAY[1, 2]);
```

Verified with LT01 alone (no other rules involved). Also reproduces with the default rule set. Affected dialects: **postgres**, **redshift** and **duckdb** (the three I checked where `VARIADIC` is a keyword). `ansi`, `snowflake` and `trino` don't fuse it, because `VARIADIC` isn't a keyword there.

Unaffected, for contrast: `SELECT f(ARRAY[1, 2]);`, `SELECT ARRAY[1, 2];` and `SELECT f(VARIADIC arr);` are all left alone.

### Cause

`TypedArrayLiteralSegment` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_postgres.py:7424` extends the ansi segment by inserting the optional variadic prefix **inside** the segment:

```python
match_grammar = ansi.TypedArrayLiteralSegment.match_grammar.copy(
    insert=[
        Sequence(
            Ref.keyword("VARIADIC"),
            Sequence(Ref("NakedIdentifierSegment"), Ref("WalrusOperatorSegment"), optional=True),
            optional=True,
        )
    ],
    before=Ref("ArrayTypeSegment"),
)
```

The parse tree is therefore:

```
expression:
    typed_array_literal:
        keyword: 'VARIADIC'
        whitespace: ' '
        array_type:
            keyword: 'ARRAY'
            array_literal: ...
```

while `src/sqlfluff/core/default_config.cfg:228` sets

```
[sqlfluff:layout:type:typed_array_literal]
spacing_within = touch
```

`spacing_within` spans from the first to the last token of the segment, so "touch" now also applies at the `VARIADIC` / `ARRAY` boundary and LT01 deletes that space. The `array_literal` is a *sibling* of `array_type`, not a child, so `array_type`'s own `spacing_within` can't be relied on to keep `ARRAY[...]` tight instead.

### Two fixes I tried that don't work

1. **Dropping the `typed_array_literal` layout section.** Fixes the corruption but regresses the intended tightening from #5005: `SELECT ARRAY[1, 2];` becomes `SELECT ARRAY [1, 2];`.
2. **Wrapping the prefix in its own segment** (new `variadic_array_literal_prefix` type + `spacing_after = single`). The parent's `spacing_within` still wins at that boundary, so `VARIADIC ARRAY` is still fused, and the `:=` boundary then loses its space instead (`VARIADIC arr :=ARRAY[1, 2]`).

So the usable direction seems to be to keep `VARIADIC` **outside** the `typed_array_literal` segment — e.g. a `variadic_array_literal` (or prefix) segment referenced from the same places that reference `TypedArrayLiteralSegment`, so `typed_array_literal` again covers exactly `ARRAY` + `[...]` and its `spacing_within = touch` applies only there. That's a grammar change across the reference sites, so I'd rather not guess at it: happy to implement it if you point me at the preferred shape, or to try a narrower variant you prefer.

### Dialect

postgres (also redshift, duckdb).

### Configuration

None. LT01 is enabled by default.

### Version

```
sqlfluff, version 4.3.0
```
Measured on `main` at `2e2275713`.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [X] Yes I am willing to submit a PR! (pending direction on the fix shape above — I'd rather not submit a speculative grammar change)

### AI assistance disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING.md ("AI-Assisted Contributions"): this report was drafted with AI assistance. I validated it manually — reproduced the corruption through the CLI, confirmed the before/after segment types with the parser API, checked the three affected dialects plus three unaffected ones, and tried both candidate fixes above to confirm they don't work. I'm happy to provide the test cases I used for the dialect matrix.

issues.title: LT02: `sqlfluff fix` oscillates forever on nested Jinja block tags that share a source line
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` never converges for this file. It alternates between two states forever, and both states still contain LT02 violations, so a `fix` run followed by a `lint` run keeps finding the same indentation problem, with the file rewritten on every pass.

### Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff fix` reaches a fixed point: a second `fix` pass changes nothing, and `sqlfluff lint` on the result reports no LT02 violations.

### Observed Behaviour

```sh
cat > osc.sql <<'EOF'
select
{% if true %}{% if false %}    a,
{% endif %}{% endif %}    b
EOF
sqlfluff fix osc.sql --dialect ansi -f
```

Pass 1 produces:

```sql
select
    {% if true %}
        {% if false %}    a,
        {% endif %}{% endif %}    b
```

Pass 2 produces:

```sql
select
{% if true %}
    {% if false %}    a,
        {% endif %}{% endif %}    b
```

Pass 3 produces the pass 1 output again, pass 4 the pass 2 output, and so on. Each `fix` exits 0 and reports the violations as fixed.

`sqlfluff lint` on either state still reports two LT02 violations, and each state contradicts the other:

| state | line 2 | line 3 | LT02 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (after pass 1) | `    {% if true %}` | `        {% if false %}    a,` | `Line should not be indented.` / `Expected indent of 4 spaces.` |
| B (after pass 2) | `{% if true %}` | `    {% if false %}    a,` | `Expected indent of 4 spaces.` / `Expected indent of 8 spaces.` |

So state A says line 2 must be at indent 0 and line 3 at indent 4 -- exactly what pass 2 produced -- and state B says line 2 must be at indent 4 and line 3 at indent 8 -- exactly what pass 1 produced.

With `--logger rules -vvvv` on state A:

```
DEBUG  Correcting indent @ line 2. Expected: ''. Found '    '
DEBUG  Correcting indent @ line 3. Expected: '    '. Found '        '
```

Note this is not only a whitespace oscillation: pass 1 also moves the `{% if %}` tags onto their own lines, which pass 2 then moves back.

### How to reproduce

The file above is the whole reproducer. The API form is:

```python
from sqlfluff import fix
from sqlfluff.core import FluffConfig

sql = "select\n{% if true %}{% if false %}    a,\n{% endif %}{% endif %}    b\n"
cfg = FluffConfig(overrides={"dialect": "ansi"})
state = sql
for _ in range(3):
    state = fix(state, config=cfg)
    print(state)
```

The third result equals the first.

### Controls

| variant | result |
| --- | --- |
| the reproducer | **oscillates** |
| same file with `--rules LT02` only | **oscillates** |
| same file with `--dialect postgres` / `--dialect snowflake` | **oscillates** |
| inner tag changed to `{% if true %}` | converges |
| single level `{% if true %}` ... `{% endif %}` | converges |
| outer tag changed to `{% for %}` | converges |
| dropping the trailing `b` line content | converges |

So the trigger is: two opening block tags on the same source line, where the inner block is skipped by the templater, plus content after the inner closing tag.

### Cause

`sqlfluff render` shows two variants here -- one where the `{% if false %}` body is dropped and one where it is kept -- and both render the remaining content at indent 4:

```
Variant 1:      Variant 2:
select          select
    b              a,
from t           b
                 from t
```

Both variants agree that the content belongs at indent 4, but the indentation of the two template tags on lines 2 and 3 comes out differently depending on which state the file is in, which is what makes the fix flip. The relevant code looks like the block-tag handling in `src/sqlfluff/utils/reflow/reindent.py` (`_revise_templated_lines()` and the `block_start` / `block_end` cases that compute indent balances), but I have not pinned down the exact line yet.

### Impact

For anyone running `sqlfluff fix` in CI or through a pre-commit hook, the file is rewritten on every run and the violations never go away, so `sqlfluff lint` after a `fix` still fails. The file also never settles, so the diff noise continues indefinitely.

### Dialect

ansi. Confirmed identical with postgres and snowflake.

### Version

- sqlfluff 4.3.0 (released) and `main` at `2e22757`
- Python 3.13
- macOS and Linux both reproduce

### Configuration

None. Plain `--dialect ansi` with the default configuration, no `.sqlfluff` file.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

I can put together the failing case as a regression test and attempt a fix. Since this sits in the templated indentation code, which has a lot of edge cases, I would rather agree on the approach first -- in particular whether the expectation is that the two tags end up at the same indent, or that the fix stops re-indenting them at all -- before I change anything.

### AI assistance disclosure

Per the project's contributing guidance: this report was prepared with AI assistance. I built it by running a small harness that checks whether `sqlfluff fix` reaches a fixed point, over a corpus of Jinja-templated SQL snippets; everything quoted above (the two states, the lint output, the debug log lines, the controls, the versions) was produced by executing that harness against the released 4.3.0 and against `main`, and I checked each claim manually.

issues.title: LT05 leaves part of a comment as SQL when the comment contains a Jinja tag
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

LT05 moves a long trailing comment to a new line above the code. When the comment contains a Jinja tag, this fix corrupts the file. `sqlfluff fix` prints a warning, reports the file as fixed and exits with 0.

The moved copy of the comment has no tags, because LT05 builds it from the rendered text. The original comment is deleted only up to the first tag. The result depends on the tag:

- `{% if %}`, `{% endif %}` and `{# ... #}`: the text from the first tag to the end of the comment stays on the code line. The parser then reads it as SQL (q1.sql, q3.sql).
- `{% set %}` and `{{ ... }}`: no part of the original comment is deleted. The file has the comment twice, and the line is still too long (q2.sql). Each new run of `sqlfluff fix` adds one more copy.

LT05 also counts each tag in the comment twice. q3.sql is 77 characters long, but LT05 reports `84 > 80`. So the fix also corrupts a line which is not too long.

This is not #8611. In #8611, the token which spans the tag stays in the file, and a fix next to it deletes the start of the token. Here LT05 deletes the comment token itself. #8615 does not change the output for the three files below.

### Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff fix` keeps all of the comment text and its tags. If LT05 cannot move a comment with its tags, it does not move it and reports the line as unfixable. LT05 does not report q3.sql, because the line is 77 characters long.

### Observed Behaviour

The command in "How to reproduce" prints this and exits with 0:

```
WARNING    Skipping edit patch on uncertain templated section [('mid_point', slice(35, 53, None))], Please report this warning on GitHub along with the query that produced it.
WARNING    Skipping edit patch on uncertain templated section [('mid_point', slice(53, 101, None))], Please report this warning on GitHub along with the query that produced it.
== [q1.sql] FAIL
L:   1 | P:   1 | LT05 | Line is too long (125 > 80). [layout.long_lines]
== [q1.sql] FIXED
WARNING    Skipping edit patch on uncertain templated section [('mid_point', slice(25, 99, None))], Please report this warning on GitHub along with the query that produced it.
== [q2.sql] FAIL
L:   1 | P:   1 | LT05 | Line is too long (114 > 80). [layout.long_lines]
== [q2.sql] FIXED
WARNING    Skipping edit patch on uncertain templated section [('mid_point', slice(16, 77, None))], Please report this warning on GitHub along with the query that produced it.
== [q3.sql] FAIL
L:   1 | P:   1 | LT05 | Line is too long (84 > 80). [layout.long_lines]
== [q3.sql] FIXED
3 fixable linting violations found
```

The files are then:

q1.sql keeps `{% if true %} more{% endif %} text here that goes on and on and on` as SQL:

```sql
-- comment more text here that goes on and on and on
select a, b, c from tbl  {% if true %} more{% endif %} text here that goes on and on and on
```

q2.sql has the comment twice:

```sql
-- comment more text here that goes on and on and on and on
select a, b, c from tbl  -- comment{% set q = 1 %} more text here that goes on and on and on and on
```

q3.sql keeps `{# x #} this comment text ...` as SQL:

```sql
-- note this comment text is long enough to put the line over
select 1 {# x #} this comment text is long enough to put the line over
```

`sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi` then reports `PRS` for q1.sql and q3.sql. In q1.sql, `more` becomes a table alias (AL01, AL05). In q3.sql, `this` becomes a column alias (AL02). For q2.sql it reports `Line is too long (114 > 80)` again.

**Cause.** `_fix_long_line_with_comment` in `src/sqlfluff/utils/reflow/reindent.py` deletes the comment segment and creates a copy of it before the line. The `raw` of the segment is the rendered text, so the copy has no tags.

The lexer yields the placeholder for each tag, and the indent or dedent meta of a block tag, before the comment token. Their templated positions are inside the comment. After the delete, `_iter_templated_patches` in `src/sqlfluff/core/linter/patch.py` splits the deletion of the comment at each of these segments. For q1.sql, the parts are the source slices `25:35`, `35:53` and `53:101`. `generate_source_patches` keeps `25:35`, because it is all literal. It skips the other two parts with the warning, because they contain a tag.

The #7582 guard skips the `templated` placeholder of a `{% set %}` tag. The deletion is then one part, `25:99` in q2.sql. That part contains the tag, so it is skipped whole. A `{{ ... }}` tag gives the same result.

The normal break path of LT05 checks `_is_templated_safe_break` (#7640). `_fix_long_line_with_comment` has no such check. One possible fix: do not move a comment when `comment_seg.pos_marker.is_literal()` is false, and report the line as unfixable.

### How to reproduce

```sh
cat > q1.sql <<'EOF'
select a, b, c from tbl  -- comment{% if true %} more{% endif %} text here that goes on and on and on
EOF
cat > q2.sql <<'EOF'
select a, b, c from tbl  -- comment{% set q = 1 %} more text here that goes on and on and on and on
EOF
cat > q3.sql <<'EOF'
select 1 -- note{# x #} this comment text is long enough to put the line over
EOF
sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules LT05 q1.sql q2.sql q3.sql
```

### Dialect

ansi. postgres gives the same output for q1.sql. The default rule set gives the same comment damage in q1.sql.

### Version

```
sqlfluff, version 4.3.0
Python 3.12.14
```

Measured on `main` at `2e2275713`. The `4.3.0` release and #8615 at `282bb2f69` give the same output for the three files.

### Configuration

None. There is no `.sqlfluff` file. The command line gives the dialect and the rule, and the templater is the default `jinja`.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issues.title: Rust parser diverges from Python parser on Databricks `INSERT ... REPLACE ON <condition> (subquery)`
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Databricks supports `INSERT INTO ... REPLACE ON <boolean_expression>` where the source can be either a normal query or a parenthesized query with an optional source alias:

```text
REPLACE ON boolean_expression
{ (query) [source_alias] | query }
```

I originally worked on aligning the Databricks `INSERT` grammar with the documented syntax in #8264. During review, it was identified that the parenthesized query form after `REPLACE ON` did not parse correctly.

I am working on the follow-up fix in [timothyvries/sqlfluff#5](https://github.com/timothyvries/sqlfluff/pull/5).

The underlying problem is that `ExpressionSegment` used for the `REPLACE ON` condition can consume the opening parenthesis of the following query. For example:

```sql
INSERT INTO TABLE students AS t
REPLACE ON t.name = s.name
(SELECT * FROM people) AS s;
```

Without a boundary between the condition and the query, the parser can interpret the parenthesis as belonging to the preceding identifier, effectively treating it like:

```text
s.name(SELECT ...)
```

rather than treating `t.name = s.name` as the complete boolean expression followed by a separate parenthesized query.

My current fix bounds the expression using `ParseMode.GREEDY` and terminators (before i also tried with SelectableGrammar instead of individual terminators) for tokens that can start the following query:

```python
Sequence(
    Ref("ExpressionSegment"),
    parse_mode=ParseMode.GREEDY,
    terminators=[
        Ref.keyword("SELECT"),
        Ref.keyword("VALUES"),
        Ref.keyword("WITH"),
        Ref("StartBracketSegment"),
    ],
),
Ref("SelectableGrammar"),
```

This produces the intended parse with the Python parser and the Python dialect parse suite passes.

However, when the same fixture is run using the Rust parser, it produces a different parse result and the Rust-backed CI suite fails.

I am therefore looking for guidance on either restructuring this grammar so that both parser implementations behave consistently, or identifying why the Rust parser handles this boundary differently.

### Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff's Databricks dialect should support the documented `INSERT ... REPLACE ON` forms, including both an unparenthesized query:

```sql
INSERT INTO TABLE students AS t
REPLACE ON t.name = s.name
SELECT * FROM people AS s;
```

and a parenthesized query with an optional source alias:

```sql
INSERT INTO TABLE students AS t
REPLACE ON t.name = s.name
(SELECT * FROM people) AS s;
```

In the second example, the parse tree should treat:

```text
t.name = s.name
```

as the `REPLACE ON` boolean expression, and:

```text
(SELECT * FROM people) AS s
```

as the source query and its alias.

The Python and Rust parser implementations should produce equivalent parse trees for this syntax.

### Observed Behaviour

Without explicitly bounding the `REPLACE ON` expression, the opening parenthesis of the following query can be consumed as part of `ExpressionSegment`.

This causes the parser to interpret the query as though it were function arguments attached to the final identifier of the condition rather than as the separate source query.

I can prevent this on the Python side by making the condition a greedy sequence with query-start terminators. With the current implementation in  [timothyvries/sqlfluff#5](https://github.com/timothyvries/sqlfluff/pull/5):

- the Python parser parses the statement correctly;
- the Python dialect parse suite succeeds;
- the generated Python fixture represents the condition and parenthesized query separately;
- the Rust-backed parser suite does not produce the same result and fails in CI.

So the remaining blocker is parser parity between the Python and Rust implementations for this grammar.

### How to reproduce

The minimal SQL example is:

```sql
INSERT INTO TABLE students AS t
REPLACE ON t.name = s.name
(SELECT * FROM people) AS s;
```

This is also covered by the Databricks `insert_into.sql` fixture in  [timothyvries/sqlfluff#5](https://github.com/timothyvries/sqlfluff/pull/5).

On the `feature/bynamereplace` branch, the relevant grammar currently uses:

```python
Sequence(
    Ref("ExpressionSegment"),
    parse_mode=ParseMode.GREEDY,
    terminators=[
        Ref.keyword("SELECT"),
        Ref.keyword("VALUES"),
        Ref.keyword("WITH"),
        Ref("StartBracketSegment"),
    ],
),
Ref("SelectableGrammar"),
```

The standard Python dialect parse suite succeeds, while the equivalent Rust-backed dialect test fails in CI.

The relevant work is:

- Original Databricks `INSERT` implementation: #8264
- Current follow-up / reproduction:  [timothyvries/sqlfluff#5](https://github.com/timothyvries/sqlfluff/pull/5)
- Branch: feature/bynamereplace

### Dialect

databricks

### Version

SQLFluff 4.3.0

The current reproduction is against the source branch feature/bynamereplace in  [timothyvries/sqlfluff#5](https://github.com/timothyvries/sqlfluff/pull/5).

The failing CI run uses Python 3.14 for the dialect parse suite, with the Rust parser (sqlfluffrs 4.3.0).

### Configuration

No special configuration is required.

The issue is in the dialect/parser grammar and does not depend on templating or linting-rule configuration.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issues.title: `sqlfluff fix` deletes source text when a token spans a Jinja tag
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` deletes source text when a token spans a Jinja tag. A token spans a tag when the rendered SQL joins the text on both sides of the tag. For example, `b{% if true %}c{% endif %}` renders as the one identifier `bc`.

A fix deletes the part of such a token before the tag in two cases:

- The fix puts a new segment directly before the token. LT02 does this in q1.sql, and LT05 does it in q3.sql and q4.sql.
- The fix changes another segment in the same clause. In q2.sql, LT01 removes the spaces before the comma. The space before `b` does not change, but the `b` is deleted. `select b{% if true %}c{% endif %}, a  , x` loses its `b` too, with the fix after the token.

`sqlfluff fix` reports the violation as fixed and exits with 0. After the fix, `sqlfluff lint` with the same rule reports nothing.

I found this with LT05 and a skipped `{% if false %}` block. A skipped block is not necessary. LT01 and LT02 delete text in the same way with `{% if true %}`.

### Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff fix` keeps all source text which is not whitespace. For q1.sql below, the expected output is:

```sql
select
    b{% if true %}c{% endif %}
```

For q2.sql it is `select a, b{% if true %}c{% endif %}`. If a fix cannot keep the text, `sqlfluff fix` does not apply it and reports the violation as unfixable.

### Observed Behaviour

Each command in "How to reproduce" prints `FIXED` for its files and exits with 0. The files are then:

q1.sql loses the `b`:

```sql
select
    {% if true %}c{% endif %}
```

q2.sql loses the `b`:

```sql
select a, {% if true %}c{% endif %}
```

q3.sql loses the comment `-- trailing comment here`:

```sql
select a, b, c
from tbl
{% if false %} xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx{% endif %}
```

q4.sql loses the 65 `a` characters:

```sql
{% if false %}
    select
{% endif %}select 1
```

`sqlfluff render` shows the column `bc` in q1.sql and q2.sql before the fix, and `c` after it. With the default rules, q1.sql, q3.sql and q4.sql lose the same text. q2.sql instead gets a second `{% if true %}` tag, and `sqlfluff render` then fails with `Failed to parse Jinja syntax`.

q3.sql is the `trailing_comment` test input in #8605. `main` without #8605 gives the same output, so the loss does not come from #8605.

**Cause.** The lexer yields the placeholder for a tag before the token which spans the tag. The code is `_iter_segments` in `src/sqlfluff/core/parser/lexer.py`. The placeholder and its indent or dedent meta then sit between the whitespace and the token. Their templated position is after the start of the token. Two functions use that position as the end of a source range, so the range covers the start of the token:

- `BaseSegment._position_segments` in `src/sqlfluff/core/parser/segments/base.py` positions a new segment up to the next sibling with a position. In q1.sql, the new indent from LT02 gets source slice `7:8`, which is the `b`. The new newline from LT05 gets source slice `23:49` in q3.sql and `20:86` in q4.sql.
- `_iter_templated_patches` in `src/sqlfluff/core/linter/patch.py` walks into each parent segment which has a change. It treats the gap before the placeholder as a deletion. In q2.sql, the parent is the `select_clause`. It yields a `mid_point` patch for source slice `12:13`, which is the `b`.

#7582 added a guard at both places for #6261. The guard skips only a `templated` placeholder which renders to an empty string. Here the placeholder is for a `block_start` or `block_end` tag. `generate_source_patches` then keeps the patch, because its source slice is inside one literal slice. In q3.sql and q4.sql, the token spans the tag only in the variant which renders the `{% if false %}` block.

The guard does not cover a Jinja comment either. With LT01, `select a  , b{# note #}c` loses its `b`. A `{% set x = 1 %}` tag gives a `templated` placeholder, and the guard keeps the `b`. The indent or dedent meta of the tag has the same templated position as its placeholder. With the guard widened to `block_start`, `block_end` and `comment` placeholders, q2.sql and q4.sql still lose their text.

### How to reproduce

```sh
cat > q1.sql <<'EOF'
select
b{% if true %}c{% endif %}
EOF
cat > q2.sql <<'EOF'
select a  , b{% if true %}c{% endif %}
EOF
cat > q3.sql <<'EOF'
select a, b, c from tbl  -- trailing comment here{% if false %} xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx{% endif %}
EOF
cat > q4.sql <<'EOF'
{% if false %}select aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa{% endif %}select 1
EOF
sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules LT02 q1.sql
sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules LT01 q2.sql
sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules LT05 q3.sql q4.sql
```

### Dialect

ansi. postgres, bigquery, snowflake and tsql give the same output for q1.sql and q2.sql.

### Version

```
sqlfluff, version 4.3.0
Python 3.12.14
```

Measured on `main` at `2e2275713`. The `4.3.0` tag gives the same output for the four files.

### Configuration

None. There is no `.sqlfluff` file. The command line gives the dialect and the rule, and the templater is the default `jinja`.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issues.title: BigQuery - Missing support for WITH Expressions
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### Description

In BigQuery, the WITH keyword isn't just for CTEs, it can also be used as a way to create temporary variables when creating a column for example.

It is documented [here](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators#with_expression).

Here is the configuration used for the following tests:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = bigquery
templater = raw
```

And here the examples provided by the documentation with the parsing error message from SQLFluff:

```sql
SELECT WITH(a AS '123',               -- a is '123'
            b AS CONCAT(a, '456'),    -- b is '123456'
            c AS '789',               -- c is '789'
            CONCAT(b, c)) AS result;  -- b + c is '123456789'
```

```
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   8 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 8: Found unparsable section: "WITH(a AS '123',   
                       | -- a is '..."
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'bigquery'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

---

```sql
SELECT WITH(a AS RAND(), a - a);
```

```
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   8 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 8: Found unparsable section: 'WITH(a AS RAND(), a
                       | - a)'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'bigquery'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```


### Use case

There's many thing we can imagine that would be nice to add in SQLFluff:

- A rule for forbidding WITH expressions
- A rule for encouraging WITH expressions when an expressions is getting lengthy or has repetitive bits
- A rule for defining variable case (may not be pertinent, as we could follow column casing but just letting it here)
- A rule for forbidding/forcing the use of "final variables":

```sql
SELECT
    WITH(
        a AS 1,
        b AS 2,
        -- Here we create a "final variable" that will return the result
        result AS a + b,
        result
    ) AS foo,
    WITH(
        a AS 1,
        b AS 2,
```

issues.title: LT05 does not count Jinja source which the template does not render
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

LT05 measures a line by its length in the source file. `_source_char_len` in `src/sqlfluff/utils/reflow/reindent.py` (line 2042) counts a literal segment by its raw length. Literal source which the current variant does not render has an empty raw, so it counts as 0 characters. That source is:

- the body of a `{% macro %}` definition,
- an `if` or `else` branch which the variant skips,
- the body of a `{% for %}` loop with no iterations,
- whitespace which a Jinja `-` marker such as `{%-`, `-%}`, `{{-` or `{#-` removes.

A line with such source can be over `max_line_length` in the file, and LT05 does not report it. When LT05 reports the line, the length in the message can be too short. `sqlfluff fix` can also leave a line over the limit, and LT05 does not report that line after the fix.

The unrendered source can also span several lines, for example a macro body on its own lines. LT05 does not measure the lines inside that block at all.

I described this gap on #8580, where it affects the new `list_wrapping = fill` mode.

### Expected Behaviour

LT05 counts every character of the source line, including source which does not render. It reports every line which is over `max_line_length` in the file, with the length of the source line.

### Observed Behaviour

Measured on `main` at `4d259e33f` with `sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi --rules LT05` and the default limit of 80:

| input | source line length | LT05 |
|---|---|---|
| macro definition and a `SELECT` on one line | 94 | nothing |
| macro definition on its own line | 83 | nothing |
| `if`/`else` on its own line (below) | 104 | nothing |
| `{% for x in [] %}` loop on its own line | 93 | nothing |
| 4 spaces before `{%- if true %}` | 84 | nothing |
| 1 space before `{%- if true %}` and 1 before `{%- endif %}` | 99 | `Line is too long (97 > 80).` |
| a line inside a multi-line macro definition | 85 | nothing |
| a line inside a multi-line `{% for x in [] %}` loop | 82 | nothing |
| `{% if false %}` with no `else` | 107 | `Line is too long (107 > 80).` |

The last row is correct because the templater renders a second variant for the skipped `if` branch. With an `else` branch, each variant renders only one branch, so every variant counts the line as short.

The `if`/`else` fixture input from #8580 shows the effect on `sqlfluff fix`. The input is:

```
select a
from tbl
group by col_a, {% if flag %}col_b{% else %}col_c{% endif %}, col_d, long_column_name1, long_column_name2
```

The `.sqlfluff` file next to it is:

```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = ansi
max_line_length = 46

[sqlfluff:templater:jinja:context]
flag = true
```

Line 3 is 105 characters long, and `sqlfluff lint --rules LT05` reports `Line is too long (100 > 46).` Then `sqlfluff fix --rules LT05` gives this output:

```
select a
from tbl
group by
    col_a,
    {% if flag %}col_b{% else %}col_c{% endif %},
    col_d,
    long_column_name1,
    long_column_name2
```

Line 5 is 49 characters long. `sqlfluff lint --rules LT05` on the fixed file reports nothing.

### How to reproduce

```
cat > q.sql <<'EOF'
SELECT a FROM t
{% if flag %}WHERE b_column_with_a_long_name = 1{% else %}WHERE c_column_with_a_long_name = 2{% endif %}
EOF
awk '{ print length($0) }' q.sql
sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi --rules LT05 q.sql
```

`awk` prints 15 and 104. LT05 reports nothing.

### Dialect

ansi. The rule is not dialect-specific.

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0 from `main` at `4d259e33f`, Python 3.12.14.

### Configuration

None for the table and for `q.sql`. The command line gives the dialect and the rule, and the jinja templater is the default. The #8580 example uses the `.sqlfluff` file above.

issues.title: Postgres: ON/OFF option values and PostgreSQL 16-17 EXPLAIN, VACUUM and ANALYZE options do not parse
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

The postgres dialect reads a boolean option value with `BooleanLiteralGrammar` in `EXPLAIN`, `ANALYZE`, `REINDEX`, `COPY`, `CREATE DATABASE`, `ALTER DATABASE` and `CREATE COLLATION`. The two `DATABASE` statements use it for `ALLOW_CONNECTIONS` and `IS_TEMPLATE`. `CREATE COLLATION` uses it for `DETERMINISTIC`. That grammar is only `TRUE` or `FALSE`. PostgreSQL also accepts `ON`, `OFF`, `1` and `0` for these options. The [EXPLAIN page](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-explain.html) lists all six values. In `gram.y`, `utility_option_arg`, `copy_generic_opt_arg` and `createdb_opt_item` read the value as `opt_boolean_or_string` or `NumericOnly`. `CREATE COLLATION` reads the value as a `def_arg` in `gram.y`, and `DefineCollation` converts it with `defGetBoolean`.

The grammar also has no rule for these options from PostgreSQL 16 and 17:

| statement | option | added in |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPLAIN` | `GENERIC_PLAN` | 16 |
| `EXPLAIN` | `SERIALIZE`, `MEMORY` | 17 |
| `VACUUM` | `PROCESS_MAIN`, `SKIP_DATABASE_STATS`, `ONLY_DATABASE_STATS`, `BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT` | 16 |
| `ANALYZE` | `BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT` | 16 |

The grammar is in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_postgres.py`:

- `ExplainOptionSegment` (line 2341)
- `CreateDatabaseStatementSegment` (line 3684)
- `AlterDatabaseStatementSegment` (line 3757)
- `VacuumStatementSegment` (line 3940)
- `ReindexStatementSegment` (line 4825)
- `AnalyzeStatementSegment` (line 5168)
- `CopyStatementSegment` (line 6021)
- `CreateCollationStatementSegment` (line 6707)

### Expected Behaviour

Each statement in the table below parses.

### Observed Behaviour

Measured on `main` at `4d259e33f` with `sqlfluff lint --dialect postgres --rules LT01`, one statement at a time:

| statement | result |
|---|---|
| `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE ON, BUFFERS OFF) SELECT 1;` | unparsable from position 1 |
| `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN) SELECT 1;` | unparsable from position 1 |
| `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, SERIALIZE BINARY, MEMORY) SELECT 1;` | unparsable from position 1 |
| `VACUUM (SKIP_DATABASE_STATS);` | unparsable from position 8 |
| `VACUUM (PROCESS_MAIN FALSE, BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT 256) t;` | unparsable from position 8 |
| `ANALYZE (BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT 256) t;` | unparsable from position 9 |
| `ANALYZE (VERBOSE ON) t;` | unparsable from position 9 |
| `REINDEX (VERBOSE 1) TABLE t;` | unparsable from position 1 |
| `COPY t FROM STDIN WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER ON);` | unparsable from position 24 |
| `CREATE DATABASE d WITH IS_TEMPLATE ON;` | unparsable from position 24 |
| `ALTER DATABASE d WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS OFF;` | unparsable from position 18 |
| `CREATE DATABASE d IS_TEMPLATE = 1 ALLOW_CONNECTIONS = off CONNECTION LIMIT 5;` | unparsable from position 19 |
| `ALTER DATABASE d IS_TEMPLATE ON CONNECTION LIMIT 5;` | unparsable from position 18 |
| `CREATE COLLATION c (provider = icu, locale = 'und', deterministic = off);` | unparsable from position 1 |

The output for the first statement includes this violation:

```
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'EXPLAIN
                       | (ANALYZE ON, BUFFERS OFF) SELECT...'
```

`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE TRUE, COSTS FALSE) SELECT 1;` parses. `CREATE DATABASE d WITH IS_TEMPLATE TRUE ALLOW_CONNECTIONS = false;` parses. `CREATE COLLATION c (provider = icu, locale = 'und', deterministic = false);` parses. `VACUUM (INDEX_CLEANUP off) t;` also parses, because the `VACUUM` value grammar accepts an identifier.

### How to reproduce

```
for q in \
  'EXPLAIN (ANALYZE ON, BUFFERS OFF) SELECT 1;' \
  'VACUUM (SKIP_DATABASE_STATS);' \
  'ANALYZE (BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT 256) t;' \
  'CREATE DATABASE d WITH IS_TEMPLATE ON;' \
  'ALTER DATABASE d WITH ALLOW_CONNECTIONS OFF;' \
  "CREATE COLLATION c (provider = icu, locale = 'und', deterministic = off);"
do
  printf '%s\n' "$q" | sqlfluff lint --dialect postgres --rules LT01 -
done
```

### Dialect

postgres

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0 from `main` at `4d259e33f`, Python 3.12.14.

### Configuration

None. The command line gives the dialect.

issues.title: dbt templater fails with `DbtCatalogIntegrationNotFoundError` when using  `catalogs.yml`
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

(disclaimer: used AI for debugging and bug description, but everything has been reviewed and verified by me)

With the dbt templater, `sqlfluff lint` fails for the whole project if any model sets `catalog_name` to a catalog defined in `catalogs.yml`. The failure happens while dbt parses the project, before any file is linted. Excluding the file or using `.sqlfluffignore` doesn't help.

The dbt CLI (`dbt compile`, `dbt run`, `dbt build`) works fine on the same project.

**Root cause:** the dbt CLI loads `catalogs.yml` and registers each catalog with the adapter before parsing:

- It calls `load_catalogs_v2()` or `load_catalogs()`, then `adapter.bridge_v2_catalog()` and
  `adapter.add_catalog_integration()`.
- This happens in `dbt/cli/requires.py::setup_manifest` and `dbt/parser/manifest.py::parse_manifest`.

`DbtTemplater` does none of this. It calls `register_adapter()` in `dbt_config` and then
`ManifestLoader.get_full_manifest()` in `dbt_manifest`. The adapter therefore only knows its built-in catalogs
(`info_schema` and `managed_iceberg` for BigQuery). While parsing each node, dbt calls
`adapter.build_catalog_relation()`, which asks the adapter for the custom catalog and fails because it was never
registered.

This affects both the v1 `catalogs.yml` format and the v2 format (`flags.use_catalogs_v2: true`), because the
templater skips both loading paths.

### Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff lint` compiles the project the same way `dbt compile` does, including catalogs from `catalogs.yml`, and lints the models normally.

### Observed Behaviour

Got error:
```text
=== [dbt templater] Sorting Nodes...
User Error: dbt failed during project compilation. Consider  running  `dbt debug` or `dbt compile` to get more information from dbt. dbt.adapters.catalogs._exceptions.DbtCatalogIntegrationNotFoundError: Runtime Error
  Catalog not found.Received: my_catalogExpected one of: info_schema, managed_iceberg?
```

### How to reproduce

1. Create a dbt project with these files.

   `dbt_project.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: "example"
   version: "1.0.0"
   config-version: 2
   profile: "example"
   flags:
     use_catalogs_v2: true
   ```

   `catalogs.yml`:

   ```yaml
   catalogs:
     - name: my_catalog
       type: biglake_metastore
       table_format: iceberg
       config:
         bigquery:
           external_volume: 'gs://my-bucket'
           file_format: parquet
   ```

   `models/my_model.sql`:

   ```sql
   {{ config(
       materialized = 'table',
       catalog_name = 'my_catalog',
       storage_uri = 'gs://my-bucket/my_model',
   ) }}

   SELECT 1 AS id
   ```

2. Add a BigQuery profile named `example` to `~/.dbt/profiles.yml`.
3. Run `dbt compile`. It succeeds.
4. Run `sqlfluff lint models/my_model.sql`. It fails with the error above.

**Workaround:** a `sitecustomize.py` placed on `PYTHONPATH` that wraps `dbt.adapters.factory.register_adapter` and
registers the catalogs itself. With it, linting works:

```python
import contextlib

from dbt.adapters import factory
from dbt.adapters.catalogs import DbtCatalogIntegrationAlreadyExistsError
from dbt.config.catalogs import load_catalogs_v2
from dbt.config.runtime import RuntimeConfig

_original = factory.register_adapter


def _register_adapter_with_catalogs(config, mp_context, adapter_registered_log_level=None):
    _original(config, mp_context, adapter_registered_log_level)
    if not isinstance(config, RuntimeConfig):
        return
    adapter = factory.get_adapter(config)
    for catalog in load_catalogs_v2(config.project_root, config.project_name, config.cli_vars):
        with contextlib.suppress(DbtCatalogIntegrationAlreadyExistsError):
            adapter.add_catalog_integration(adapter.bridge_v2_catalog(catalog))


factory.register_adapter = _register_adapter_with_catalogs
```

**Suggested fix:** in `DbtTemplater.dbt_manifest`, before calling `ManifestLoader.get_full_manifest()`, mirror what
`setup_manifest` does:

- If `use_catalogs_v2` is set, load the catalogs with `load_catalogs_v2` and register each one via
  `bridge_v2_catalog` and `add_catalog_integration`.
- Otherwise, load them with `load_catalogs` and register each one's active write integration.

### Dialect

`bigquery`

### Version

- sqlfluff 4.3.0
- sqlfluff-templater-dbt 4.3.0
- dbt-core 1.12.4
- dbt-adapters 1.24.5
- dbt-bigquery 1.12.0
- Python 3.13

### Configuration

`.sqlfluff`:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = bigquery
templater = dbt
max_line_length = 120
max_parse_depth = 510

[sqlfluff:templater:dbt]
project_dir = data
```

The rest of our config (rule exclusions and layout/capitalisation settings) doesn't affect this; the failure occurs
before any rules run.

issues.title: RF01: false positive when an alias/table reference differs in letter case from its declaration
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`RF01` (`references.from`) reports a false-positive "reference not found" when
a table alias or table name is referenced using a different letter case than
it was declared with, even though the two spellings denote the same
identifier under the dialect's own identifier-casing rules.

```sql
SELECT CI.id
FROM source_table AS ci
JOIN second_table AS b ON ci.id = b.id;
```

On `dialect = ansi` this raises:

```
Reference 'CI.id' refers to table/view not found in the FROM clause or found
in ancestor statement.
```

even though `ci`/`CI` are the same identifier under ansi's own upper-folding
rule for unquoted identifiers, and the query is valid, executable SQL. The
same false positive reproduces for an unaliased table reference (e.g.
`SELECT SOURCE_TABLE.id FROM source_table ...`), and for other dialects
regardless of which way they fold (verified upper-folding `ansi`/`trino`/
`tsql` and lower-folding `postgres`).

### Expected Behaviour

An unquoted alias/table reference should resolve case-insensitively,
consistent with the dialect's own identifier-casefold rules -- the same way
sibling rules `RF02`/`RF07`/`ST07` already compare identifiers (via
`raw_normalized()`), and the same way real databases treat unquoted
identifiers as case-insensitive. A **quoted** identifier should keep matching
case-sensitively, since most dialects do not casefold those.

### Observed Behaviour

`RF01` flags the reference as undefined instead of resolving it, in every
case where the reference's case differs from the alias/table's declared
case. Reversing which side is upper/lower-case still fails, confirming this
isn't about one direction (declared-vs-used) but that identifier comparisons
inside `RF01` never case-fold at all.

### How to reproduce

```
$ sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi -
SELECT CI.id
FROM source_table AS ci
JOIN second_table AS b ON ci.id = b.id;
^D
```

Also reproduces with the alias/reference case direction reversed, with an
unaliased table (`SELECT SOURCE_TABLE.id FROM source_table;`), and on
`postgres`/`trino`/`tsql`.

### Dialect

`ansi` (reproduces on every dialect `RF01` runs against by default; verified
`ansi`, `postgres`, `trino`, `tsql`).

### Version

`sqlfluff`, version 4.3.0 (current `main`, commit `e2d032239`). Python 3.12.3.

### Configuration

Default configuration, `RF01` enabled (its default state).

### Impact and validation

Impact: contract-violation — `RF01`'s job is to distinguish valid FROM-clause
references from undefined ones, and it gets this wrong for identifiers the
dialect itself treats as equivalent.

Entry point / who reaches it: any user running `sqlfluff lint`/`fix` with
`RF01` enabled (its default state) on SQL where an unquoted alias or table
name is referenced with different letter case than it was declared with.
This is triggered via the plain CLI/API lint path, no special configuration
needed.

Negative control: reverting the fix and re-running
`pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k RF01 -q` gives `3 failed, 116
passed`; with the fix restored, `119 passed`.

This issue was drafted with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code).
AI-assisted: locating the root cause and drafting this report. Manually
validated: I reproduced the false positive myself by directly running
`sqlfluff lint` against the queries above on four dialects with opposite
identifier-folding directions, and I manually validated which identifier
types each dialect casefolds by reading the dialect definitions myself.

I will open a PR fixing this shortly.

Signed-off-by: Udaya Tejas <udayatejas2004@gmail.com>

issues.title: Parser does not validate data type argument arity (e.g. `DECIMAL(10, 2, 3)` is accepted)
issues.body:
- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

## What Happened

While checking Databricks SQL I found that `CREATE TABLE t (a DECIMAL(10, 2, 3))`
parses with no violations. `DECIMAL`/`NUMERIC` take at most a precision and an
optional scale (0–2 arguments), so a third argument is invalid here.

Looking at the shared grammar, this isn't specific to `DECIMAL`: the ANSI
`DatatypeSegment` attaches an unconstrained bracketed argument list to *any*
primitive type name, so argument arity is never validated for any data type.
`VARCHAR(3, 4)`, `CHAR(3, 4)` and `INT(1, 2, 3)` are accepted as well.

## Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff should report the input as unparsable (`Found unparsable section`),
because the type accepts at most two bracketed arguments.

## Observed Behaviour

No violations; `sqlfluff parse` exits 0 and builds a `bracketed_arguments` node
containing three numeric literals:

```
$ echo 'CREATE TABLE t (a DECIMAL(10, 2, 3));' | sqlfluff parse - --dialect ansi
...
|                    data_type:
|                        primitive_type:
|                            keyword:                          'DECIMAL'
|                            bracketed_arguments:
|                                bracketed:
|                                    start_bracket:            '('
|                                    numeric_literal:          '10'
|                                    comma:                    ','
|                                    numeric_literal:          '2'
|                                    comma:                    ','
|                                    numeric_literal:          '3'
|                                    end_bracket:              ')'
...
```

Identical result (accepted, no violations) for `ansi`, `databricks`, `sparksql`,
`postgres` and `snowflake`, on both the Python and Rust parsers.

## How to reproduce

```bash
$ echo 'CREATE TABLE t (a DECIMAL(10, 2, 3));' | sqlfluff parse - --dialect ansi >/dev/null; echo "exit: $?"
exit: 0
```

Other over-accepted examples (each independent):

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (a NUMERIC(1, 2, 3));
CREATE TABLE t (a VARCHAR(3, 4));
CREATE TABLE t (a CHAR(3, 4));
CREATE TABLE t (a INT(1, 2, 3));
```

Valid controls `DECIMAL(10, 2)`, `DECIMAL(10)` and `VARCHAR(3)` are also accepted,
as expected.

## Dialect

All dialects that inherit the ANSI data type grammar. Verified directly on
`ansi`, `databricks`, `sparksql`, `postgres` and `snowflake`.

## Version

- `main` at `c7401613e851a6913ec3de8e003247e6fe8e5387` (2026-09-26), Python and
  Rust parsers both
- Released `4.3.0` reproduces as well

## Configuration

None — defaults. Command used: `sqlfluff parse - --dialect ansi`.

## Likely root cause

`BracketedArguments` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_ansi.py:1020` is a plain
delimited literal list with no cardinality constraint:

```python
class BracketedArguments(BaseSegment):
    type = "bracketed_arguments"
    match_grammar = Bracketed(
        # The brackets might be empty for some cases...
        Delimited(Ref("LiteralGrammar"), optional=True),
    )
```

and `DatatypeSegment` (`dialect_ansi.py:1033`) references it after any
`DatatypeIdentifierSegment`:

```python
Ref("DatatypeIdentifierSegment"),
allow_gaps=False,
...
Ref("BracketedArguments", optional=True),
```

Because the same unconstrained `BracketedArguments` is shared across data-type
productions — and inherited by many dialects (`postgres`, `oracle`, `athena`,
`hive`, `teradata` reference it; TSQL and Exasol subclass it) — there is nowhere
for a per-type arity rule to live. A proper fix likely means a type-family
argument production with its own cardinality constraint, rather than further
relaxing the shared one. Happy to be guided on the preferred shape.

issues.title: `max_parse_depth` boundary differs between the Python and Rust parsers
issues.body:
## Summary

The `max_parse_depth` DoS guard trips at different nesting levels depending on which parser is active. The Python parser and the Rust (`sqlfluffrs`) parser measure parse depth differently, so the same configured `max_parse_depth` rejects at a different point under each engine.

The divergence is in the **safe direction** — Rust is always the more permissive of the two — so the default engine never rejects input that pure Python accepts. But the configured limit is not honoured identically, and the gap is not constant, so the boundary cannot be reconciled by re-tuning the default.

## Reproduce

With the Rust extension installed (`sqlfluffrs`) and `core.use_rust_parser = auto` (the default), sweep `max_parse_depth` for nested brackets:

```python
def accepts(sql, use_rust, limit):
    config = FluffConfig(overrides={
        "dialect": "ansi", "use_rust_parser": use_rust,
        "max_parse_nodes": 0, "max_parse_depth": limit,
    })
    return not any(
        v.rule_code() == "PRS" and "Maximum parse depth exceeded" in v.desc()
        for v in Linter(config=config).parse_string(sql).violations
    )
```

At the default `max_parse_depth = 600`:
- Python rejects from ~35 nested brackets.
- Rust rejects from ~40 nested brackets.

## Measurements

Smallest `max_parse_depth` at which each engine accepts (i.e. peak tracked depth), nesting depth 25:

| Shape | Python | Rust |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| nested brackets | 453 | 394 |
| nested functions | 665 | 557 |
| nested subqueries | 680 | 570 |
| bracketed arithmetic | 528 | 469 |
| flat `1+1+…` | 56 | 47 |

Fitted against nesting depth `d` (brackets): Python `≈ 53 + 16d`, Rust `≈ 44 + 14d`. The per-level rate varies by construct (functions/subqueries diverge ~2.4×/level versus Rust), so a fixed offset or scale factor cannot align the two engines.

## Root cause

- **Python** (`src/sqlfluff/core/parser/context.py`) increments `match_depth` on every `deeper_match()` context. There are 15 call sites, and several are incidental to traversal rather than grammar structure — notably one per *segment* match (`segments/base.py`) on top of the grammar reference (`grammar/base.py`), so each segment reference is counted twice, plus algorithm wrappers (`Bracket`, `GreedyUntil`, `Bracketed-StartBracket`/`-EndBracket`, `Trim-Greedy*`, `Delimited-Term`).
- **Rust** (`sqlfluffrs/sqlfluffrs_parser/src/parser/table_driven/iterative.rs`) checks the table-driven frame-stack length. A `Ref` frame descends into the referenced grammar; there is no frame for the segment itself.

## Impact

Rust is never *stricter*, so the default engine does not produce false rejections relative to Python. The observable difference is the reverse: switching to pure Python (`use_rust_parser = False`) lowers the effective nesting ceiling for the same config. The existing tests use inputs far over the limit (120 brackets at limit 100), so the boundary itself is uncovered.

## Possible fixes

1. Remove Python's incidental extra depth entries so depth means "grammar-node nesting" in both engines, then recalibrate the default (touches `ParseContext` and its 15 call sites; moves a user-facing default).
2. Mirror Python's accounting in Rust via a dedicated depth counter, recorded as a parity invariant in `table_driven/parity.rs` (audit of ~36 descend sites).

Both are estimated at 2–3 focused days including validation. An interim safeguard has been opened as a PR: a differential test that pins only the safe direction (Rust not stricter than Python) across a shape matrix, so the direction cannot silently flip.

## Related

- #7805 (closed) — the T-SQL nested-function case that motivated raising the default 255 → 600. This is the same guard, reported from the engine-parity angle.

issues.title: ST04 fix deletes the space before the outer END when flattening a nested CASE
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

`sqlfluff fix` with ST04 flattens a nested `CASE` in an `ELSE` clause. When the nested `END` and the outer `END` are on the same line with no comment between them, the fix deletes the space between the nested value and the outer `END`. The fixed SQL does not parse.

The cause is `_nested_end_trailing_comment` in `src/sqlfluff/rules/structure/ST04.py:201-219`. It deletes every whitespace segment on the nested `END` line up to the first comment, then moves that comment to a new line. With no comment on the line, it deletes all the whitespace on the line, including the space before the outer `END`.

The default rule set hides this, because LT01 puts the space back in the same `fix` run. A run with `--rules ST04`, or a config that excludes LT01, keeps the broken output.

### Expected Behaviour

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN x = 1 THEN a
        WHEN x = 2 THEN b END AS y FROM t
```

### Observed Behaviour

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN x = 1 THEN a
        WHEN x = 2 THEN bEND AS y FROM t
```

`sqlfluff parse --dialect ansi` on the output reports `Found unparsable section: 'CASE WHEN x = 1 ...'`. When the value is a quoted string, as in `THEN 'b' END END`, the output `THEN 'b'END` still parses, so an identifier or a number before `END` is needed to see the error.

### How to reproduce

```
printf 'SELECT CASE WHEN x = 1 THEN a ELSE CASE WHEN x = 2 THEN b END END AS y FROM t\n' > q.sql
sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules ST04 q.sql
cat q.sql
sqlfluff parse --dialect ansi q.sql
```

### Dialect

ansi. The rule is not dialect-specific.

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0 from `main` at `ff76fce3f`, Python 3.12.14.

### Configuration

None. The command line gives the dialect and the rule.

issues.title: colon_optional_quotes placeholder style replaces colons inside time literals and array slices
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

The placeholder templater with `param_style = colon_optional_quotes` treats every colon that does not follow another colon as a parameter. A colon inside a time literal or an array slice is replaced, so the rendered SQL changes.

The `colon` style does not have this problem. Its regex at `src/sqlfluff/core/templaters/placeholder.py:25` skips a colon that follows a word character or a backslash: `(?<![:\w\x5c])`. The `colon_optional_quotes` regex at line 28 skips only a colon that follows a colon: `(?<!:)`.

### Expected Behaviour

`'2024-01-01 12:30:00'` and `tags[1:3]` render unchanged. Only the standalone `:user_id` is replaced.

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ sqlfluff render q.sql
SELECT
    '2024-01-01 123000'::timestamp AS ts,
    tags[13] AS first_tags
FROM users
WHERE user_id = 42
```

The time literal loses both colons and the slice loses its colon. `:30`, `:00` and `:3` are each read as a parameter. None has a value, so each one renders as its own name.

### How to reproduce

`.sqlfluff`:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = postgres
templater = placeholder

[sqlfluff:templater:placeholder]
param_style = colon_optional_quotes
user_id = 42
```

`q.sql`:

```sql
SELECT
    '2024-01-01 12:30:00'::timestamp AS ts,
    tags[1:3] AS first_tags
FROM users
WHERE user_id = :user_id
```

Then run `sqlfluff render q.sql`.

### Dialect

postgres. The templater runs before the dialect, so the dialect does not matter.

### Version

sqlfluff 4.3.0 from `main` at `ff76fce3f`, Python 3.12.14.

The `.sqlfluff` above.

issues.title: MySQL/MariaDB: support the `SOURCE` client command
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### Description

`SOURCE file.sql` is how a MySQL/MariaDB script includes another script. It is
the mechanism multi-file schemas and programs are assembled with, so it
appears in exactly the top-level files that drive everything else.

It's terminated by an end of line or a semicolon, so it can't easily be fixed
without lexer support.  It also allows spaces, and does not accept surrounding
quotes, as they are interpreted as part of the filename (not by sqlfluff, but by
MySQL/MariaDB).

SQLFluff currently reports the whole line as an unparsable section:

```
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'SOURCE
                       | schema/tables.sql'
```

It is a client command rather than server SQL, but so is `DELIMITER`, which
SQLFluff already models as `DelimiterStatement`.

All of these are currently unparsable, on both `mysql` and `mariadb`:

```sql
SOURCE setup.sql
SOURCE schema/tables.sql;
source lowercase/path.sql
SOURCE path/with spaces/file.sql
\. schema/tables.sql
```

Paths may be relative or absolute, the trailing semicolon is optional, and an
unquoted path may contain spaces, because the client reads to end of line.

I think it needs to lex like this to fit MySQL/MariaDB, **at start of
statement** (case insensitive):
`(?i)[ \t]*(SOURCE|\\\.)[ ]+([^\n\r;]+?)[ ]*(\r\n|\n|;)`

It is genuinely statement-positional rather than line-positional — this runs
the SOURCE, so an anchor on the preceding newline would miss it:

```
> select 1; source 'abcd';
ERROR: Failed to open file ''abcd'', error: 2
```

Though actually turning that into code is nontrivial.  Note the lazy file capture
to avoid swallowing the later spaces.  Case-insensitivity will need an inline
`(?i)`: `RegexLexer` compiles with `regex.DOTALL` only and takes no flags
argument.

A SOURCE directive with multiple semicolons is parsed only up to the first
semicolon, the second one is read by the sql client as another statement.

Multiple spaces are allowed both before and after the keyword, but there
must be at least one after the keyword.

The argument is arbitrary text rather than SQL tokens, which is why this needs
the lexer.  `SOURCE schema/tables.sql` happens to lex because `/` and `.` have
matchers, but a filename need not be made of those — and then it fails exactly
the way `DELIMITER $$` does:

```
SOURCE a$b.sql       Unable to lex characters: '$b.sql'
SOURCE C:\db\x.sql    Unable to lex characters: '\db\x.sql'
```

`DELIMITER` is the model: `DelimiterStatement` is inserted into
`StatementSegment`, so it is only offered where a statement can begin. That is
what keeps it unambiguous even though `DELIMITER` is an unreserved keyword and
`SELECT delimiter FROM t` parses fine. A `SourceStatement` in the same place
gets the same protection, which matters because `SOURCE` is unreserved too.

The one wrinkle is the path's end. `DELIMITER` sidesteps it —
`match_grammar = Ref.keyword("DELIMITER")` never consumes its own argument —
but `SOURCE` has to capture the path, and the terminator is a newline whenever
the optional semicolon is omitted. There is precedent for matching newlines
from a grammar: postgres defines

```python
MultilineConcatenateNewline=TypedParser("newline", NewlineSegment, type="newline"),
MultilineConcatenateDelimiterGrammar=AnyNumberOf(
    Ref("MultilineConcatenateNewline"), min_times=1, allow_gaps=False
),
```

for multiline string concatenation, which is the same need.

#3599 is the same kind of problem and may want the same solution:
https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/3599#issuecomment-5430153824

`\.` is the documented alias for `SOURCE` and means the same thing, so it is in
the syntax above. It needs one extra piece — the backslash currently fails with
`Unable to lex characters`, so it wants a fixed-string matcher. That is a
one-liner of a kind `dialect_mysql.py` already has six sets of
(`StringLexer("walrus_operator", ":=", ...)` and friends), it is stateless, and
`build_lexers.py` handles `StringLexer` so the Rust side comes along for free.
Nothing like the stateful matcher #3599 needs. Worth doing at the same time.

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

Sort of.  I'm trying to make MySQL/MariaDB first class in the functions/procedures
realm, but I know @Mynk11 is working on a very similar problem with DELIMITER,
and I think i should stay out of this while that's occurring.  It also looks easier to
subtly get wrong than my other PR's so I'd prefer that someone else do it.  That
being said, sure, maybe.

### Use case

Linting a multi-file schema where scripts include `SOURCE` lines. Those files are
currently unparsable in their entirety, so they have to be excluded, which means
the files that define the load order are the ones that get no checking at all.

### Dialect

mysql and mariadb


### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

issues.title: ST01 silently deletes a comment inside a redundant ELSE NULL clause on autofix
issues.body:
## Summary

`ST01` (`structure.else_null`) removes a redundant `ELSE NULL` clause from a `CASE` expression when autofixing. If that `ELSE NULL` clause contains a comment (e.g. `else /* keep default */ null`), the comment is a child of the deleted `else_clause` segment, so `sqlfluff fix` silently deletes the comment along with the clause — with no warning, and no way for the user to recover it afterwards.

**Impact: data-loss**

Entry point / who reaches it: any user running `sqlfluff fix` (or `lint --fix`) with `ST01`/`structure.else_null` enabled — it's in the default `all` rule group — on a `CASE` expression whose redundant `ELSE NULL` branch carries a comment.

Reproduction:
```sql
select
    case
        when name = 'cat' then 'meow'
        when name = 'dog' then 'woof'
        else /* keep default */ null
    end
from x
```
Before this fix, `sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules ST01` on the above silently drops `else /* keep default */ null` entirely, including the comment — the user's annotation is gone with no diagnostic. There is no `--fix` output, log line, or lint message that mentions the comment at all.

## Root cause

`Rule_ST01._eval` (`src/sqlfluff/rules/structure/ST01.py`), on detecting a redundant `else null`, unconditionally emits `LintFix.delete(else_clause[0])` plus deletes of the leading whitespace — deleting the entire `else_clause` segment as one unit. A comment nested between the `ELSE` keyword and the `NULL` literal is a genuine child of that segment (not a sibling the rule already preserves), so it is deleted along with the redundant clause. Nothing in the rule inspects the clause's children for a comment before deleting it.

## Fix

Before deleting the clause, look for comment children of `else_clause`. If any are found, re-home them onto their own line immediately after the last `WHEN` clause (so they attach to the `CASE` expression the same way a comment placed there manually would), then delete the clause as before. Verified this can't leave an `else_clause` with no expression child for a case ST02 might also touch, since the whole clause is still deleted as a single unit either way — only the comment is relocated, not exempted from the clause deletion.

## Testing (negative control — reproduce by execution)

Added `redundant_else_null_preserves_comment` to `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/ST01.yml`.

With the production fix reverted (fixture kept), running the targeted test fails exactly this new case and nothing else:
```
$ pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k ST01 -q
```
