issues.title: Oracle: SELECT...INTO with record/collection-field targets (e.g. \INTO rec.field`) is unparsable, causing false ST03 unused-CTE positives`
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Oracle `PL/SQL SELECT ... INTO` clauses that target fields of a record variable (e.g. `INTO out_rec.col1, out_rec.col2`) fail to parse. The `.field` portion after the first `INTO `identifier; and everything following it in the statement, including the trailing `FROM `clause; collapses into a single `unparsable` segment. As a knock-on effect, because the `FROM` `cte_name` text is now buried inside `unparsable` rather than a real from_clause/table_reference node, rule ST03 (`structure.unused_cte`) incorrectly reports the referenced **CTE** as unused, since its usage-detection (`recursive_crawl("table_reference")`) never sees a proper `table_reference` node for it.

### Expected Behaviour

The `INTO` clause should parse cleanly when its targets are dotted record/collection-field references (e.g. `out_rec.col1`), not just bare identifiers or bind variables.

No `PRS` (parse) error, and no `ST03` violation for `cte1`, since it's genuinely referenced in the `FROM` clause.

### Observed Behaviour

See "How to reproduce" for repro.sql lines.

```
== [repro.sql] FAIL
L:   5 | P:   8 | ST03 | Query defines CTE "cte1" but does not use it.
                       | [structure.unused_cte]
L:  12 | P:  16 |  PRS | Line 12, Position 16: Found unparsable section: '.a,\n
                       | out_metrics.b\n  from cte1'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'oracle'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```
`sqlfluff parse` shows the break clearly; parsing succeeds up through the first `INTO` target (`out_metrics` as a bare `naked_identifier`), then hits unparsable right at the following `.`:

```
into_clause:
    keyword:                  'into'
    newline:                  '\n'
    naked_identifier:         'out_metrics'
unparsable:                   !! Expected: 'Nothing here.'
    dot:                      '.'
    word:                     'a'
    comma:                    ','
    ...
    word:                     'from'
    word:                     'cte1'
```

### How to reproduce


Create a file called repro.sql with the following lines:
```
create or replace procedure test_proc(out_rec out sys_refcursor) is
  type t_rec is record (a number, b number);
  out_metrics t_rec;
begin
  with cte1 as (
    select 1 as x from dual
  )
  select
    cte1.x,
    cte1.x
  into
    out_metrics.a,
    out_metrics.b
  from cte1;
end;
/
```

`sqlfluff lint --dialect oracle --rules ST03 repro.sql`
`sqlfluff parse --dialect oracle repro.sql`



### Dialect

oracle

### Version

sqlfluff, version 4.2.0

### Configuration

No project .sqlfluff/.sqlfluffignore needed to reproduce; the repro above fails with just --dialect oracle passed on the CLI, no config file present. 

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

issues.title: Missing keyword handling for IBM DB2 dialect
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

The db2 dialect seems to be missing handling of some keywords. I experience parsing erros that interrupt linting of the remaining SQL script.

Suppression with `-- noqa: PRS` does not help, because formatting is interrupted.

I encounter parsing errors on these valid IBM DB2 statements:

```sql
comment on column schema.table.column is 'hello world';
```

```sql
-- create view schema.foo
-- ...
with no row movement;
```

Several user grants in one statement:

```sql
grant all
on schema.table
to  user user1,
    user user2,
    user user3;
```

From a brief look into the source code, I suspect the class `CommentOnStatementSegment` might be required for the comment-clause as is present in the dialects of postgres and databricks.

### Expected Behaviour

The above statements are parsed and recognized for the db2 dialect.

### Observed Behaviour

1. This file content results in the following linting error:

```sql
create view schema.foo as
select col1
from schema.bar
with no row movement;
```

```sh
$> sqlfluff lint testing_with_no_row_movement.sql --dialect db2

                       | [aliasing.unused]
L:   4 | P:   1 | LT02 | Expected indent of 4 spaces. [layout.indent]
L:   4 | P:   1 | RF04 | Keywords should not be used as identifiers.

L:   4 | P:   5 | LT02 | Expected line break and no indent before 'no'.

WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'db2'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

2. This file content results in the following linting error:

```sh
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'comment
```

issues.title: [Snowflake] CALL statement with a colon-prefixed bind variable inside BEGIN...END causes PRS error
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When linting/parsing a Snowflake Scripting block (DECLARE ... BEGIN ... END, either standalone or inside CREATE TASK/CREATE PROCEDURE) that contains a CALL statement whose argument is a bind variable prefixed with a colon (e.g. CALL my_proc(:my_var)), SQLFluff fails to parse the statement. This is the officially documented way to pass a Snowflake Scripting variable as an argument to CALL (see [Snowflake docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/stored-procedure/stored-procedures-snowflake-scripting#calling-a-stored-procedure-without-using-the-returned-value)): "If you need to pass in any variables or arguments as input arguments in the CALL statement, remember to use a colon (:) in front of the variable name."

The same bind variable syntax (:var) works fine in other statements inside the same block (e.g. SELECT :var;), and CALL works fine if the colon is removed — so the issue is specific to the combination of CallStatementSegment + a colon-prefixed variable reference as an argument.

### Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff should parse a CALL statement whose arguments include colon-prefixed bind/scripting variables (:var) when used inside a Snowflake Scripting BEGIN ... END block, since this is valid and officially documented Snowflake syntax. No PRS error should be raised.

### Observed Behaviour

Linting the query below raises a PRS error:

```sql
DECLARE
  load_timestamp VARCHAR DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP();
BEGIN
  CALL my_schema.my_procedure(:load_timestamp);
END;
``` 
```
violations:
  - start_line_no: 4
    start_line_pos: 3
    code: PRS
    description: "Line 4, Position 3: Found unparsable section: 'CALL my_schema.my_procedure(:load_timest...'"
    name: ''
    warning: false
``` 


For comparison, these related cases all parse correctly, which narrows the bug down specifically to CALL + :variable:
```sql
-- OK: same variable used with SELECT instead of CALL
BEGIN
  SELECT :load_timestamp;
END;

-- OK: CALL with the variable but without the colon prefix (non-valid syntax, shown only for isolation)
BEGIN
  CALL my_schema.my_procedure(load_timestamp);
END;
``` 

### How to reproduce

Run sqlfluff lint (or sqlfluff parse) on the SQL block above with --dialect snowflake.

### Dialect

snowflake

### Version

4.2.2

### Configuration

dialect = snowflake
templater = raw
encoding = utf-8
max_line_length = 0

rules = AL02, AL03, AL04, AL05, AL08, AM01, AM02, AM04, AM05, AM06, AM07, CV05, CV07, CV08, CV12, LT07, LT10, LT11, LT13, LT14, RF01, RF02, RF04, RF05, RF06, ST02, ST03, ST04, ST07, ST08, ST10, ST11, ST12

indent_unit = space

indented_joins = False

issues.title: dbt templater ignores DBT_POPULATE_CACHE: relation-cache warm-up runs on every lint
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the issues and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

The dbt templater unconditionally warms dbt's relation cache before templating anything. In `connection()` it calls:

```python
adapter.set_relations_cache(self.dbt_manifest.nodes.values())
```

https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/ba911518e/plugins/sqlfluff-templater-dbt/sqlfluff_templater_dbt/templater.py#L892

That issues one `SHOW OBJECTS` / `information_schema` query **per target schema** before a single file is templated. In our project (Snowflake, ~22 target schemas, 632 relations) it costs ~8s, and it is a fixed cost paid on every invocation — including `sqlfluff lint one_file.sql`.

dbt itself makes this optional. `dbt/cli/params.py` defines:

```
--populate-cache / --no-populate-cache   (envvar: DBT_POPULATE_CACHE)
help: "At start of run, use `show` or `information_schema` queries to populate
       a relational cache, which can speed up subsequent materializations."
```

But setting `DBT_POPULATE_CACHE=false` has **no effect** on SQLFluff. The gate lives in dbt's *task* layer (`dbt/task/runnable.py`, `populate_adapter_cache()` starts with `if not self.args.populate_cache: return`), and the templater calls the adapter directly, bypassing it.

Note dbt's own wording: the cache speeds up *materializations*. Linting performs none.

### Expected Behaviour

The dbt templater already honours dbt's environment variables elsewhere — `DBT_TARGET` (#7900), `DBT_TARGET_PATH`, and the `DBT_ENGINE_*` family (#7902). `DBT_POPULATE_CACHE` looks like a gap in that same pattern.

Either (or both) of:

1. Honour `DBT_POPULATE_CACHE` in the templater.
2. Add a `populate_relations_cache` option to `[sqlfluff:templater:dbt]`, mirroring the existing `dbt_skip_compilation_error` boolean.

I'd suggest defaulting to `True` so there is no behaviour change, though there's a reasonable case for `False` — see below.

### Observed Behaviour

`DBT_POPULATE_CACHE=false sqlfluff lint <one file>` takes the same time as without it. No warning, no way to opt out.

Measured in our project (single file, warm dbt manifest):

| | wall clock |
|---|---|
| stock | 10.0s |
| with the `set_relations_cache` call skipped | 1.9s |

Skipping it appears to be safe, for two reasons:

**dbt degrades gracefully on a cache miss.** `BaseAdapter.list_relations()` checks `_schema_is_cached()`; on a miss it fires a `CacheMiss` event and falls back to `list_relations_without_caching()` for that schema. Same result, just lazy instead of batched.

**Almost nothing during linting reads that cache.** It only backs `get_relation` / `list_relations` / `check_schema_exists`. In our 379-file project the only consumer is `is_incremental()` — in exactly **one** model. Notably `dbt_utils.star` does *not* use it: it goes through `adapter.get_columns_in_relation`, which the relation cache does not serve (the cache holds relation names and types, not columns).

So we pay ~22 metadata queries to serve one lookup that would have cost one.

We verified equivalence by linting all 365 files both ways: identical results, 0 violations both times, no additional skipped files.

The warm-up has also been an outright liability at least once: #5922 was a hard crash on Databricks raised entirely inside `set_relations_cache` → `list_relations_without_caching`, over a relation type the linter never needed to know about.

Possibly related: #7666 (`--processes N` gives no speedup with the dbt templater) — same theme of fixed templating cost, different cause.

### How to reproduce

Any dbt project with more than a handful of target schemas, against a real warehouse:

1. `time sqlfluff lint models/some_trivial_model.sql`
2. `DBT_POPULATE_CACHE=false time sqlfluff lint models/some_trivial_model.sql`

Both take the same time. Query history on the warehouse shows one `SHOW OBJECTS` per target schema in both runs, before templating starts.

The code path is unconditional, so this reproduces regardless of dialect: `connection()` → `set_relations_cache()` at templater.py#L892.

### Dialect

snowflake (the code path is dialect-independent)

### Version

```
sqlfluff                 4.2.2
sqlfluff-templater-dbt   4.2.2
dbt-core                 1.11.12
dbt-snowflake            1.12.0
dbt-adapters             1.24.5
Python                   3.13.14
```

### Configuration

```ini
[sqlfluff]
templater = dbt
dialect = snowflake
max_line_length = 0
large_file_skip_byte_limit = 0
exclude_rules = LT05, AM04, ST01, ST06, ST07, LT09, RF04, TQ01
```

issues.title: Rule CV12 fix deletes WHERE clause when joined table uses Jinja templating
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When the joined table reference uses a Jinja template expression (e.g. `{{ ref('table') }}`), `sqlfluff fix` with rule CV12 **deletes the entire WHERE clause** instead of moving its conditions to an ON clause. This results in silently corrupted SQL that produces wrong results.

Without Jinja templating on the joined table, the fix works correctly (moves WHERE conditions to ON).

### Expected Behaviour

```sql
-- input.sql
select a.id, b.id as b_id
from table_a as a
left join {{ ref('table_b') }} as b
where a.region = b.region
```

```bash
sqlfluff fix --dialect snowflake --rules CV12 input.sql
```

### Expected result:
```sql
select a.id, b.id as b_id
from table_a as a
left join {{ ref('table_b') }} as b
    on a.region = b.region
```

### Observed Behaviour

```sql
-- input.sql
select a.id, b.id as b_id
from table_a as a
left join {{ ref('table_b') }} as b
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
-- input.sql
select a.id, b.id as b_id
from table_a as a
left join {{ ref('table_b') }} as b
where a.region = b.region
```

```bash
sqlfluff fix --dialect snowflake --rules CV12 input.sql
```
--> see how the `where` is dropped and no `on` is added

### Dialect

snowflake

### Version

4.2.2

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = snowflake
templater = jinja

[sqlfluff:templater:jinja]
apply_dbt_builtins = True

issues.title: Databricks: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW column CONSTRAINT ... EXPECT (...) ON VIOLATION ... unparsable
issues.body:
### What Happened
`TableConstraintSegment` for the databricks dialect only supports PRIMARY KEY / FOREIGN KEY / CHECK. It doesn't support Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines' `EXPECT` data-quality constraint syntax, so any `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` using it is unparsable.

### Expected Behaviour
Should parse. This is valid, documented syntax:
https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/developer/ldp-sql-ref-create-materialized-view

### How to reproduce
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW dim_country (
    country_id INT,
    CONSTRAINT country_id_not_null EXPECT (country_id IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW
)
AS
SELECT 1 AS country_id;
```

### Dialect
databricks

### Version
sqlfluff 4.2.2

issues.title: Oracle dialect: KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST|LAST ORDER BY ...) on aggregate functions is unparsable and produces a spurious AL02 violation
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Oracle's KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST|LAST ORDER BY ...) clause on aggregate functions (MIN, MAX, SUM, AVG, COUNT, VARIANCE, STDDEV) isn't recognized by the oracle dialect grammar. The parser falls back to treating the bare word KEEP as an implicit alias for the aggregate call, then treats everything from the following ( onward as an unparsable section; including any legitimate, already-explicit AS alias that appears later in that same clause. The knock-on effect: rule AL02 (require explicit column aliasing) fires on the phantom KEEP alias, even when the actual column alias is written correctly with AS.

[oracle parser errors · Issue #7313 · sqlfluff/sqlfluff](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/7313) (unrelated/closed - confirms no existing umbrella issue covers this)

### Expected Behaviour

The KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST|LAST ORDER BY ...) clause should parse as part of the aggregate function expression (see Oracle's docs below), and AL02 should not fire when an explicit AS is present.

[FIRST/LAST Aggregate Functions — Oracle SQL Language Reference 19c](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/FIRST.html)

### Observed Behaviour

$ sqlfluff parse --dialect oracle repro.sql
```
select_clause_element:
    function:
        function_name: MAX
        function_contents: (salary)
    alias_expression:
        naked_identifier: 'KEEP'          <-- phantom alias hallucinated from the KEEP keyword
unparsable:                                <-- everything else, including the real "AS best_salary", is dropped here
    (DENSE_RANK LAST ORDER BY commission_pct) AS best_salary
```

$ sqlfluff lint --dialect oracle --rules AL02 repro.sql
`L:   2 | P:  20 | AL02 | Implicit/explicit aliasing of columns. [aliasing.column]`


### How to reproduce

```
SELECT department_id,
       MAX(salary) KEEP (DENSE_RANK LAST ORDER BY commission_pct) AS best_salary
  FROM employees
  GROUP BY department_id;
```
(This is Oracle's own canonical example for the clause, per their SQL Language Reference — see below.)


sqlfluff lint --dialect oracle --rules AL02 repro.sql

[FIRST/LAST Aggregate Functions — Oracle SQL Language Reference 19c](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/FIRST.html)


### Dialect

oracle

### Version

sqlfluff, version 4.0.4 (Python 3.12.3)

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = oracle
rules = AL02

issues.title: BigQuery pipe AGGREGATE/EXTEND clauses can't be indented (LT02 false positive)
issues.body:
# BigQuery pipe `AGGREGATE` / `EXTEND` clauses are not indentable (LT02 false positive)

## Dialect
`bigquery`

## Version
sqlfluff 4.2.2 (also reproduces on `main`)

## Description
In BigQuery [pipe query syntax](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/pipe-syntax),
the `AGGREGATE` and `EXTEND` clauses take a comma-delimited list of
expressions, just like `SELECT` and `GROUP BY`. But unlike `SELECT` /
`GROUP BY`, their grammar emits no `Indent` / `Dedent` metadata around
the list. As a result, `LT02` (layout.indent) flags any continuation
line as *"Line should not be indented"*, and `sqlfluff fix` refuses to
indent them — so a multi-line `AGGREGATE` cannot be written in an
indented style at all.

## Expected Behaviour
A multi-line pipe `AGGREGATE` / `EXTEND` list indents like a `SELECT` or
`GROUP BY` list and lints clean.

## Observed Behaviour
```
$ sqlfluff lint --dialect bigquery example.sql
L:   3 | P:   1 | LT02 | Line should not be indented. [layout.indent]
L:   4 | P:   1 | LT02 | Line should not be indented. [layout.indent]
```

## Steps to Reproduce
Lint this with `--dialect bigquery`:
```sql
FROM my_table
|> AGGREGATE
    SUM(a) AS total_a,
    SUM(b) AS total_b
GROUP BY c
```

## Root cause
`AggregateClauseSegment` and `ExtendClauseSegment` in
`src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_bigquery.py` wrap their `Delimited(...)`
list without `Indent` / `Dedent`, whereas `GroupAndOrderByClauseSegment`
(the `GROUP BY` used within the same pipe syntax) does. Adding
`Indent` / `Dedent` around the two lists resolves it.

issues.title: CV10 corrupts string literals that use quote-doubling escapes (e.g. 'O''Brien' → "O''Brien")
issues.body:
### What Happened

`CV10` (`convention.quoted_literals`) silently changes the **value** of a string literal when it rewrites the quote style, if that literal uses SQL's quote-doubling escape (`''` inside `'…'`, or `""` inside `"…"`).

The rule's normalizer (`_normalize_preferred_quoted_literal_style`) was adapted from Black's Python string handling and understands only **backslash** escaping. SQL escapes an embedded quote by **doubling** it, so when CV10 converts a literal to the other quote char it copies the doubled quotes through unchanged, and they stop being an escape in the new context.

This fires under the **default** config: `preferred_quoted_literal_style = consistent` derives the target quote char from the file's first literal, so any file whose first string is double-quoted will convert later `'…''…'` literals and corrupt them.

### Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff fix` must never change what a query returns. The literal `'O''Brien'` (value `O'Brien`) should either be left alone or re-encoded to an equivalent double-quoted form — not turned into a literal with a different value.

### Observed Behaviour

The value silently changes. `'O''Brien'` → `"O''Brien"`: inside a MySQL double-quoted string `''` is **not** an escape, so the value becomes `O''Brien` (two apostrophes). Confirmed in both directions.

### How to reproduce

```sql
-- t.sql  (default full ruleset, so CV10 runs)
select "x", 'O''Brien' from t
```
```
sqlfluff fix t.sql --dialect mysql -f
```
```sql
-- result
select
    "x",
    "O''Brien"     -- value changed from O'Brien to O''Brien
from t
```
Reverse direction too: `"say ""hi"""` (value `say "hi"`) → `'say ""hi""'` (value `say ""hi""`).

**Control** — the backslash-escape path is fine: `'it\'s'` → `"it's"` (correct). Only the quote-doubling path corrupts, which is why the existing `CV10.yml` fixtures (bigquery, backslash-only) never caught it. Affected dialects are the ones in CV10's list that treat `''`/`""` as escapes (mysql/mariadb; the databricks/hive/sparksql grammars are worth checking too).

### Dialect / Version

`mysql` (and `mariadb`); sqlfluff 4.2.2 (also present on `main` @ 203599e).

### Possible fix / scope question

The raw-string branch already bails out (`return s`) when it can't convert safely. The minimal safe fix is the same: **skip the fix when the literal body contains an unescaped `orig_quote`** (i.e. a bare `'` in a `'…'` string signals quote-doubling this logic can't re-encode). A fuller fix would re-encode the doubling for the target quote char, but that depends on per-dialect escape semantics — I'd rather let you pick the scope. Happy to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer.

---

*Disclosure: this bug was found and this report written by an AI agent (Claude Code), running autonomously on this account; every repro above was executed against 4.2.2, not taken on trust.*

issues.title: CV11 swaps the arguments of MySQL CONVERT(expr, type)
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues. (The existing MySQL `CONVERT` issues — #6277, #6255 — are about `ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET`, which is unrelated.)

### What Happened

MySQL's `CONVERT` takes its arguments the other way round from T-SQL's: `CONVERT(expr, type)` rather than `CONVERT(type, expr)`. CV11 assumes the T-SQL order for every dialect, so on `mysql` it rewrites the two arguments into a `CAST` the wrong way round — silently, because the result still parses.

I'm opening an issue rather than a PR because the right fix looks like a judgement call, and I'd rather ask than guess. Details at the bottom.

### Expected Behaviour

```sql
SELECT CONVERT(b, SIGNED) FROM t
```

should either be rewritten to `CAST(b AS SIGNED)`, or left alone — but not have its arguments swapped.

### Observed Behaviour

`sqlfluff fix` produces a cast of the *type name* to the *column*:

```sql
SELECT cast(SIGNED as b) FROM t
```

`SIGNED` is now the value being cast and `b` is the target type. `DECIMAL(10,2)` goes the same way:

```
CONVERT(b, DECIMAL(10,2))  ->  cast(DECIMAL(10,2) as b)
```

For contrast, the same rule on `tsql` — where the argument order it assumes is the real one — is correct:

```
tsql:  CONVERT(INT, b)  ->  cast(b as INT)     # right
mysql: CONVERT(b, SIGNED)  ->  cast(SIGNED as b)  # wrong
```

`CONVERT(b USING utf8mb4)` is correctly left alone.

### How to reproduce

`.sqlfluff`:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = mysql
rules = CV11

[sqlfluff:rules:convention.casting_style]
preferred_type_casting_style = cast
```

`a.sql`:

```sql
SELECT CONVERT(b, SIGNED) FROM t
```

```
$ sqlfluff fix --rules CV11 -f a.sql
$ cat a.sql
SELECT cast(SIGNED as b) FROM t
```

### Dialect

`mysql`, and the dialects that inherit it: `mariadb`, `doris`, `starrocks`.

### Version

```
$ sqlfluff --version
python -m sqlfluff, version 4.2.2
```
Reproduced on `main` at e92448c.

---

### Why I'm asking instead of sending a patch

While digging into this I found the surrounding picture is a bit more tangled than "CV11 has the argument order wrong", and I don't want to pick a direction on your behalf:

**Most MySQL `CONVERT` forms don't parse at all today.** `CONVERT(b, CHAR)` and `CONVERT(price, UNSIGNED)` are unparsable in the `mysql` dialect:

```
L:   1 | P:  15 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 15: Found unparsable section: '(b, CHAR)'
```

They're untouched by CV11 not because anything guards them, but because parsing already failed. `CONVERT(b, SIGNED)` happens to parse — `SIGNED` isn't a reserved keyword, so it comes through as a plain `column_reference` — and that's the case that gets mangled. `grep -i convert dialect_mysql.py` only turns up `ALTER ... CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET`, so as far as I can tell the `mysql` dialect doesn't model `CONVERT(expr, type)` at all.

So there seem to be two ways to go, and they're quite different in scope:

1. **Teach the `mysql` dialect about `CONVERT(expr, type)`**, which would fix the unparsable forms too and let CV11 rewrite it correctly.
2. **Have CV11 decline to rewrite `CONVERT` on the MySQL-family dialects.** This stops the corruption but leaves the unparsable forms as they are.

For what it's worth, (2) has a precedent sitting in the same function — the `cast_expression` branch already refuses to touch dialect-specific variants for exactly this reasoning:

> CV11 can only rewrite the standard `::` shorthand. Dialect-specific variants such as Databricks `?::` (try_cast) and Vertica `::!` (null cast) are not interchangeable with CAST/CONVERT, so rewriting them would change semantics (and may even be unparsable).

MySQL's `CONVERT` looks like the same category to me. But (1) is clearly the more complete answer, and you'd know better than I would whether it's wanted.

Happy to put up a PR for whichever you'd prefer.

`CV11.yml` currently has no `mysql`/`mariadb` cases, which is presumably why this hasn't surfaced.

### Disclosure

AI-assisted, and I'd rather say so plainly. Everything above — the reproducer, the tsql contrast, the unparsable forms, the dialect grep — I ran and read myself rather than assumed.

issues.title: Unparsable Snowflake Dynamic Table Keywords and Stream-on-DynamicTable Syntax
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

sqlfluff fails to parse the following valid Snowflake syntax:

- INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE parameter in CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE statements
- REFRESH_MODE = ADAPTIVE parameter in CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE statements
- CREATE STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE syntax for change data capture streams

sqlfluff reports parsing errors for these valid Snowflake statements and the sections are marked as unparsable.

### Expected Behaviour

1. sqlfluff should successfully parse INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE as a valid parameter in dynamic table creation

2. sqlfluff should successfully parse REFRESH_MODE with the value ADAPTIVE as it does with the other values FULL and INCREMENTAL

3. sqlfluff should recognize CREATE STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE as a valid stream creation syntax

### Observed Behaviour

When sqlfluff attempts to parse the SQL files containing these Snowflake constructs, the following issues occur:

1.  INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE Parameter:

> 

> - sqlfluff fails to recognize INITIALIZATION_WAREHOUSE as a valid parameter in the CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE statement
> - The parser flags this line as an unparsable section and doesn't format it properly.

2.  REFRESH_MODE Parameter:

> 
> - sqlfluff does not recognize REFRESH_MODE = ADAPTIVE as valid syntax
> - The parameter is treated as unparsable, causing the parser to report an error on the line
> - Valid refresh mode values REFRESH_MODE = FULL/INCREMENTAL both are parsed properly

3. CREATE STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE Syntax:
> 
> - sqlfluff does not recognize ON DYNAMIC TABLE as a valid target for stream creation
> - The parser properly recognizes ON TABLE and ON VIEW as valid stream targets
> - Attempting to create a stream on a dynamic table results in parse errors


### How to reproduce

Snowflake

### Version

issues.title: Postgres: add support for GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) VIRTUAL
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

[PostgreSQL18](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createforeigntable.html) has added virtual [generated columns](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-generated-columns.html).

`VIRTUAL` seems to be [unreserved / non-reserved](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blame/1ae87df63ff693a91fbcb968850103a5a5d8cd96/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L19246). Also `STORED` isn't anymore required, and defaults to `VIRTUAL` if both are omitted.

Does `sqlfluff` have support for restricting this only for Postgres v18, and still failing on <= v17?

issues.title: Rename Rust `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code` helpers
issues.body:
This name collides with Python but has inverted semantics.

## Problem

The Rust parser has three backward-skip-to-code helpers whose names and semantics are misaligned with each other and with the Python reference. The helper whose name is identical to Python's canonical function has the opposite comment-handling behavior, which is a trap for anyone porting from Python.

Python's canonical `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code` (src/sqlfluff/core/parser/match_algorithms.py:32) checks only is_code, i.e. it excludes comments. So:

- The Rust method named `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code` does not match Python's `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code` (it keeps comments).
- The helper that does match Python is the one with the longer _excluding_comments suffix.
- Two definitions share the exact name but differ in return convention (idx vs idx + 1).

Proposed change (naming only — no behavior change)

Make the name that matches Python carry the Python semantics:

- Rename the comment-keeping method helpers.rs:142 → `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code_or_comment` (name states what it actually keeps).
- Rename the comment-excluding helper (_excluding_comments, added in #8118) → `skip_stop_index_backward_to_code` so it lines up with the Python function it mirrors.
- Consider collapsing the match_algorithms.rs:73 free fn into the same helper, or at least reconciling the idx vs idx + 1 return convention so the two "code-only" helpers don't silently differ by one. (The free fn's caller at :256 adds +1 itself, so a shared idx + 1 version would let the call site drop the manual +1.)

## Context

Follow-up from PR #8118 review, which added the `_excluding_comments` variant to fix GREEDY Bracketed absorbing trailing trivia. The doc comments there mitigate the confusion but don't remove the underlying naming trap.

issues.title: CTE Materialization hints are not properly parsed in SQLite dialect
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

SQLite has support for non-standard SQL syntax `AS MATERIALIZED` and `AS NOT MATERIALIZED` in CTE definitions. (see: [The WITH Clause: Materialization Hints](https://sqlite.org/lang_with.html#materialization_hints)).
This syntax originates from Postgres. 

SQLFluff parses these materialization hints properly for the Postgres dialect (see: [dialect_postgres.py:6058](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/4.2.2/src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_postgres.py#L6058)) but not for SQLite.

### Expected Behaviour

The example should be properly linted for SQLite dialect.

### Observed Behaviour

With the example from the section below, SQLFluff returns the following:
```
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'WITH cte
                       | AS MATERIALIZED (\n    SELECT co...'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'sqlite'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

In comparison, SQLFluff returns the following with option `--dialect postgres`

```
All Finished 📜 🎉!
```

### How to reproduce

`query.sql`
```sql
WITH cte AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT col FROM table
)

SELECT col FROM cte
```

Command to run: `sqlfluff lint --dialect sqlite query.sql`

### Dialect

SQLite

### Version

sqlfluff, version 4.2.2
python, 3.14.6

No configuration needed with the command provided above (or just a bare configuration file that sets `dialect` to `sqlite`)

issues.title: Snowflake: Missing support for WITH TAG clause in CREATE TASK definition causes unparsable section error
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

The following Snowflake CREATE TASK statement is valid Snowflake syntax, but SQLFluff reports an unparsable section when the task definition uses WITH TAG:

```
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK GLOBAL_SANDBOX.SHARED_PLAYGROUND.SELECT_ONE_TASK
    WITH TAG (GLOBAL_SANDBOX.SHARED_PLAYGROUND.data_owner = 'data_team')
    SCHEDULE = 'USING CRON 0 0 1 1 * UTC'
AS
    SELECT 1;
```

Removing the tag clause, removes the issue again

```
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK GLOBAL_SANDBOX.SHARED_PLAYGROUND.SELECT_ONE_TASK
    SCHEDULE = 'USING CRON 0 0 1 1 * UTC'
AS
    SELECT 1;
```

### Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff should parse Snowflake CREATE TASK statements that include WITH TAG without reporting an unparsable section.
For example, this should parse successfully:

```
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK GLOBAL_SANDBOX.SHARED_PLAYGROUND.SELECT_ONE_TASK
    WITH TAG (GLOBAL_SANDBOX.SHARED_PLAYGROUND.data_owner = 'data_team')
    SCHEDULE = 'USING CRON 0 0 1 1 * UTC'
AS
    SELECT 1
```

### Observed Behaviour

SQLFluff shows an unparsable section (PRS) error when run on a CREATE TASK clause that contains WITH TAG.

### How to reproduce

`sqlfluff.exe lint -i .\sqlfluff.ini --dialect snowflake repro.sql`

issues.title: [Snowflake] SYSTEM$-prefixed functions cause PRS error
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When linting a Snowflake query that uses a SYSTEM$ built-in function (e.g. SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME()) inside a SELECT clause, SQLFluff fails to parse the statement. The parser probably treats the $ in the function name as a token boundary, so it cannot recognise SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME() as a single function call. This produces a PRS error.


### Expected Behaviour

SQLFluff should parse SYSTEM$-prefixed functions (such as SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME, SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_DEPTH, SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA, etc.) as valid Snowflake built-in functions. The query should parse cleanly, the explicit AS aliases should be recognised, and no PRS or other rule violations should be raised.

### Observed Behaviour

Linting the query below raises a PRS error:

```sql
SELECT
    A.COL_1,
    SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME() AS TASK_NAME,
    IFF(SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME() <> '', SYSTEM$CURRENT_USER_TASK_NAME(), CURRENT_USER()) AS LOAD_USER
FROM (SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SEQ4()) AS COL_1 FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 5))) A;
``` 
```
violations:
  - start_line_no: 3
    start_line_pos: 5
    code: AL03
    description: Column expression without alias. Use explicit `AS` clause.
    name: aliasing.expression
    warning: false
  - start_line_no: 3
    start_line_pos: 37
    code: PRS
    description: "Line 3, Position 37: Found unparsable section: 'AS TASK_NAME,\\n    IFF(SYSTEM$CURRENT_USE...'"
    name: ''
    warning: false
``` 
This query is valid Snowflake SQL and executes without any error. It returns the expected result set (TASK_NAME is empty this time because the statement is run directly by a user rather than from a task).
| COL_1 | TASK_NAME | LOAD_USER |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 |  | DUMMYUSER |
| 2 |  | DUMMYUSER |
| 3 |  | DUMMYUSER |
| 4 |  | DUMMYUSER |
| 5 |  | DUMMYUSER |

issues.title: ClickHouse: GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS / ROLLUP / CUBE modifiers are unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

ClickHouse's `GROUP BY` modifiers `WITH TOTALS`, `WITH ROLLUP` and `WITH CUBE`
produce an unparsable section in the `clickhouse` dialect.

### Expected behaviour

The statements parse; the modifier is recognised as part of the `GROUP BY`
clause.

### Observed behaviour

```
L1:P37 PRS: Found unparsable section: 'WITH TOTALS'
```

(equivalently `WITH ROLLUP` / `WITH CUBE`)

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT a, count() FROM t GROUP BY a WITH TOTALS
SELECT a, count() FROM t GROUP BY a WITH ROLLUP
SELECT a, count() FROM t GROUP BY a WITH CUBE
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

All three are valid and were verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/group-by

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12. Also applies to `main` — the only
change to the ClickHouse dialect grammar since 4.2.2 is the ternary operator
(#8016).

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: non-reserved keywords (keys, order, rows, inner, on, union, case, ...) rejected as identifiers
issues.body:
### What happened

ClickHouse documents that keywords are **not reserved** — a word is a keyword
only in its syntactic context — so words like `keys`, `order`, `rows`, `inner`,
`on`, `format`, `overlaps`, `where`, `limit`, `settings`, `union`, `case` are
legal unquoted column names and aliases. The `clickhouse` dialect rejects them
in identifier position.

### Expected behaviour

These words parse as identifiers when used in identifier position (alias,
column reference, function argument).

### Observed behaviour

Two surfaces:

**As an alias** — all of `keys, order, rows, inner, on, format, overlaps, where,
limit, settings, union, case` PRS:

```
SELECT x AS keys FROM t   ->  L1:P10 PRS: Found unparsable section: 'AS keys'
```

**As a function argument / column reference** — `order, rows, inner, on, union,
case` PRS:

```
SELECT sum(order) FROM t  ->  L1:P11 PRS: Found unparsable section: '(order)'
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT x AS keys FROM t
SELECT x AS order FROM t
SELECT sum(order) FROM t
SELECT sum(rows) FROM t
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2: all 12 words accepted unquoted as aliases; all of
`order, rows, inner, on, union, case` accepted unquoted as function arguments.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/syntax — "Keywords are not
reserved."

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: identifiers beginning with a digit (e.g. 30_day_cm3) are unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

Unquoted identifiers that begin with a digit but contain letters
(`3s_video_views`, `30_day_cm3`) are reported as unparsable — both as column
references and as aliases.

### Expected behaviour

They parse as identifiers.

Note: ClickHouse's syntax docs describe the stricter regex
`^[a-zA-Z_][0-9a-zA-Z_]*$` for non-quoted identifiers, but in practice the
ClickHouse parser accepts digit-leading names unquoted (verified on 26.4.2 —
see below). So this may be best addressed as relaxed lexing and/or a config
opt-in rather than unconditionally; happy to follow whatever policy the team
prefers.

### Observed behaviour

```
SELECT 3s_video_views FROM t      ->  L1:P8  PRS: Found unparsable section: '3s_video_views'
SELECT 1 AS 30_day_cm3            ->  L1:P13 PRS: Found unparsable section: 'AS 30_day_cm3'
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT 3s_video_views FROM t
SELECT 1 AS 30_day_cm3
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2: `SELECT 3s_video_views FROM t`,
`SELECT 1 AS 3s_video_views`, `SELECT 1 AS 30_day_cm3` all accepted unquoted.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/syntax#identifiers

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: SELECT * EXCEPT col without parentheses is unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

The parenthesised column-exclusion modifier `* EXCEPT (col)` parses, but the
unparenthesised single-column form `* EXCEPT col` does not (also `t.* EXCEPT col`).

Related: #7654 added `APPLY(...)` and #7999 fixed an RF02 false positive on
`* EXCEPT (...)`. The remaining gap is the unparenthesised `EXCEPT` spelling.

### Expected behaviour

Both `* EXCEPT col` and `* EXCEPT (c1, c2)` parse.

### Observed behaviour

```
SELECT * EXCEPT c FROM t    ->  L1:P10 PRS: Found unparsable section: 'EXCEPT c FROM t'
SELECT t.* EXCEPT c FROM t  ->  L1:P12 PRS: Found unparsable section: 'EXCEPT c FROM t'
```

For contrast, `SELECT * EXCEPT (c) FROM t` and `SELECT * EXCEPT (c1, c2) FROM t`
parse fine.

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT * EXCEPT c FROM t
SELECT t.* EXCEPT c FROM t
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Valid, verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select#except

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.body:
### What happened

ClickHouse accepts `==` as a synonym for `=` (both map to `equals()`).
The `clickhouse` dialect reports `==` as an unparsable section.

### Expected behaviour

`a == b` parses as an equality comparison (equivalent to `a = b`).

### Observed behaviour

```
L1:P25 PRS: Found unparsable section: '== 1'
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT a FROM t WHERE a == 1
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Valid, verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/operators (comparison operators).

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: tuple element access .N on a parenthesised / subscript / literal expression is unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

Tuple element access by dot-index works on a bare identifier (`x.1`, `x.1.2`
parse) but fails whenever the left-hand side ends in `)` or `]` — i.e. a
function call, a subscript, or a tuple literal.

Follow-up to #3816 (tuple access, fixed for the identifier case) — the
expression-prefixed cases remain.

### Expected behaviour

`<expr>.N` tuple-element access parses whenever `<expr>` is a tuple-valued
expression, including function calls, subscripts and tuple literals.

### Observed behaviour

```
SELECT f(x).2 FROM t    ->  L1:P12 PRS: Found unparsable section: '.2'
SELECT arr[1].2 FROM t  ->  L1:P14 PRS: Found unparsable section: '.2'
SELECT (a, b).1 FROM t  ->  L1:P14 PRS: Found unparsable section: '.1'
```

For contrast, these already parse: `SELECT x.1 FROM t`, `SELECT x.1.2 FROM t`.

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT f(x).2 FROM t
SELECT arr[1].2 FROM t
SELECT (a, b).1 FROM t
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Valid, verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2 (`(tuple(1,2)).2`, `[tuple(1,2)][1].2`,
`(a, b).1` all accepted).
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/data-types/tuple

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: ORDER BY / LIMIT / SETTINGS on a non-final UNION member is unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

ClickHouse permits `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT` and `SETTINGS` on an individual,
non-final member of a `UNION` (without wrapping the member in parentheses).
sqlfluff treats everything from `UNION` onward as unparsable when a left-hand
member carries one of those clauses.

Related, already fixed: #7120 / #7600 fixed `SETTINGS` for the union as a whole.
The remaining gap is clauses attached to a **non-final member** of an
unparenthesised `UNION`.

### Expected behaviour

Each member of a `UNION` may carry its own `ORDER BY` / `LIMIT` / `SETTINGS`.

### Observed behaviour

These PRS (clause on the first/left member):

```
SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u            -> PRS 'UNION ALL ...'
SELECT a FROM t LIMIT 10 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u              -> PRS 'UNION ALL ...'
SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a LIMIT 10 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u   -> PRS 'UNION ALL ...'
SELECT a FROM t SETTINGS max_threads = 1 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u -> PRS 'UNION ALL ...'
```

These already parse (shown for contrast — the gap is specifically the non-final
member):

```
SELECT a FROM t UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u ORDER BY a               -- ok (tail)
SELECT a FROM t UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u SETTINGS max_threads = 1 -- ok (tail)
(SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a LIMIT 1) UNION ALL (SELECT b FROM u)   -- ok (parenthesised)
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a LIMIT 10 UNION ALL SELECT b FROM u
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Valid, verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/union

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

### Configuration

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: ClickHouse: LIMIT n BY with multiple columns is unparsable
issues.body:
### What happened

`LIMIT n BY a` parses, but a comma-separated column list `LIMIT n BY a, b`
leaves the trailing column(s) unparsable.

This is a follow-up to #5494 (single-column `LIMIT BY`, fixed) — the multi-column
form still fails.

### Expected behaviour

`LIMIT n BY <expr> [, <expr>]...` accepts a list of expressions.

### Observed behaviour

```
SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1 BY a, b  ->  L1:P29 PRS: Found unparsable section: ', b'
SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1 BY a     ->  parses fine
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
SELECT * FROM t LIMIT 1 BY a, b
```

```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse -
```

Valid, verified on ClickHouse 26.4.2.
Docs: https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/limit-by

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff 4.2.2 (latest release), Python 3.12; also applies to `main`.

None — default rules, `--dialect clickhouse`.

issues.title: [Oracle]: parsing error with INTERVAL data types
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When formatting Oracle SQL statements, layout rules are not applied if the target type of a CAST expression is an INTERVAL data type.

For example, the following statement remains unchanged after formatting:

`select cast(type_char as interval year(9) to month) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

The same behaviour is reproducible with the following Oracle interval types:

interval year to month
interval year(9) to month
interval day to second
interval day(2) to second(6)

### Expected Behaviour

The formatter should apply layout rules to statements containing Oracle INTERVAL data types in CAST expressions.

With the following configuration:

```
[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
keyword_line_position = leading
```

the following statement:

`select cast(type_char as interval year(9) to month) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

should be formatted as:

```
select cast(type_char as interval year(9) to month) as val
from sample_types
where id = 1;
```

### Observed Behaviour

The statement is left unchanged after formatting.

Layout rules such as moving the FROM and WHERE clauses onto separate lines are not applied.

### How to reproduce

Configure SQLFluff to use the Oracle dialect.
Use the following configuration:

```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = oracle
[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
keyword_line_position = leading
```

Format the following statement:

`select cast(type_char as interval year(9) to month) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

Observe that the statement remains on a single line.

The same behaviour can be reproduced with:

```
select cast(type_char as interval year to month) as val from sample_types where id = 1; 
select cast(type_char as interval day to second) as val from sample_types where id = 1; 
select cast(type_char as interval day(2) to second(6)) as val from sample_types where id = 1;
```

### Dialect

Oracle

### Version

SQLFluff 4.1.0

### Configuration

```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = oracle

[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
keyword_line_position = leading
```

issues.title: [Oracle]: parsing error with TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE data type
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

When formatting Oracle SQL, layout rules are not applied to statements containing CAST(... AS TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE) or CAST(... AS TIMESTAMP(<precision>) WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE).

For example, the following statement remains unchanged after formatting:

`select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

Expected output:

```
select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val
from sample_types
where id = 1;
```

The issue is reproducible with SQLFluff 4.1.0 using the Oracle dialect.

The same statement is formatted correctly when TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE is replaced with any of the following:

DATE
TIMESTAMP
TIMESTAMP(<precision>)
TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
TIMESTAMP(<precision>) WITH TIME ZONE

### Expected Behaviour

The formatter should apply layout rules to SQL statements containing TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE in the same way as it does for other Oracle data types.

With the following configuration:

```
[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
```

the statement

`select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

should be formatted as:

```
select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val
from sample_types
where id = 1;
```

### Observed Behaviour

Layout rules are not applied when the statement contains TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE or TIMESTAMP(<precision>) WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE in a CAST expression.

The statement remains unchanged after formatting. For example:

Input:

`select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

Output:

`select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

The same statement is formatted correctly when TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE is replaced with DATE, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMP(<precision>), TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, or TIMESTAMP(<precision>) WITH TIME ZONE.

### How to reproduce

Configure SQLFluff to use the Oracle dialect.
Configure the from_clause layout rule:
```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = oracle
[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
keyword_line_position = leading
```

Format the following SQL statement:
`select cast(type_char as timestamp with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

Observe that the statement remains on a single line instead of moving the FROM and WHERE clauses onto separate lines.

The same behavior is reproducible with:

`select cast(type_char as timestamp(9) with local time zone) as val from sample_types where id = 1;`

### Dialect

Oracle

### Version

SQLFluff 4.1.0

### Configuration

```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = oracle

[sqlfluff:layout:type:from_clause]
line_position = alone
keyword_line_position = leading
```

issues.title: [ClickHouse]: unparsable ternary conditional operator cond ? a : b
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

ClickHouse supports a C-style ternary conditional operator, cond ? then : else, as shorthand for if(cond, then, else). sqlfluff's clickhouse dialect fails to parse it: everything from the ? onward is captured in an unparsable segment, which surfaces as a PRS violation on lint and prevents layout/whitespace rules from being applied to the statement.

### Expected Behaviour

col = '' ? 0 : 1 AS x should parse as a conditional expression (semantically equivalent to if(col = '', 0, 1) AS x), the same way ClickHouse itself accepts it.



### Observed Behaviour

$ sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse tern.sql
...
[L:  1, P: 14]      |                        quoted_literal:                       "''"
[L:  1, P: 16]      |                [META] dedent:
[L:  1, P: 17]      |                unparsable:                                   !! Expected: 'Nothing here.'
[L:  1, P: 17]      |                    question:                                 '?'
[L:  1, P: 19]      |                    numeric_literal:                          '0'
[L:  1, P: 21]      |                    colon:                                    ':'
[L:  1, P: 23]      |                    numeric_literal:                          '1'
[L:  1, P: 25]      |                    word:                                     'AS'
[L:  1, P: 28]      |                    word:                                     'x'
...

### How to reproduce

-- tern.sql
SELECT col = '' ? 0 : 1 AS x FROM t

sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse tern.sql
sqlfluff lint  --dialect clickhouse tern.sql   # reports PRS (unparsable section)

### Dialect

clickhouse

### Version

sqlfluff version: 4.2.2

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = clickhouse

issues.title: Databricks View doesn't support long_lines ignore_comment_clauses setting
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

The ignore_comment_clauses = True for the layout.long_lines rule (LT05) doesn't work with a Databricks syntax CREATE VIEW with a COMMENT. When running a lint, it fails with a "Line is too long" error.

### Expected Behaviour

The `ignore_comment_clauses = True` should skip the rule for COMMENT clauses within CREATE VIEW statements.

### Observed Behaviour

I received the error:
```
L:   2 | P:   1 | LT05 | Line is too long (654 > 100).
                       | [layout.long_lines]
```

### How to reproduce

Create a test_view.sql with:

```sql
CREATE VIEW my_schema.my_view
COMMENT 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Integer nec dignissim diam, eu consectetur dolor. Aliquam vestibulum hendrerit massa ac dapibus. Duis luctus ut nunc quis mollis. Pellentesque at ultricies justo. Mauris nulla metus, posuere in lorem eget, mattis eleifend dui. In ullamcorper, enim id posuere mattis, urna ex tempus ipsum, ac bibendum neque arcu at mi. Pellentesque ultricies rutrum nibh a accumsan. Morbi non fermentum eros. Sed at nisl et purus suscipit congue. Vestibulum auctor vehicula maximus. In semper felis neque, eu condimentum lacus pharetra ut. Curabitur nibh metus, dapibus sed tellus ac, commodo porta orci.'
AS
SELECT 1 AS col
```

Set .sqlfluff to:
```
[sqlfluff]
dialect = databricks
max_line_length = 100

[sqlfluff:rules:layout.long_lines]
ignore_comment_clauses = True
```

Run `sqlfluff lint test_view.sql`.

The error should be raised.

Functions operate correctly and no errors are raised.
```sql
CREATE FUNCTION my_schema.my_function ()
RETURNS TABLE
COMMENT 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Integer nec dignissim diam, eu consectetur dolor. Aliquam vestibulum hendrerit massa ac dapibus. Duis luctus ut nunc quis mollis. Pellentesque at ultricies justo. Mauris nulla metus, posuere in lorem eget, mattis eleifend dui. In ullamcorper, enim id posuere mattis, urna ex tempus ipsum, ac bibendum neque arcu at mi. Pellentesque ultricies rutrum nibh a accumsan. Morbi non fermentum eros. Sed at nisl et purus suscipit congue. Vestibulum auctor vehicula maximus. In semper felis neque, eu condimentum lacus pharetra ut. Curabitur nibh metus, dapibus sed tellus ac, commodo porta orci.'
RETURN
SELECT 1 AS col
```

### Dialect

Databricks

### Version

sqlfluff, version 4.2.1
Python 3.11.9

### Configuration

issues.title: Parsing error on oracle PIVOT and UNPIVOT when using where and numeric literals
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

While deploying sqlfluff on a project with hundreds of Oracle queries, I am running into a few unparsable sections where we are using the PIVOT and UNPIVOT clauses.

The code runs and yields expected results, but the parser is unable to parse.


### Expected Behaviour

- When using PIVOT or UNPIVOT, I should be able to also use a WHERE clause without errors.
- When using UNPIVOT, numeric labels should be able to parse.

### Observed Behaviour

Specifically, I have two related bugs:
- When using PIVOT or UNPIVOT, a parsing error appears only if a WHERE clause is also used, the parser works if I remove the WHERE clause.
- When using UNPIVOT, a parsing error appears when I use numeric labels instead of characters, even though it is permitted by Oracle. Character labels are also parsed as `identifiers` instead of `literals` which contradicts the documentation. 

### How to reproduce

Here are sample sql queries that showcase every error mentionned, modified from the current test cases. The first one also showcases that the labels are parsed as identifiers instead of literals.

```
-- unpivot does not parse before a where clause, labels are parsed as identifiers
select
    quantity,
    product_code
from sale_stats
unpivot
(
    quantity
    for product_code
    in (
        product_a as 'A', -- <- labels are literals, not identifiers
        product_b as 'B',
        product_c as 'C'
    )
)
where
    quantity > 0;

-- pivot does not parse before a where clause either
select * from (
    select
        times_purchased,
        state_code
    from customers
) purchases
pivot
(
    count(state_code)
    for state_code in (select distinct state_code from state)
)
where
    state_code in ('NY', 'CT', 'NJ', 'FL', 'MO');

-- unpivot does not parse when using numeric labels
select
    quantity,
    product_id
from sale_stats
unpivot
(
    quantity
    for product_id
    in (
        product_a as 1, -- <- should parse
        product_b as 2,
        product_c as 3
    )
);
```
(as a file: [pivot_unpivot.sql](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29101900/pivot_unpivot.sql))

issues.title: LT05: _is_templated_safe_break incomplete — corrupts SQL with mixed literal+Jinja lines
issues.body:
## Description

The `_is_templated_safe_break` guard added in #7640 (released in 4.1.0) only catches the case where **both** adjacent segments at a break point are non-literal (within template expansion). It misses the case where **one side is literal SQL and the other is a rendered Jinja template** — which is the common pattern in dbt models.

## Environment

- sqlfluff: 4.2.2
- templater: dbt (dbt-bigquery 1.10)
- dialect: bigquery

## Observed behavior

When running `sqlfluff fix` on ~268 dbt model files in bulk (BigQuery dialect, dbt templater), we observed:

1. **Duplicated lines** — a SQL line containing a mix of literal SQL and Jinja macro calls was duplicated during LT05 line-breaking
2. **Truncated logic** — complex SQL expressions were split at a break point between a literal segment and a template segment, and trailing clauses were lost
3. **Silent semantic changes** — the fixed SQL compiled and ran without errors, but produced different (incorrect) results

All three files had long lines with mixed literal SQL + Jinja (e.g., `SELECT col1, {{ macro_call() }}, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS(context.time) AS ...`).

## Root cause analysis

The `_is_templated_safe_break` function at `sqlfluff/utils/reflow/reindent.py:2403` checks:

```python
# Unsafe only if BOTH sides are non-literal (within template expansion).
return before_literal or after_literal
```

This returns `True` (safe) when one side is literal and the other is templated. But inserting a line break at such a boundary can still cause corruption because the template expansion may span across what sqlfluff considers independent segments. The rendered template content can't always be cleanly split at arbitrary literal/non-literal boundaries.

## Expected behavior

`_is_templated_safe_break` should be more conservative — either:
1. Flag a break as unsafe if **either** adjacent segment is non-literal (not just both)
2. Or check whether the break point falls within a broader template span, not just the immediately adjacent segments

## Workaround

Exclude `layout.long_lines` from auto-fix when running on files that haven't been previously linted:
```
sqlfluff fix --exclude-rules layout.long_lines
```

## Related

- #7639 (original report, fixed by #7640 but fix is incomplete)
- #6098 (dbt templater producing incorrect SQL with duplicated macro lines)
- #5667 (related duplication issue)

issues.title: [postgres] PG01 rule misleading check for NOT VALID
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

The [PG01](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/reference/rules.html#rule-PG01) rule added in 4.2.2 patch release (#7832) checks for excessive locks in PostgreSQL DDL statements:
```
CREATE INDEX → use CONCURRENTLY (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX excluded)
DROP INDEX → use CONCURRENTLY
REINDEX → use CONCURRENTLY
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW → use CONCURRENTLY
ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY → use NOT VALID
```

The last check did not pass in our CI so I read a little more about it in the [PostgreSQL docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-altertable.html#SQL-ALTERTABLE-DESC-ADD-TABLE-CONSTRAINT).
From my understanding, `NOT VALID` allows to skip a lengthy scan by marking existing rows as "NOT VALID" while allowing concurrent insert and updates (which are checked against the added constraint). However, it requires a [`VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-altertable.html#SQL-ALTERTABLE-DESC-VALIDATE-CONSTRAINT) later in order to validate the constraint previously created as `NOT VALID`.

From the Examples section:
> To add a foreign key constraint to a table with the least impact on other work:
> 
> ```
> ALTER TABLE distributors ADD CONSTRAINT distfk FOREIGN KEY (address) 
>   REFERENCES addresses (address) NOT VALID;
> ALTER TABLE distributors VALIDATE CONSTRAINT distfk;
> ```

IMO this may lead users to apply an insufficient fix: simply adding `NOT VALID`, as stated in the rule description, is not enough.


### Expected Behaviour

IMO the check for `NOT VALID` in `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY` differs significantly from the other index-related `CONCURRENTLY` checks in `PG01`.

I would expect the check to be moved out from `PG01` to a specific rule (`PG02`?) with a more detailed description on how to fix it.

Also, the [changelog](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#422---2026-06-04) should mention the added PG01 instead of the CV13

> There are also rule and templater fixes, **including a new Postgres-specific CV13 rule to prefer CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY**, fewer ST11 false positives for LEFT SEMI and LEFT ANTI joins, and dbt templater support for the DBT_TARGET and DBT_TARGET_PATH environment variables. Performance is also improved by deferring parse-tree serialisation in logging calls.


A final thought: patch releases should not include new rules or maybe introduce them as warnings until they get stabilized?

```console
Python 3.12.0
```

issues.title: Databricks: Missing Syntax Support For `?::` as a Shorthand For `TRY_CAST`
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Unable to parse statements containing the "question double colon" (`?::`) shorthand syntax for `try_cast` using databricks dialect.

### Expected Behaviour

Section is parsed and no error is raised.

### Observed Behaviour

When parsing 

```
SELECT 1?::INT
```

as dialect databricks

We get 

L:   1 | P:   9 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 9: Found unparsable section: '?::INT'


Even though this is valid syntax in databricks as of version 15.3 and above

https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/functions/questiondoublecolonsign

### How to reproduce

Create a file called "test.sql" containing this text:

```
SELECT 1?::INT
```

run `sqlfluff lint --dialect databricks`

observe 
L:   1 | P:   9 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 9: Found unparsable section: '?::INT'

### Dialect

Databricks 

### Version

sqlfluff, version 4.2.2

### Configuration

Empty

I tried a couple of things:
* Move from block comment to three single line comments, then it works
* Move from `min` to `max` or other functions, still fails
* Move the `min(` part a line up so it's `/* min(` still fails
* Move the `AS type_arr` a line up so it's `) AS type_arr`, then it works
* Move the `)` a line up so it's `min()`, then it works

This indicates to me, that sqlfluff is unnecessarily trying to parse the block comment.

athena

issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

We are seeing AL04 violations after upgrading from 3.1.1 to 4.2.1 when we have identical aliases across multiple CTEs.

This appears to be related to changes made for https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues/6326.

Similar to the override added for AL02, perhaps a similar override can be provided here as this is not uncommon, nor is it wrong.


### Expected Behaviour

As long as the aliases are within separate CTEs, I would not expect an error to be flagged.

### Observed Behaviour

```
  FROM dim_dates AS dd

  SELECT
    dd.date AS second_date
  FROM dim_dates AS dd
)

  second_cte.second_date
```

issues.title: ST11 (structure.unused_join) false positives for `LEFT SEMI` and `LEFT ANTI` joins
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

`sqlfluff lint` on a SQL file containing a `LEFT SEMI` join or `LEFT ANTI` join produces false positives for the [ST11 rule](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/reference/rules.html#rule-ST11).

Note that the inclusion of `LEFT` is optional and it's that which triggers the rule.

See [Spark SQL join types](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-ref-syntax-qry-select-join.html#join-types).

### Expected Behaviour

No ST11 failure.

The ST11 docs say:

>Because some types of joins are often used as filters or to otherwise control granularity without being referenced (e.g. INNER and CROSS), this rule only applies to explicit OUTER joins (i.e. LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL joins).

SEMI and ANTI joins are _always_ "used as filters" so should also be excluded.

### Observed Behaviour

```
ST11 | Joined table 'tab2 AS r' not referenced elsewhere in query [structure.unused_join]
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
-- test.sql
SELECT l.id
FROM tab1 AS l
LEFT SEMI JOIN tab2 AS r
    ON l.id = r.id;
```

```sh
sqlfluff lint --dialect sparksql test.sql
```

### Dialect

`sparksql` and `databricks`

issues.body:
### Search before asking

### What Happened

Given this input:

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (
    time_updated timestamp NOT NULL
    DEFAULT current_timestamp()
    ON UPDATE current_timestamp(),
    ok_col text DEFAULT some_func()
);

DEFAULT current_timestamp()
ON UPDATE current_timestamp();
```

issues.title: Latest docker images incompatible with gitlab CI pipelines
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

As of version 4.2.0 our gitlab pipelines using sqlfuff no longer function.
The issue is due to bash being removed from the sqfluff docker container here: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/pull/7752

Unfortunately gitlab expects any stage running in a docker container to be running `sh` and execute a provided script. Their instructions on how to do this are to overwrite any existing entrypoint and provide your own script.

Something like:
```
SQLFluff:
  stage: test
  image:
    name: sqlfluff/sqlfluff:4.2.1@sha256:0b1f131e3e9b4ac10bf45f1b2cb8680e67f74e63f8e6db9f0f0207dbbe3c71d2
    entrypoint:
      - ''
  script:
    - sqlfluff lint --processes 0 --disable-progress-bar
```

This works fine for 4.1.0, but as of 4.2.0 starts failing with:
```docker: Error response from daemon: failed to create task for container: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: "sh": executable file not found in $PATH```

Is it possible for the base container image to change from a prod dhi to a dev dhi image?

I understand that including bash within the container does make it less secure. But I'm not sure that too many people would be using a linting tool in a production environment as opposed to a dev or CI environment so is that extra security actually required?

### Expected Behaviour

Our gitlab pipline to still work

### Observed Behaviour

```docker: Error response from daemon: failed to create task for container: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: "sh": executable file not found in $PATH```

### How to reproduce

Run `docker run -it --entrypoint sh  sqlfluff/sqlfluff:4.1.0`  - runs fine
Run `docker run -it --entrypoint sh  sqlfluff/sqlfluff:4.2.1`  - complains about sh missing

issues.title: LT01 fix crashes with NotImplementedError on leading comma + shorthand cast (Redshift)
issues.body:
## Summary

`sqlfluff fix` throws `NotImplementedError: Unexpected Constraints: single, newline` when LT01 encounters a shorthand cast (`::`) combined with leading comma layout.

`sqlfluff lint` works fine — the crash only occurs during `fix`.

## Minimal Reproduction

**.sqlfluff:**
```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = redshift

[sqlfluff:layout:type:comma]
line_position = leading
```

**test.sql:**
```sql
SELECT
    id
    , SUM(value)::DOUBLE PRECISION / NULLIF(SUM(total), 0) AS ratio
FROM my_table
GROUP BY id
;
```

**Command:**
```bash
sqlfluff fix test.sql
```

## Error Output

```
CRITICAL   [LT01] Applying rule LT01 threw an Exception: Unexpected Constraints: single, newline
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sqlfluff/core/rules/base.py", line 528, in crawl
    res = self._eval(context=context)
  File ".../sqlfluff/rules/layout/LT01.py", line 71, in _eval
    return sequence.respace().get_results()
  File ".../sqlfluff/utils/reflow/sequence.py", line 515, in respace
    new_lint_results, new_point = point.respace_point(...)
  File ".../sqlfluff/utils/reflow/elements.py", line 819, in respace_point
    segment_buffer, new_results, edited = handle_respace__inline_without_space(...)
  File ".../sqlfluff/utils/reflow/respace.py", line 788, in handle_respace__inline_without_space
    raise NotImplementedError(
        f"Unexpected Constraints: {pre_constraint}, {post_constraint}"
    )
NotImplementedError: Unexpected Constraints: single, newline
```

## Environment

- **sqlfluff version:** 4.1.0
- **Python version:** 3.13.9
- **OS:** macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
- **Dialect:** redshift

## Workaround

Exclude LT01 in config:
```ini
exclude_rules = LT01
```

## Notes

- `sqlfluff lint` with LT01 enabled works without error — crash is only in the fix/respace path
- The combination of `line_position = leading` for commas and `::` shorthand casts triggers the unhandled constraint pair `(single, newline)` in `handle_respace__inline_without_space`

issues.title: ClickHouse dialect: WHERE after ARRAY JOIN is parsed as alias, predicate becomes unparsable
issues.body:
**Search before asking:** I searched the issues and found no similar issues.

## What Happened

A `SELECT` that uses `ARRAY JOIN` followed by a `WHERE` clause fails to parse under the `clickhouse` dialect. The parser handles `ARRAY JOIN` itself, but does not terminate the clause. Instead it consumes the trailing `WHERE` keyword as an `alias_expression` on the `ARRAY JOIN`, leaving the predicate body as an unparsable section.

## Expected Behaviour

The query parses cleanly. ClickHouse explicitly permits `WHERE` (and `PREWHERE`) to follow `ARRAY JOIN`, and the [ARRAY JOIN docs](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/select/array-join) state that `ARRAY JOIN` must be specified before `WHERE/PREWHERE` in the `SELECT` structure.

## Observed Behaviour

```
$ sqlfluff lint --dialect clickhouse repro.sql
== [repro.sql] FAIL
L:   4 | P:   1 | RF04 | Keywords should not be used as identifiers. [references.keywords]
L:   4 | P:   7 |  PRS | Line 4, Position 7: Found unparsable section: "item != ''"
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'clickhouse'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

Both findings have the same root cause:
- **RF04 at `L:4 P:1`** is the symptom. The parser treats the `WHERE` keyword as a `naked_identifier` (an alias).
- **PRS at `L:4 P:7`** is the consequence. Once `WHERE` has been consumed as an alias, the predicate `item != ''` is left dangling with no clause to live under.

The parse tree (from `sqlfluff parse --dialect clickhouse repro.sql`) shows this directly:

```
            from_clause:
                ...
                from_expression:
                    from_expression_element:
                        table_expression:
                            table_reference:
                                naked_identifier:             'some_table'
                    array_join_clause:
                        keyword:                              'ARRAY'
                        keyword:                              'JOIN'
                        select_clause_element:
                            column_reference:
                                naked_identifier:             'line_items'
                            alias_expression:
                                alias_operator:
                                    keyword:                  'AS'
                                naked_identifier:             'item'
                    alias_expression:
                        naked_identifier:                     'WHERE'   <-- bug
            unparsable:
                word:                                         'item'
                not:                                          '!'
                equals:                                       '='
                single_quote:                                 "''"
```

The fix likely lives in the `ArrayJoinClauseSegment` grammar, or in how it integrates into `FromClauseSegment` / `SelectStatementSegment`. The clause needs a terminator that prevents alias matching on a following `WHERE` / `PREWHERE` / `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` / `QUALIFY` / `ORDER BY` / `LIMIT` / `SETTINGS` keyword.

## How to reproduce

Save as `repro.sql`:

```sql
SELECT item
FROM some_table
ARRAY JOIN line_items AS item
WHERE item != ''
```

Run:

```
sqlfluff lint --dialect clickhouse repro.sql
```

**Control case** (removing the `WHERE`) parses cleanly, confirming the boundary:

```sql
SELECT item
FROM some_table
ARRAY JOIN line_items AS item
```

```
$ sqlfluff lint --dialect clickhouse control.sql
All Finished!
```

## Dialect

`clickhouse`

## Version

```
sqlfluff, version 4.1.0
Python 3.13
```

## Configuration

None. Reproduces with stock `--dialect clickhouse` and no `.sqlfluff` file.

## Code of Conduct

I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

issues.title: bug: placeholder templater silently suppresses lint violations for rules with broad anchors
issues.body:
## Summary

When using the `placeholder` templater, lint rules with broad anchors (e.g. statement-level `SegmentSeekerCrawler`) silently produce **zero violations** for SQL that should fail. The same SQL linted with literal values correctly reports violations.

## Expected Behaviour

`sqlfluff lint` should report the same violations regardless of whether a value is written as a literal or substituted via a placeholder template variable.

## Observed Behaviour

Rules such as AM04 (ambiguous column count in `UNION`), AM07 (`UNION` vs `UNION ALL`), and ST11 (set operation without brackets) return **no violations** when the SQL contains placeholder substitutions like `{{schema}}`, even though the substituted values have no effect on the rule logic.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Create test SQL and config
echo "SELECT a, b FROM {{schema}}.t1 UNION SELECT c FROM {{schema}}.t2" > /tmp/test.sql
echo -e "[sqlfluff]\ndialect = ansi\ntemplater = placeholder\n[sqlfluff:templater:placeholder]\nparam_regex = \$\{[a-zA-Z_]+\}\nparam_style = dollar" > /tmp/.sqlfluff

# Lint - expect AM04/AM07 violations but get NONE
sqlfluff lint /tmp/test.sql --config /tmp/.sqlfluff
```

Compare with literal SQL (no placeholders):
```bash
echo "SELECT a, b FROM myschema.t1 UNION SELECT c FROM myschema.t2" > /tmp/test_literal.sql
sqlfluff lint /tmp/test_literal.sql --dialect ansi
# Correctly reports AM04, AM07 violations
```

## Root Cause

`Linter.remove_templated_errors()` discards any violation whose anchor position marker returns `is_literal() == False`. The placeholder templater creates `RawFileSlice` objects with `slice_type="templated"` for substitutions, causing `TemplatedFile.is_source_slice_literal()` to return `False` for any source span overlapping a placeholder. Rules with broad anchors (spanning an entire statement) inevitably overlap placeholder regions and get silently dropped.

## Affected Rules

Any rule using `SegmentSeekerCrawler` with broad segment types is affected. Confirmed affected rules include:

| Rule | Description | Confirmed |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| AL04 | Unique column aliases | Yes |
| AL05 | Unused CTE aliases | Yes |
| AL06 | Short alias length | Yes |
| AL07 | Avoid right joins | Yes |
| AL08 | Distinct used with parentheses | Yes |
| AL09 | Self-aliasing | Yes |
| AM04 | Ambiguous column count in set operations | Yes |
| AM07 | UNION vs UNION ALL | Yes |
| AM09 | ORDER BY in set operations | Yes |
| CV03 | Trailing commas | Yes |
| LT09 | SELECT targets on separate lines | Yes |
| LT10 | Inconsistent indent of SELECT targets | Yes |
| ST11 | Set operations without brackets | Yes |

## Dialect

All dialects using the placeholder templater are affected.

## Version

Tested against `main` branch (commit 39b5a60).
