issues.title: tsql: DECLARE ... CURSOR FOR with UNION (or any set operation) in the SELECT body fails to parse
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In the `tsql` dialect, a `DECLARE … CURSOR FOR …` whose body is a set-expression
(`SELECT … UNION ALL SELECT …`, or `UNION` / `INTERSECT` / `EXCEPT`) is reported
as an unparsable section. A simple non-set SELECT body parses cleanly; adding a
`UNION ALL` immediately breaks the entire enclosing batch.

T-SQL allows any `<select_statement>` after `FOR` in `DECLARE CURSOR`, including
set operations:

> DECLARE cursor_name CURSOR ... FOR select_statement

where `select_statement` is the full SELECT grammar — set expressions included.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/declare-cursor-transact-sql

### Root cause (from reading the source) by claude code

In `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_tsql.py` around L3659:

```python
class DeclareCursorStatementSegment(BaseSegment):
    type = "declare_segment"
    match_grammar = Sequence(
        "DECLARE",
        Ref("CursorNameGrammar"),
        OneOf(
            Ref("CursorDefinitionSegment"),
            Sequence(
                AnySetOf(
                    Ref.keyword("INSENSITIVE", optional=True),
                    Ref.keyword("SCROLL", optional=True),
                ),
                "CURSOR",
                "FOR",
                Ref("SelectStatementSegment"),   # <-- single SELECT only
                ...
            ),
        ),
    )

### Expected Behaviour

The following should parse cleanly under `--dialect tsql`:

```sql
CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[p]
AS
BEGIN
    DECLARE cur CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR
        SELECT 1 AS Id
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 2 AS Id
    OPEN cur
END
```

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'CREATE PROCEDURE
                       | [dbo].[p]\nAS\nBEGIN\n...'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'tsql'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

Removing `UNION ALL` and the second `SELECT` makes the file parse cleanly.

### How to reproduce

1. Save the snippet above as `repro.sql`.
2. Run `sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql`.
3. Observe the unparsable section starting at line 1.
4. Replace the body with a single `SELECT 1 AS Id` — file parses, no PRS.

### Dialect

tsql

### Version

Python 3.14.4 (Windows)

[sqlfluff]
dialect = tsql

issues.title: tsql: Unicode (e.g. Cyrillic) characters in @parameter names break the parser
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In the `tsql` dialect, `@parameter` names that contain Unicode letters
(Cyrillic, Greek, accented Latin, CJK, …) are not parsed. SQLFluff fails
the entire enclosing batch as one big unparsable section starting at line
1, even though the parameter is a perfectly valid T-SQL identifier in
SQL Server.

T-SQL allows Unicode letters in regular identifiers (and therefore in
parameter names), since SQL Server uses Unicode identifier rules:

> A regular identifier ... must comply with rules from the Unicode 3.2
> standard. ... Letters, as defined in the Unicode Standard 3.2.

Reference (identifier rules):
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/databases/database-identifiers

Reference (parameter name rules — same as identifier rules):
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/declare-local-variable-transact-sql

### Root cause (from reading the source) by claude code

In `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_tsql.py` (line ~578):

```python
ParameterNameSegment=RegexParser(
    r"@(?!@)[A-Za-z0-9_@$#]+", CodeSegment, type="parameter"
),
```

The character class `[A-Za-z0-9_@$#]+` is ASCII-only and so does not match
any Unicode letter that T-SQL identifier rules permit.

Suggested fix: broaden the regex to allow Unicode letters/digits/marks. A
conservative replacement that still excludes whitespace and operators
would be something like:

```python
ParameterNameSegment=RegexParser(
    r"@(?!@)[\w@$#]+",         # \w is Unicode-aware in Python re
    CodeSegment, type="parameter"
),
```

…or, if a stricter character set is preferred, an explicit Unicode class
matching SQL Server's identifier rules (`L`, `Mn`, `Mc`, `Nd`, plus `_`,
`@`, `$`, `#`):

```python
ParameterNameSegment=RegexParser(
    r"@(?!@)[\p{L}\p{Mn}\p{Mc}\p{Nd}_@$#]+",
    CodeSegment, type="parameter"
),
```

(`regex` package or `re` with the appropriate flag, depending on the
project's preferred dependency).

A YAML test fixture under
`test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/unicode_parameter_names.{sql,yml}` would
cover regression.

The same issue likely affects `NakedIdentifierSegment` and other
identifier-matching grammars in this dialect — worth a once-over while
fixing parameters.



### Expected Behaviour

Parameter names containing Unicode letters should parse cleanly. For
example:

```sql
DECLARE @Дата DATETIME2
```

…should parse

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ cat repro.sql
DECLARE @Дата DATETIME2

$ sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'CREATE FUNCTION
                       | [dbo].[fn_test]\n(\n...'

issues.title: tsql: `Maximum parse depth exceeded (limit 255)` triggers on modest nested function calls
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

Several short, perfectly ordinary T-SQL scalar UDFs in our codebase fail to
parse with `PRS | Maximum parse depth exceeded (limit 255)`, even though the
human-readable nesting depth is small (5–7 levels of `REPLACE` / `LTRIM` /
`RTRIM` / `CHAR`).

Because the limit fails the entire batch as a single top-level unparsable
section starting at L1,P1, this also masks any other diagnostic the user
might want from such files. There is no `--noqa` workaround for this
particular error since it is emitted before noqa-directives are applied.

Setting `max_parse_depth = 0` in `.sqlfluff` resolves all of them with no observed
side effects

### Expected Behaviour

A scalar function with ~6 nested function calls should parse without
hitting the parse-depth limit. The default limit of 255 should be reachable
only for genuinely pathological / DoS-style input, not normal
`REPLACE(REPLACE(...))` chains

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ cat repro.sql
CREATE FUNCTION [dbo].[fn_StringWithoutSpace]
(
    @string NVARCHAR(MAX)
)
RETURNS NVARCHAR(MAX)
WITH INLINE = OFF
AS
BEGIN
    RETURN (
        SELECT LTRIM(RTRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(
            @string,
            CHAR(160), CHAR(32)),
            CHAR(32),  '()'),
            ')(',      ''),
            '()',      CHAR(32))))
    )
END

$ sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Maximum parse depth exceeded (limit 255). This may indicate deeply
                       | nested SQL or a malicious input.
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'tsql'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

Visible nesting:
`LTRIM( RTRIM( REPLACE( REPLACE( REPLACE( REPLACE( ... ) ) ) ) ) )` — 6
levels — produces a parse-depth value of 256+.

Setting `max_parse_depth = 0` (disable check) makes the file parse cleanly
with no further violations, confirming that the grammar itself can handle
the input — only the depth counter trips.

### How to reproduce

1. Save the snippet above as `repro.sql`.
2. Run `sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql`.
3. Observe the `Maximum parse depth exceeded (limit 255)` PRS at L1,P1.
4. Add `max_parse_depth = 0` to `.sqlfluff`
   under `[sqlfluff]`. Re-run — the file parses with no PRS.

### Dialect

tsql

### Version

4.1.0
Python 3.14.4 (Windows)

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = tsql

issues.title: tsql: ALTER TABLE … ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER … fails to parse
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In the `tsql` dialect, the canonical Microsoft T-SQL statement
`ALTER TABLE <table> { ENABLE | DISABLE } TRIGGER <trigger_name>` does not
parse — sqlfluff reports the line as an unparsable section.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-table-transact-sql
(the `{ ENABLE | DISABLE } TRIGGER { ALL | trigger_name [ ,...n ] }` clause)

### Root cause (from reading the source) by claude code

In `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_tsql.py`, the `AlterTableSegment` does not
contain a branch matching the `{ ENABLE | DISABLE } TRIGGER …` clause. There
are existing standalone segments for similar trigger-related statements
(e.g. `EnableDisableTriggerStatementSegment` exists in some other dialects),
but no equivalent is wired into `tsql`.

Suggested fix: add an alternative inside `AlterTableSegment` (or a separate
`AlterTableTriggerStatementSegment` reachable from `StatementSegment`) along
the lines of:

```python
Sequence(
    OneOf("ENABLE", "DISABLE"),
    "TRIGGER",
    OneOf(
        "ALL",
        Delimited(Ref("TriggerReferenceSegment")),
    ),
)
```

…and a YAML test fixture under
`test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/alter_table_enable_disable_trigger.{sql,yml}`

### Expected Behaviour

All of the following statements should parse cleanly under `--dialect tsql`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] DISABLE TRIGGER [TRContactID];
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] ENABLE TRIGGER [TRContactID];
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] DISABLE TRIGGER ALL;
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] ENABLE TRIGGER ALL;
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] ENABLE TRIGGER [t1], [t2];
```

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ cat repro.sql
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] DISABLE TRIGGER [TRContactID]

$ sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql
[L:  1, P:  1]      |file:
[L:  1, P:  1]      |    unparsable:                                               !! Expected: "<Sequence: [<AnyNumberOf: [<Ref: 'BatchSegment'>]>]>"
...
==== parsing violations ====
L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'ALTER TABLE
                       | [dbo].[Contact] DISABLE TRIGGER [TRContactID]...'
WARNING: Parsing errors found and dialect is set to 'tsql'. Have you configured your dialect correctly?
```

The error happens both on its own and after a preceding `CREATE TRIGGER … END` block (with or without an intervening `GO`).

### How to reproduce

1. Save the following as `repro.sql`:

   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Contact] DISABLE TRIGGER [TRContactID];
   ```

2. Run:

   ```
   sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql
   ```

3. Observe the unparsable section starting at line 1.

### Dialect

tsql 

### Version

4.1.0
Python 3.14.4 (Windows)

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = tsql

issues.title: tsql: SET DATEFORMAT <format> fails to parse (canonical MS syntax)
issues.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In the tsql dialect, the canonical Microsoft T-SQL statement SET DATEFORMAT dmy (and the equivalent quoted form SET DATEFORMAT 'dmy') is
  not parsed. SQLFluff reports the entire enclosing batch as an unparsable section, which means a single SET DATEFORMAT line inside a large
  CREATE PROCEDURE body causes the whole procedure to be marked unparsable, with the error pointing at line 1.
 
  Per the official documentation, the syntax is:

`  SET DATEFORMAT { format | @format_var }`

  where format is one of mdy | dmy | ymd | ydm | myd | dym and may be specified unquoted or as a Unicode/character string.

  Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-dateformat-transact-sql

### Expected Behaviour

 All of the following statements should parse cleanly under --dialect tsql:

```
  SET DATEFORMAT dmy;
  SET DATEFORMAT 'dmy';
  SET DATEFORMAT mdy;
  SET DATEFORMAT ymd;
  SET DATEFORMAT ydm;
  SET DATEFORMAT myd;
  SET DATEFORMAT dym;
  SET DATEFORMAT @fmt;
```

### Observed Behaviour

 The bare-format and string-literal forms produce an unparsable section. Minimal output:

  ```
$ sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql -
  SET DATEFORMAT dmy;
  ^D
  [L:  1, P:  1]      |file:
  [L:  1, P:  1]      |    unparsable:                                               !! Expected: "<Sequence: [<AnyNumberOf: [<Ref:
  'BatchSegment'>]>]>"
  ...
  ==== parsing violations ====
  L:   1 | P:   1 |  PRS | Line 1, Position 1: Found unparsable section: 'SET DATEFORMAT dmy;'
```

  Test matrix actually observed:
| Statement | Parses? |
| :--- | :--- |
| SET DATEFORMAT dmy; | NO |
| SET DATEFORMAT 'dmy'; | NO |
| SET DATEFORMAT mdy; | NO |
| SET DATEFORMAT ymd; | NO |
| SET DATEFORMAT @x; | yes |
 


### How to reproduce

1. Save the following as repro.sql:   `SET DATEFORMAT dmy;`
2. Run:  `sqlfluff parse --dialect tsql repro.sql`
3. Observe the unparsable section on line 1.

### Dialect

tsql

### Version

4.1.0
Python 3.14.4 (Windows)

### Configuration

[sqlfluff]
dialect = tsql
large_file_skip_byte_limit = 0

[sqlfluff:indentation]
indent_unit = tab
tab_space_size = 4

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.keywords]
capitalisation_policy = upper

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.identifiers]
extended_capitalisation_policy = pascal
ignore_words_regex = ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,3}$

The `EXECUTE` command does not seem to be supported by SQLFluff. This comes up as an error, however this might be an oversight that could increase coverage, so not sure if this is considered to be a bug or not.
